+func TestDeadlineAndCleanupChooseOneTerminalOutcome(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, forceFirst := range []bool{false, true} {
+		name := "clean first"
+		if forceFirst {
+			name = "deadline first"
+		}
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			ledger := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "lifecycle.jsonl")
+			forced := -1
+			r := &serveRun{flog: dlog.New(io.Discard, dlog.LevelDebug, time.Now),
+				pid: os.Getpid(), startedAt: time.Now(), perProcessLedger: true,
+				exitRequested: make(chan struct{}), deadlineExit: func(code int) { forced = code },
+			}
+			r.lcIn.ledger = ledger
+			r.exitRow(tenancy.ExitSignal, "signal before cleanup", 143)
+			close(r.exitRequested)
+			cleanGate, deadlineGate := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
+			cleanDone, deadlineDone := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
+			go func() { <-cleanGate; r.completeCleanup(); close(cleanDone) }()
+			go func() { <-deadlineGate; r.forceExitAtDeadline(143); close(deadlineDone) }()
+			if forceFirst {
+				close(deadlineGate)
+				<-deadlineDone
+				close(cleanGate)
+				<-cleanDone
+				rows := readRowsT(t, ledger)
+				if forced != 143 || r.terminalState != 2 || len(rows) != 2 || rows[1].Reason != tenancy.ExitUnclean {
+					t.Fatalf("forced outcome: code=%d state=%d rows=%+v", forced, r.terminalState, rows)
+				}
+			} else {
+				close(cleanGate)
+				<-cleanDone
+				close(deadlineGate)
+				<-deadlineDone
+				if forced != -1 || r.terminalState != 1 {
+					t.Fatalf("completed cleanup forced later: code=%d state=%d", forced, r.terminalState)
+				}
+				if _, err := os.Stat(ledger); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
+					t.Fatalf("clean ledger remains: %v", err)
+				}
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+func readGracefulStoreState(t *testing.T, path string) gracefulStoreState {
+	t.Helper()
+	db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", path)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	defer db.Close()
+	rows, err := db.Query("SELECT type, name, tbl_name, sql FROM sqlite_schema ORDER BY type, name")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	var s gracefulStoreState
+	for rows.Next() {
+		var kind, name, table string
+		var statement sql.NullString
+		if err := rows.Scan(&kind, &name, &table, &statement); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		s.schema += fmt.Sprintf("%s|%s|%s|%s\n", kind, name, table, statement.String)
+	}
+	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	rows.Close()
+	if err := db.QueryRow("SELECT rowid, value FROM graceful_fixture").Scan(&s.rowID, &s.value); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := db.QueryRow("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM graceful_fixture").Scan(&s.rows); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := db.QueryRow("PRAGMA user_version").Scan(&s.version); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	return s
+}

+// A real test binary runs serve-http in an owned process group. TERM and INT
+// must return their conventional codes after the SQLite connection closes,
+// without changing the existing schema or row.
+func TestServeHTTPSignalsCloseStoreBeforeExit(t *testing.T) {
+	if testing.Short() {
+		t.Skip("spawns serve-http")
+	}
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name    string
+		sig     syscall.Signal
+		code    int
+		managed bool
+	}{
+		{"unmanaged TERM", syscall.SIGTERM, 143, false},
+		{"unmanaged INT", syscall.SIGINT, 130, false},
+		{"managed TERM", syscall.SIGTERM, 0, true},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			dir := t.TempDir()
+			path := filepath.Join(dir, "scratch.sqlite")
+			st, err := store.NewSQLiteStore(path)
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if err := st.Close(); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", path)
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if _, err := db.Exec("CREATE TABLE graceful_fixture (value TEXT NOT NULL)"); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if _, err := db.Exec("INSERT INTO graceful_fixture (rowid, value) VALUES (41, 'kept')"); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if err := db.Close(); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			before := readGracefulStoreState(t, path)
+			addr := freeAddr(t)
+			logPath := filepath.Join(dir, "serve.log")
+			cmd := exec.Command(os.Args[0])
+			cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}
+			managed := "0"
+			if tc.managed {
+				managed = "1"
+			}
+			cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), testHelperEnv+"=rt-graceful-serve", "RT_GRACEFUL_STORE="+path,
+				"RT_GRACEFUL_ADDR="+addr, "RT_GRACEFUL_LOG="+logPath, "RT_GRACEFUL_MANAGED="+managed, "XPC_SERVICE_NAME=")
+			if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			waited := make(chan error, 1)
+			go func() { waited <- cmd.Wait() }()
+			t.Cleanup(func() { _ = cmd.Process.Kill() })
+			logText := func() string { b, _ := os.ReadFile(logPath); return string(b) }
+			httpClient := &http.Client{Timeout: 300 * time.Millisecond}
+			deadline := time.Now().Add(waitSafety)
+			for {
+				resp, err := httpClient.Get("http://" + addr + "/healthz")
+				if err == nil {
+					resp.Body.Close()
+					if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusOK {
+						break
+					}
+				}
+				select {
+				case err := <-waited:
+					t.Fatalf("daemon exited before serving: %v\n%s", err, logText())
+				default:
+				}
+				if time.Now().After(deadline) {
+					t.Fatalf("daemon never served: %s", logText())
+				}
+				time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
+			}
+			if err := cmd.Process.Signal(tc.sig); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			select {
+			case err := <-waited:
+				if tc.code == 0 {
+					if err != nil {
+						t.Fatalf("exit = %v, want 0\n%s", err, logText())
+					}
+				} else {
+					var exit *exec.ExitError
+					if !errors.As(err, &exit) || exit.ExitCode() != tc.code {
+						t.Fatalf("exit = %v, want %d\n%s", err, tc.code, logText())
+					}
+				}
+			case <-time.After(waitSafety):
+				t.Fatalf("daemon did not exit after %s\n%s", tc.name, logText())
+			}
+			if err := syscall.Kill(-cmd.Process.Pid, 0); !errors.Is(err, syscall.ESRCH) {
+				t.Fatalf("owned process group %d remains: %v", cmd.Process.Pid, err)
+			}
+			for _, sidecar := range []string{"-wal", "-shm"} {
+				if _, err := os.Stat(path + sidecar); !errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
+					t.Fatalf("SQLite sidecar %s remains: %v", sidecar, err)
+				}
+			}
+			if after := readGracefulStoreState(t, path); !reflect.DeepEqual(after, before) {
+				t.Fatalf("store changed across signal: before=%+v after=%+v", before, after)
+			}
+			wantReason := "signal "
+			if tc.managed {
+				wantReason = "drain: done"
+			}
+			if !strings.Contains(logText(), wantReason) {
+				t.Fatalf("exit reason %q not logged:\n%s", wantReason, logText())
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+// requestServeExit makes the serving goroutine return through its registered
+// cleanups. A managed drain has already shut HTTP down; an unmanaged exit
+// shuts it down here. The request precedes store-wait cancellation and
+// listener close, so either return path retains the requested code.
+func (r *serveRun) requestServeExit(code int, shutdownHTTP bool) {
+	r.exitOnce.Do(func() {
+		if shutdownHTTP {
+			r.watchExitDeadline(code, 9*time.Second)
+		}
+		r.exitCode.Store(int32(code))
+		close(r.exitRequested)
+		r.cancelExit()
+		r.stopRefresh()
+		if shutdownHTTP {
+			r.stopServing()
+		}
+		close(r.exitDone)
+	})
+}
+
+// watchExitDeadline preserves the daemon's terminal exit bound if a request
+// or cleanup refuses cancellation. Such an exit leaves the ledger on disk
+// with an explicit unclean row; it never claims that SQLite closed.
+func (r *serveRun) watchExitDeadline(code int, budget time.Duration) {
+	r.watchOnce.Do(func() {
+		schedule := r.deadlineTimer
+		if schedule == nil {
+			schedule = func(d time.Duration, f func()) { time.AfterFunc(d, f) }
+		}
+		schedule(budget, func() { r.forceExitAtDeadline(code) })
+	})
+}
+
+// completeCleanup and forceExitAtDeadline choose one terminal outcome under
+// one lock. A finished cleanup cannot later be forced; a forced exit keeps
+// its unclean ledger instead of having it removed by the return path.
+func (r *serveRun) completeCleanup() {
+	r.terminalMu.Lock()
+	defer r.terminalMu.Unlock()
+	if r.terminalState != 0 {
+		return
+	}
+	if r.perProcessLedger {
+		select {
+		case <-r.exitRequested:
+			removePerProcessLedger(r.lcIn.ledger)
+		default:
+		}
+	}
+	r.terminalState = 1
+}
+
+func (r *serveRun) forceExitAtDeadline(code int) {
+	r.terminalMu.Lock()
+	defer r.terminalMu.Unlock()
+	if r.terminalState != 0 {
+		return
+	}
+	r.terminalState = 2
+	r.exitRow(tenancy.ExitUnclean, "cleanup incomplete at exit deadline", code)
+	r.flog.Warn("serve-http: cleanup incomplete at exit deadline; forcing exit")
+	if r.deadlineExit != nil {
+		r.deadlineExit(code)
+	} else {
+		os.Exit(code)
+	}
+}
+
+func (r *serveRun) requestedExitCode() (int, bool) {
+	select {
+	case <-r.exitRequested:
+		<-r.exitDone // HTTP shutdown completes before the store is closed.
+		return int(r.exitCode.Load()), true
+	default:
+		return 0, false
+	}
+}

+package main
+
+// Explicit trace decision inputs are literal, bounded reads of Git objects at
+// COMMIT. The default builder keeps its original paths/parser unchanged.
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"os/exec"
+	"path"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"regexp"
+	"sort"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+	"unicode"
+	"unicode/utf8"
+
+	"github.com/yuin/goldmark"
+	goldast "github.com/yuin/goldmark/ast"
+	"github.com/yuin/goldmark/extension"
+	extast "github.com/yuin/goldmark/extension/ast"
+	"github.com/yuin/goldmark/text"
+)
+
+const (
+	traceDecisionSelectorLimit = 16
+	traceDecisionFileLimit     = 256
+	traceDecisionFileBytes     = 1 << 20
+	traceDecisionTotalBytes    = 8 << 20
+	traceDecisionTreeBytes     = 1 << 20
+	traceDecisionPathBytes     = 4096
+)
+
+func traceDecisionPath(raw string) (string, error) {
+	if raw == "" || len(raw) > traceDecisionPathBytes || !utf8.ValidString(raw) || strings.Contains(raw, `\`) || filepath.IsAbs(raw) || path.IsAbs(raw) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("decision source path must be a bounded repository-relative literal: %q", raw)
+	}
+	if len(raw) >= 3 && raw[1] == ':' && raw[2] == '/' {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("decision source path must not be absolute: %q", raw)
+	}
+	for _, r := range raw {
+		if unicode.IsControl(r) {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("decision source path contains a control character: %q", raw)
+		}
+	}
+	for _, component := range strings.Split(raw, "/") {
+		if component == ".." {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("decision source traversal is forbidden: %q", raw)
+		}
+	}
+	return path.Clean(raw), nil
+}
+
+func canonicalTraceDecisionSources(selectors []string) ([]string, error) {
+	if len(selectors) == 0 {
+		return nil, nil
+	}
+	seen := map[string]bool{}
+	for _, raw := range selectors {
+		p, err := traceDecisionPath(raw)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, err
+		}
+		seen[p] = true
+		if len(seen) > traceDecisionSelectorLimit {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source selector limit exceeded (%d)", traceDecisionSelectorLimit)
+		}
+	}
+	out := make([]string, 0, len(seen))
+	for p := range seen {
+		out = append(out, p)
+	}
+	sort.Strings(out)
+	return out, nil
+}
+
+// Git stderr is diagnostic, never an unbounded second output channel.
+type traceGitDiagnostic []byte
+
+func (b *traceGitDiagnostic) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	n := len(p)
+	if remaining := (16 << 10) - len(*b); remaining > 0 {
+		if len(p) > remaining {
+			p = p[:remaining]
+		}
+		*b = append(*b, p...)
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+func traceDecisionGit(ctx context.Context, repo string, limit int, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
+	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", append([]string{"-C", repo}, args...)...)
+	var diagnostic traceGitDiagnostic
+	cmd.Stderr = &diagnostic
+	pipe, err := cmd.StdoutPipe()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source git: %w", err)
+	}
+	b, readErr := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(pipe, int64(limit)+1))
+	if readErr != nil || len(b) > limit {
+		_ = cmd.Process.Kill()
+		_ = cmd.Wait()
+		if readErr != nil {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source read: %w", readErr)
+		}
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source Git output limit exceeded (%d bytes)", limit)
+	}
+	if err := cmd.Wait(); err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source git: %w: %s", err, strings.TrimSpace(string(diagnostic)))
+	}
+	return b, nil
+}
+
+type traceDecisionBlob struct {
+	path string
+	size int
+}
+
+func traceDecisionBlobs(ctx context.Context, repo, commit string, selectors []string) ([]traceDecisionBlob, error) {
+	args := []string{"ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "-l", "--full-tree", commit, "--"}
+	for _, p := range selectors {
+		args = append(args, ":(literal)"+p)
+	}
+	listing, err := traceDecisionGit(ctx, repo, traceDecisionTreeBytes, args...)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	matched := map[string]bool{}
+	files := map[string]traceDecisionBlob{}
+	total := 0
+	for _, record := range bytes.Split(listing, []byte{0}) {
+		if len(record) == 0 {
+			continue
+		}
+		meta, rawPath, ok := bytes.Cut(record, []byte{'\t'})
+		if !ok {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source tree has malformed metadata")
+		}
+		p, err := traceDecisionPath(string(rawPath))
+		if err != nil || p != string(rawPath) {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source tree has unsafe path %q", rawPath)
+		}
+		fields := strings.Fields(string(meta))
+		if len(fields) != 4 || fields[1] != "blob" || (fields[0] != "100644" && fields[0] != "100755") {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source %q is not a regular Git blob (symlinks/gitlinks forbidden)", p)
+		}
+		if path.Ext(p) != ".md" {
+			continue
+		}
+		for _, selector := range selectors {
+			if selector == "." || p == selector || strings.HasPrefix(p, selector+"/") {
+				matched[selector] = true
+			}
+		}
+		if _, exists := files[p]; exists {
+			continue
+		}
+		size, err := strconv.ParseInt(fields[3], 10, 64)
+		if err != nil || size < 0 || size > traceDecisionFileBytes {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source %q file size limit exceeded (%d bytes)", p, traceDecisionFileBytes)
+		}
+		total += int(size)
+		if len(files) == traceDecisionFileLimit || total > traceDecisionTotalBytes {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source file/total limit exceeded (%d files, %d bytes)", traceDecisionFileLimit, traceDecisionTotalBytes)
+		}
+		files[p] = traceDecisionBlob{path: p, size: int(size)}
+	}
+	for _, selector := range selectors {
+		if !matched[selector] {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("decision source %q has no committed Markdown file", selector)
+		}
+	}
+	out := make([]traceDecisionBlob, 0, len(files))
+	for _, blob := range files {
+		out = append(out, blob)
+	}
+	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].path < out[j].path })
+	return out, nil
+}
+
+var (
+	traceProjectADR       = regexp.MustCompile(`^(ADR(?:-| )?\d+)\b`)
+	traceProjectInvariant = regexp.MustCompile(`^I\d+$`)
+)
+
+// Declarations come from real Markdown nodes, never filenames, numbered
+// prose, or fenced/indented examples. IDs retain their exact spelling.
+func traceProjectDecisionIDs(source []byte, decisions map[string]bool) {
+	doc := goldmark.New(goldmark.WithExtensions(extension.Table)).Parser().Parse(text.NewReader(source))
+	_ = goldast.Walk(doc, func(n goldast.Node, entering bool) (goldast.WalkStatus, error) {
+		if !entering {
+			return goldast.WalkContinue, nil
+		}
+		switch n.(type) {
+		case *goldast.Heading:
+			if match := traceProjectADR.FindSubmatch(bytes.TrimSpace(n.Text(source))); match != nil {
+				decisions[string(match[1])] = true
+			}
+		case *extast.TableRow:
+			if cell := n.FirstChild(); cell != nil {
+				id := strings.TrimSpace(string(cell.Text(source)))
+				if traceProjectInvariant.MatchString(id) {
+					decisions[id] = true
+				}
+			}
+		}
+		return goldast.WalkContinue, nil
+	})
+}

+// TOOL08 tests intentionally use only the existing CLI/review APIs. Before the
+// implementation they must compile, then fail at runtime on the unknown flag.
+// No proposed production type or helper is referenced here.
+func traceProjectWrite(t *testing.T, root, name, body string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	full := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(name))
+	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(full), 0o755); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := os.WriteFile(full, []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+}
+
+func traceProjectCommit(t *testing.T, root string) string {
+	t.Helper()
+	for _, args := range [][]string{{"add", "-A"}, {"-c", "user.email=t@example.invalid", "-c", "user.name=t", "commit", "-q", "-m", "project decision sources"}} {
+		cmd := exec.Command("git", append([]string{"-C", root}, args...)...)
+		if output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
+			t.Fatalf("git %v: %v %s", args, err, output)
+		}
+	}
+	output, err := exec.Command("git", "-C", root, "rev-parse", "HEAD").Output()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	return strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
+}

+package main
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"os/signal"
+	"syscall"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/store"
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/pkg/client"
+)
+
+const unityReferencesWireLimit = 16 << 10
+
+// cmdUnityReferences is an explicit receipt reader. Producer run directories
+// retain history; this command creates no family table or current-fact cache.
+// Even an unchanged receipt must pass the public client's current input and
+// active-generation checks on every invocation.
+func cmdUnityReferences(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {
+	fs := newFlagSet("unity-references", stderr)
+	service := fs.String("service", "", "registered service identity (required)")
+	project := fs.String("project", "", "service-relative Unity project (required)")
+	family := fs.String("family", "", "explicit receipt family identity (required)")
+	receipt := fs.String("receipt", "", "service-relative immutable producer receipt JSON (required)")
+	active := fs.String("active", "", "service-relative current family active marker JSON (required)")
+	editorVersion := fs.String("editor-version", "", "trusted exact Editor version, never accepted from the receipt (required)")
+	editorSHA := fs.String("editor-sha256", "", "trusted exact Editor executable SHA256 (required)")
+	target := fs.String("target", "", "trusted selected native build target (required)")
+	guid := fs.String("guid", "", "exact persistent target/source GUID (required)")
+	fileID := fs.String("file-id", "", "canonical signed64 decimal fileID text, without rounding (required)")
+	direction := fs.String("direction", "inbound", "inbound or outbound; one hop only")
+	limit := fs.Int("limit", 25, "maximum groups, 0 selects 25, at most 100; complete response at most 16KiB")
+	jsonOut := fs.Bool("json", false, "emit bounded compact JSON instead of text")
+	storePath := fs.String("store", defaultStorePath(), "existing registered-service store, mounted read-only")
+	if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
+		return 1
+	}
+	if fs.NArg() != 0 {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "error: unity-references accepts named flags only")
+		return 1
+	}
+	for _, required := range []struct{ name, value string }{
+		{"service", *service}, {"project", *project}, {"family", *family},
+		{"receipt", *receipt}, {"active", *active}, {"editor-version", *editorVersion},
+		{"editor-sha256", *editorSHA}, {"target", *target}, {"guid", *guid}, {"file-id", *fileID},
+	} {
+		if required.value == "" {
+			fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "error: unity-references requires --%s\n", required.name)
+			return 1
+		}
+	}
+	if *limit < 0 || *limit > 100 || (*direction != "inbound" && *direction != "outbound") {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "error: unity-references requires inbound/outbound and limit 0..100")
+		return 1
+	}
+	mounted, err := store.MountReadOnly(*storePath, store.LevelL0)
+	if err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "error: unity-references read-only store: %v\n", err)
+		return 1
+	}
+	c := client.New(nil, mounted)
+	defer func() { _ = c.Close() }() // Client owns the one mount and pipeline.
+	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
+	defer stop()
+	result, err := c.UnityAssetReferences(ctx, *service, client.UnityAssetReferenceOptions{
+		Project: *project, FamilyID: *family, ReceiptPath: *receipt, ActivePath: *active,
+		ExpectedEditorVersion: *editorVersion, ExpectedEditorSHA256: *editorSHA, ExpectedBuildTarget: *target,
+	}, client.AssetReferenceQuery{Object: client.AssetObjectID{GUID: *guid, FileID: *fileID}, Direction: *direction, Limit: *limit})
+	if err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "error: unity-references: %v\n", err)
+		return 1
+	}
+	if err := renderUnityReferences(stdout, result, *jsonOut); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "error: unity-references output: %v\n", err)
+		return 1
+	}
+	return 0
+}
+
+// Buffer the whole projection before writing: a refusal never prints a partial
+// positive response. Compact JSON has no extra newline beyond its byte budget.
+func renderUnityReferences(w io.Writer, result client.AssetReferenceResult, jsonOut bool) error {
+	encoded, err := json.Marshal(result)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if len(encoded) > unityReferencesWireLimit {
+		return fmt.Errorf("complete result exceeds 16KiB")
+	}
+	if jsonOut {
+		_, err = w.Write(encoded)
+		return err
+	}
+	var text bytes.Buffer
+	fmt.Fprintf(&text, "Unity references: %s; service=%q project=%q family=%q\n", result.Status, result.Service, result.Project, result.FamilyID)
+	fmt.Fprintf(&text, "%s %s#%s: %d/%d groups; %d elided\n", result.Direction, result.Object.GUID, result.Object.FileID, len(result.References), result.Total, result.Truncated)
+	for _, reference := range result.References {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&text, "%q [%s#%s] -> %q [%s#%s]; %d matched occurrences (locations/properties unpaired)\n", reference.SourcePath, reference.Source.GUID, reference.Source.FileID, reference.TargetPath, reference.Target.GUID, reference.Target.FileID, reference.MatchedOccurrences)
+	}
+	fmt.Fprintf(&text, "Cohort: matched=%d admitted=%d package-unbound=%d native-only=%d raw-only=%d\n", result.Counts.Matched, result.Counts.AdmittedMatched, result.Counts.NativeObservedUnbound, result.Counts.NativeOnly, result.Counts.RawOnly)
+	fmt.Fprintf(&text, "Receipt=%s source=%s context=%s\n", result.ReceiptSHA256, result.SourceSHA256, result.ContextSHA256)
+	for _, limitation := range result.Limitations {
+		fmt.Fprintf(&text, "Partial: %s\n", limitation)
+	}
+	if text.Len() > unityReferencesWireLimit {
+		return fmt.Errorf("complete text result exceeds 16KiB; use --json or a lower --limit")
+	}
+	_, err = w.Write(text.Bytes())
+	return err
+}
+
+type unityReferencesRunner struct{}
+

+func TestUnityReferencesDispatchRequiresExplicitScopeAndExactFlags(t *testing.T) {
+	base := unityReferencesArgs(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "missing.sqlite"))
+	for _, name := range []string{"service", "project", "family", "receipt", "active", "editor-version", "editor-sha256", "target", "guid", "file-id"} {
+		t.Run("missing-"+name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			args := append([]string(nil), base...)
+			for index, value := range args {
+				if value == "--"+name {
+					args = append(args[:index], args[index+2:]...)
+					break
+				}
+			}
+			var out, stderr bytes.Buffer
+			if code := run(args, &out, &stderr); code == 0 || out.Len() != 0 || !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "requires --"+name) {
+				t.Fatalf("missing flag silently accepted/printed positive output: code%d out%q err%q", code, out.String(), stderr.String())
+			}
+		})
+	}
+	for name, extra := range map[string][]string{"no-arbitrary-root": {"--root", "/untrusted"}, "invalid-bool": {"--json=maybe"}, "invalid-limit": {"--limit", "NaN"}, "overbound-limit": {"--limit", "101"}, "negative-limit": {"--limit", "-1"}, "not-transitive": {"--direction", "transitive"}, "no-positionals": {"unexpected"}} {
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			var out, stderr bytes.Buffer
+			args := append(append([]string(nil), base...), extra...)
+			if code := run(args, &out, &stderr); code == 0 || out.Len() != 0 || stderr.Len() == 0 {
+				t.Fatalf("bad flags accepted: code%d out%q err%q", code, out.String(), stderr.String())
+			}
+		})
+	}

+func TestUnityReferencesRegisteredRootRefusalPreservesStoreAndCode(t *testing.T) {
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	root, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(t.TempDir())
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	path := filepath.Join(root, "registered.sqlite")
+	st, err := store.Open(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := st.SetServiceMeta(ctx, store.ServiceMeta{ServiceID: "fixture", Path: root}); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	observations := []core.Observation{{ServiceID: "fixture", SourceRef: "code.go:1", SourceKind: core.KindGoFunc, EvidenceTier: core.TierPreScan, Symbol: "Existing", Claim: "independent code", Line: 1, EndLine: 1}}
+	edges := []core.Edge{{FromService: "fixture", FromFile: "code.go", FromSymbol: "fixture.Existing", ToSymbol: "fixture.Callee", Kind: core.EdgeDirect}}
+	if err := st.PutObservations(ctx, observations); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := st.PutTypedEdges(ctx, "fixture", "scip:independent", edges); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	beforeObs, err := st.QueryObservations(ctx, "fixture", "")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := st.Close(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	before, err := os.ReadFile(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	for name, extra := range map[string][]string{"json-false": {"--json=false"}, "zero-default-limit": {"--limit", "0"}, "negative-signed64-id": {"--file-id", "-5831914722253275453"}, "unregistered": {"--service", "unregistered"}, "noncanonical-id": {"--file-id", "9e15"}} {
+		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			var out, stderr bytes.Buffer
+			args := append(unityReferencesArgs(path), extra...)
+			if code := run(args, &out, &stderr); code == 0 || out.Len() != 0 || !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "Unity asset references refused") {
+				t.Fatalf("refusal printed positive output or never reached public client: code%d out%q err%q", code, out.String(), stderr.String())
+			}
+			if name == "unregistered" && !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "registered service root required") {
+				t.Fatalf("root authority bypass: %s", stderr.String())
+			}
+			if name == "noncanonical-id" && !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "invalid asset query scope") {
+				t.Fatalf("rounded/coerced fileID: %s", stderr.String())
+			}
+		})
+	}
+	after, err := os.ReadFile(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if !bytes.Equal(before, after) {
+		t.Fatal("read-only CLI changed main store bytes")
+	}
+	mounted, err := store.MountReadOnly(path, store.LevelL0)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	defer mounted.Close()
+	if err := mounted.SetServiceMeta(ctx, store.ServiceMeta{ServiceID: "forbidden", Path: root}); err == nil {
+		t.Fatal("read-only mount accepted a write")
+	}
+	afterObs, err := mounted.QueryObservations(ctx, "fixture", "")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	afterEdges, err := mounted.TypedEdges(ctx, "fixture")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(beforeObs, afterObs) || !reflect.DeepEqual(edges, afterEdges) {
+		t.Fatal("asset CLI disturbed code observations/typed edges")
+	}
+}

+func TestUnityReferencesRendererKeepsPathsExactIDsAndPartialDenominators(t *testing.T) {
+	result := unityReferencesPresentationFixture()
+	for _, jsonOut := range []bool{false, true} {
+		var out bytes.Buffer
+		if err := renderUnityReferences(&out, result, jsonOut); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		if out.Len() > unityReferencesWireLimit {
+			t.Fatal("output exceeded budget")
+		}
+		for _, part := range []string{"current_partial", "9007199254740993", "-5831914722253275453", "game/Fixture/Assets/Cart.prefab", "game/Fixture/Assets/Model.fbx"} {
+			if !strings.Contains(out.String(), part) {
+				t.Fatalf("lost readable/exact identity %q: %s", part, out.String())
+			}
+		}
+		if jsonOut {
+			var decoded client.AssetReferenceResult
+			if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Bytes(), &decoded); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if decoded.Counts.NativeObservedUnbound != 1 || decoded.FamilyComplete {
+				t.Fatal("JSON inflated cohort coverage")
+			}
+		} else if !strings.Contains(out.String(), "package-unbound=1") || !strings.Contains(out.String(), "unpaired") {
+			t.Fatal("text hid partial/unpaired denominator")
+		}
+	}
+}

+		t.Fatalf("exact cap includes unexpected framing: %d", exact.Len())

+	result.Limitations[0] += "x"
+	for _, jsonOut := range []bool{false, true} {
+		var out bytes.Buffer
+		if err := renderUnityReferences(&out, result, jsonOut); err == nil || out.Len() != 0 {
+			t.Fatalf("overbudget result leaked positive output: bytes%d err%v", out.Len(), err)
+		}
+	}

+package main
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"net/http"
+	"os"
+)
+
+type sourceWindowReply struct {
+	Token           string `json:"source_window_token"`
+	State           string `json:"source_window_state"`
+	Pass            int    `json:"pass"`
+	Index           int    `json:"index"`
+	Offset          int64  `json:"offset"`
+	Bytes           int64  `json:"bytes"`
+	Files           int    `json:"files"`
+	Watermark       string `json:"watermark"`
+	ExclusionReview string `json:"exclusion_review"`
+}
+
+type sourceWindowExclusion struct {
+	Path   string `json:"path"`
+	Reason string `json:"reason"`
+}
+
+func readSourceWindowExclusions(path string) ([]sourceWindowExclusion, error) {
+	if path == "" {
+		return nil, nil
+	}
+	f, err := os.Open(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	defer f.Close()
+	raw, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, 1<<20+1))
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if len(raw) > 1<<20 {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("current source window: expected exclusions exceed 1 MiB")
+	}
+	var rows []sourceWindowExclusion
+	if err = json.Unmarshal(raw, &rows); err != nil || rows == nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("current source window: expected exclusions must be a JSON array")
+	}
+	for i, row := range rows {
+		if row.Path == "" || row.Reason == "" || i > 0 && rows[i-1].Path >= row.Path {
+			return nil, fmt.Errorf("current source window: expected exclusions must have sorted unique paths and reasons")
+		}
+	}
+	return rows, nil
+}
+
+// emitCurrentWindowRefusal is an operational result, never a plan verdict.
+// In JSON mode it preserves the reason without exposing any provisional row.
+func emitCurrentWindowRefusal(stdout, stderr io.Writer, service string, jsonOut bool, err error) int {
+	fmt.Fprintf(stderr, "error: %v\n", err)
+	if jsonOut {
+		_ = json.NewEncoder(stdout).Encode(map[string]any{
+			"service":                    service,
+			"source_scope":               "current_worktree",
+			"current_worktree_freshness": "unknown",
+			"source_window_state":        "refused",
+			"error":                      map[string]string{"code": "current_source_window_refused", "reason": err.Error()},
+		})
+	}
+	return 2
+}
+
+// Source-window lifecycle travels through verify_plan's existing tree-class
+// admission. An old daemon is identified by its published input schema.
+func callSourceWindow(hc *http.Client, baseURL, service, op, token string, expected ...[]sourceWindowExclusion) (sourceWindowReply, bool, error) {
+	window := map[string]any{"op": op}
+	args := map[string]any{"service": service, "source_window": window}
+	if len(expected) > 0 && expected[0] != nil {
+		window["expected_exclusions"] = expected[0]
+	}
+	if token != "" {
+		window["token"] = token
+	}
+	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": map[string]any{"name": "verify_plan", "arguments": args}})
+	req, err := originHeader(baseURL, bytes.NewReader(body))
+	if err != nil {
+		return sourceWindowReply{}, false, err
+	}
+	resp, err := hc.Do(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		return sourceWindowReply{}, false, err
+	}
+	defer resp.Body.Close()
+	raw, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, verifyPlanReadLimit+1))
+	if err != nil {
+		return sourceWindowReply{}, false, err
+	}
+	inner, err := unwrapRPCResult(raw)
+	if err != nil {
+		return sourceWindowReply{}, false, fmt.Errorf("current source window: %w", err)
+	}
+	var answer sourceWindowReply
+	if err = json.Unmarshal(inner, &answer); err != nil {
+		return answer, false, err
+	}
+	if answer.State == "" {
+		return answer, false, fmt.Errorf("current source window: daemon omitted lifecycle state")
+	}
+	return answer, true, nil
+}
+
+func sourceWindowSupported(hc *http.Client, baseURL string) (bool, error) {
+	body := []byte(`{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list","params":{}}`)
+	req, err := originHeader(baseURL, bytes.NewReader(body))
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, err
+	}
+	resp, err := hc.Do(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, err
+	}
+	defer resp.Body.Close()
+	raw, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, verifyPlanReadLimit+1))
+	if err != nil {
+		return false, err
+	}
+	var msg struct {
+		Result struct {
+			Tools []struct {
+				Name        string `json:"name"`
+				InputSchema struct {
+					Properties map[string]json.RawMessage `json:"properties"`
+				} `json:"inputSchema"`
+			} `json:"tools"`
+		} `json:"result"`
+		Error *struct {
+			Message string `json:"message"`
+		} `json:"error"`
+	}
+	if err = json.Unmarshal(raw, &msg); err != nil {
+		return false, err
+	}
+	if msg.Error != nil {
+		return false, fmt.Errorf("current source window: tools/list: %s", msg.Error.Message)
+	}
+	for _, tool := range msg.Result.Tools {
+		if tool.Name == "verify_plan" {
+			_, ok := tool.InputSchema.Properties["source_window"]
+			return ok, nil
+		}
+	}
+	return false, fmt.Errorf("current source window: verify_plan missing from tools/list")
+}
+
+func beginCurrentWindow(hc *http.Client, baseURL, service string, expected ...[]sourceWindowExclusion) (string, error) {
+	supported, err := sourceWindowSupported(hc, baseURL)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("current source window: capability check: %w", err)
+	}
+	if !supported {
+		if len(expected) > 0 && expected[0] != nil {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("current source window: daemon lacks reviewed-exclusion protocol")
+		}
+		return "", nil
+	}
+	begin, supported, err := callSourceWindow(hc, baseURL, service, "begin", "", expected...)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	if !supported {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("current source window: advertised lifecycle omitted state")
+	}
+	if begin.Token == "" || begin.State != "hashing_before" {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("current source window: malformed begin")
+	}
+	completed := false
+	defer func() {
+		if !completed {
+			abortCurrentWindow(hc, baseURL, service, begin.Token)
+		}
+	}()
+	for i := 0; i < 4096; i++ {
+		next, _, err := callSourceWindow(hc, baseURL, service, "advance", begin.Token)
+		if err != nil {
+			return "", err
+		}
+		if next.State == "provisional" {
+			completed = true
+			return begin.Token, nil
+		}
+		if next.State != "hashing_before" {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("current source window: invalid before-hash state %q", next.State)
+		}
+	}
+	return "", fmt.Errorf("current source window: before-hash continuation limit")
+}
+
+func abortCurrentWindow(hc *http.Client, baseURL, service, token string) {
+	if token != "" {
+		_, _, _ = callSourceWindow(hc, baseURL, service, "abort", token)
+	}
+}
+
+func closeCurrentWindow(hc *http.Client, baseURL, service, token string) error {
+	if token == "" {
+		return nil
+	}
+	for i := 0; i < 4096; i++ {
+		next, _, err := callSourceWindow(hc, baseURL, service, "close", token)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if next.State == "closed" {
+			return nil
+		}
+		if next.State != "provisional" {
+			return fmt.Errorf("current source window: invalid close state %q", next.State)
+		}
+	}
+	return fmt.Errorf("current source window: close continuation limit")
+}
+
+func fetchCurrentWindowResult(hc *http.Client, baseURL, service, token, id string) (httpVerifyResult, error) {
+	body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "method": "tools/call", "params": map[string]any{"name": "verify_plan", "arguments": map[string]any{"service": service, "source_window": map[string]any{"op": "result", "token": token, "report_id": id}}}})
+	req, err := originHeader(baseURL, bytes.NewReader(body))
+	if err != nil {
+		return httpVerifyResult{}, err
+	}
+	resp, err := hc.Do(req)
+	if err != nil {
+		return httpVerifyResult{}, err
+	}
+	defer resp.Body.Close()
+	raw, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, verifyPlanReadLimit+1))
+	if err != nil {
+		return httpVerifyResult{}, err
+	}
+	result, err := parseVerifyPlanResponse(raw)
+	if err != nil {
+		return result, err
+	}
+	if result.SourceWindowState != "closed" || result.SourceWindowReportID != id {
+		return httpVerifyResult{}, fmt.Errorf("current source window: final report identity differs")
+	}
+	return result, nil
+}

+package main
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"fmt"
+	"net/http"
+	"net/http/httptest"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"

+func assertCurrentWindowRefusal(t *testing.T, code int, stdout, stderr, wantReason string) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if code != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("window refusal exit %d, want 2; stdout=%s stderr=%s", code, stdout, stderr)
+	}
+	var doc map[string]json.RawMessage
+	if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(stdout), &doc); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("window refusal JSON: %v; stdout=%s stderr=%s", err, stdout, stderr)
+	}
+	for _, key := range []string{"reports", "tasks", "summary", "pass", "proven"} {
+		if _, ok := doc[key]; ok {
+			t.Fatalf("window refusal exposed provisional %s: %s", key, stdout)
+		}
+	}
+	var scope, freshness, state string
+	_ = json.Unmarshal(doc["source_scope"], &scope)
+	_ = json.Unmarshal(doc["current_worktree_freshness"], &freshness)
+	_ = json.Unmarshal(doc["source_window_state"], &state)
+	var failure struct {
+		Code   string `json:"code"`
+		Reason string `json:"reason"`
+	}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(doc["error"], &failure); err != nil || scope != "current_worktree" || freshness != "unknown" || state != "refused" || failure.Code != "current_source_window_refused" || !strings.Contains(failure.Reason, wantReason) || !strings.Contains(stderr, wantReason) {
+		t.Fatalf("incomplete window refusal: %s stderr=%s", stdout, stderr)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestCurrentWindowRefusalJSONNeverPublishesReports(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, phase := range []string{"begin", "advance", "close", "result"} {
+		t.Run(phase, func(t *testing.T) {
+			var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
+			code := emitCurrentWindowRefusal(&stdout, &stderr, "svc", true, fmt.Errorf("current source window: %s failed", phase))
+			assertCurrentWindowRefusal(t, code, stdout.String(), stderr.String(), phase+" failed")
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestCurrentWindowExclusionManifestBounded(t *testing.T) {
+	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "excluded.json")
+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(strings.Repeat("x", 1<<20+1)), 0600); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if _, err := readSourceWindowExclusions(path); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "exceed 1 MiB") {
+		t.Fatalf("unbounded exclusion manifest: %v", err)
+	}
+}
+
+func TestCurrentWindowFallbackRequiresAbsentPublishedCapability(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name       string
+		advertised bool
+		begin      string
+		wantErr    bool
+		wantToken  string
+	}{
+		{"old daemon", false, "", false, ""},
+		{"malformed new daemon", true, `{"service":"svc","summary":{}}`, true, ""},
+		{"refused new daemon", true, `{"error":"seal changed"}`, true, ""},

+				}

+					fmt.Fprint(w, `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"message":"seal changed"}}`)
+					return
+				}
+				json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(map[string]any{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "result": map[string]any{"content": []any{map[string]any{"text": tc.begin}}}})
+			}))
+			defer srv.Close()
+			token, err := beginCurrentWindow(srv.Client(), srv.URL, "svc")
+			if (err != nil) != tc.wantErr || token != tc.wantToken {
+				t.Fatalf("token=%q err=%v", token, err)
+			}

+	var req struct {

+// O14: unsupported L1 selection is an argument error, before subject/index/
+// oracle reads, extraction or output merging. Native files cannot override an
+// explicit unsupported -scip-defs request. These controls are not native proof.
+func TestCmdLangOracleDefinitionFamilyRefusesUnsupportedBeforeWork(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, existing := range []bool{false, true} {
+		t.Run(map[bool]string{false: "absent-output", true: "existing-output"}[existing], func(t *testing.T) {
+			dir := t.TempDir()
+			out, unmatched := filepath.Join(dir, "reading.json"), filepath.Join(dir, "unmatched.json")
+			const sentinel = "previous bytes must survive\n"
+			if existing {
+				if err := os.WriteFile(out, []byte(sentinel), 0o644); err != nil {
+					t.Fatal(err)
+				}
+			}
+			if err := os.WriteFile(unmatched, []byte(sentinel), 0o644); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}

+// Declaration targets establish statement binding, not actual-use dependencies.
+const declarationMembership = "declaration-membership/v1"
+
+type importOracleFile struct {
+	Tool      string               `json:"tool"`
+	Tier      string               `json:"tier"`
+	Imports   *[]importOracleEntry `json:"imports"`
+	Semantics string               `json:"imports_semantics"`
+}

+func readImportOracle(file string) (importOracleFile, error) {
+	var tf importOracleFile
+	b, err := os.ReadFile(file)
+	if err != nil {
+		return tf, err
+	}
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &tf); err != nil {
+		return tf, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", file, err)
+	}
+	var fields map[string]json.RawMessage
+	if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &fields); err != nil {
+		return tf, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", file, err)
+	}
+	if raw, present := fields["imports_semantics"]; present && (tf.Semantics == "" || bytes.Equal(bytes.TrimSpace(raw), []byte("null"))) {
+		return tf, fmt.Errorf("%s: unknown imports_semantics (explicit null/empty is not omitted)", file)
+	}
+	if tf.Semantics == declarationMembership {
+		// New membership envelopes use the existing closed neutral shape,
+		// including its entry fields; ordinary oracle formats are unchanged.
+		var strict toolOracleFile
+		dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(b))
+		dec.DisallowUnknownFields()
+		if err := dec.Decode(&strict); err != nil {
+			return tf, fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", file, err)
+		}
+		keys := make([]string, 0, len(fields))
+		for key := range fields {
+			keys = append(keys, key)
+		}
+		sort.Strings(keys)
+		for _, key := range keys {
+			switch key {
+			case "tool", "version", "tier", "source", "revision", "licence", "disclose", "imports", "imports_semantics":
+			default:
+				return tf, fmt.Errorf("%s: declaration membership field %q is not import-family evidence", file, key)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	return tf, nil
+}
+
+func checkImportSemantics(file string, tf importOracleFile, toolSelected, scipFileEdges bool) error {
+	if tf.Semantics == "" {
+		return nil
+	}
+	if tf.Semantics != declarationMembership {
+		return fmt.Errorf("%s: unknown imports_semantics %q", file, tf.Semantics)
+	}
+	if !toolSelected || !scipFileEdges {
+		return fmt.Errorf("%s: %s needs explicit -imports-from tool and SCIP dependency truth", file, tf.Semantics)
+	}
+	if tf.Imports == nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("%s: %s needs an imports array (empty [] is valid, missing/null is not)", file, tf.Semantics)
+	}
+	for _, e := range *tf.Imports {
+		if e.SamePackage {
+			return fmt.Errorf("%s: declaration membership cannot contain dependency-only same_package entries", file)
+		}
+		if !importMemberPath(e.Path) || e.ToPath != "" && !importMemberPath(e.ToPath) {
+			return fmt.Errorf("%s: declaration-membership paths must be canonical subject-relative slash paths", file)
+		}
+		if e.Line <= 0 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("%s: declaration membership needs a positive line", file)
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func importMemberPath(p string) bool {
+	return p != "" && p != "." && p != ".." && !strings.HasPrefix(p, "../") && !path.IsAbs(p) && path.Clean(p) == p && !strings.ContainsAny(p, "\\:\x00")
+}
+
+// Validate explicit family selection before extraction/scoring. Array presence,
+// not len, distinguishes a genuine empty native denominator from no oracle.
+func checkImportOracleSelection(opts oracleOpts) error {
+	n := 0
+	for _, file := range opts.tools {
+		tf, err := readImportOracle(file)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if err := checkImportSemantics(file, tf, opts.importsFromTool, opts.scip != ""); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if tf.Imports != nil {
+			n++
+		}
+	}
+	if opts.importsFromTool && (opts.scip == "" || n != 1) {
+		return fmt.Errorf("-imports-from tool needs -scip and exactly one tool oracle carrying an imports array (got %d)", n)
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+func TestCmdLangOracleImportsFromSelectionRefusals(t *testing.T) {
+	args := importsFromArgs(t)
+	refuseImportsFrom(t, append(args, "-imports-from", "guess"), "-imports-from is scip or tool")
+	missing := writeImportsFromOracle(t, `{"tool":"no-imports"}`)

+	empty := writeImportsFromOracle(t, `{"tool":"empty-imports","imports":[]}`)
+	refuseImportsFrom(t, append(args, "-tool-oracle", empty), "imports given alongside another imports oracle")
+	refuseImportsFrom(t, append(args, "-imports-from", "tool", "-tool-oracle", empty, "-tool-oracle", empty), "exactly one")
+	membership := writeImportsFromOracle(t, `{"tool":"membership","imports_semantics":"declaration-membership/v1","imports":[]}`)
+	refuseImportsFrom(t, append(args, "-tool-oracle", membership), "-imports-from tool")
+	noSCIP := []string{"-dialect", "rust", "-subject", copyFixture(t, "rustfixture"), "-imports-from", "tool", "-tool-oracle", membership}
+	refuseImportsFrom(t, noSCIP, "needs -scip")
+	// Merely naming an unreadable/non-SCIP file cannot authorize membership.
+	invalid := writeImportsFromOracle(t, "not a SCIP protobuf")
+	refuseImportsFrom(t, append(args, "-scip", invalid, "-imports-from", "tool", "-tool-oracle", membership), "decode index")

+func TestMembershipTargetSetDiagnosticsKeepWrongPartialAndDuplicateTargets(t *testing.T) {
+	entries := []importOracleEntry{{Path: "Use.cs", Line: 1, ToPath: "one/A.cs"}, {Path: "Use.cs", Line: 1, ToPath: "two/B.cs"}}
+	refs := []langbench.OracleImport{{Path: "Use.cs", Line: 1, ToPath: "one/A.cs", Explicit: true}, {Path: "Use.cs", Line: 1, ToPath: "two/B.cs", Explicit: true}}
+	inScope := map[string]bool{"Use.cs": true, "one/A.cs": true, "two/B.cs": true, "other/Wrong.cs": true}
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name                                string
+		targets                             []string
+		statementAgree, targetAgree, misses int
+	}{
+		{"complete", []string{"one/A.cs", "two/B.cs"}, 1, 2, 0},
+		{"partial", []string{"one/A.cs"}, 1, 1, 1},
+		{"wrong", []string{"other/Wrong.cs"}, 0, 0, 2},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			si := subjectImports{done: true, ok: true, name: "native-set-control", inScope: inScope,
+				sites: []langbench.ImportSite{{Path: "Use.cs", StartLine: 1, EndLine: 1, Targets: tc.targets}}}
+			sub := langbench.Subject{Counts: map[string]int{}, Families: map[string]string{}}
+			// Duplicate native rows never inflate statement/target truth.
+			truth := append(append([]langbench.OracleImport{}, refs...), refs...)
+			if err := si.score(truth, "A", "native-set-control", &sub); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if sub.Counts[langbench.CntImportsInRepo] != 1 || sub.Counts[langbench.CntImportsAgree] != tc.statementAgree ||
+				sub.Counts[langbench.CntImportEdgesTruth] != 2 || sub.Counts[langbench.CntImportEdgesAgree] != tc.targetAgree {
+				t.Fatalf("statement agreement hid target-set error: %v", sub.Counts)
+			}
+			misses := importMisses(entries, si.sites, inScope)
+			if len(misses) != tc.misses {
+				t.Fatalf("unmatched targets %v, want %d", misses, tc.misses)
+			}
+			for _, miss := range misses {
+				if !reflect.DeepEqual(miss.Targets, tc.targets) {
+					t.Fatalf("diagnostic lost actual targets: %+v", miss)
+				}
+			}
+			if _, exists := sub.Families[langbench.FamilyFileEdges]; exists {
+				t.Fatal("statement targets became dependencies")
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+package main
+
+import (
+	"encoding/json"
+	"flag"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/langbench"
+)
+
+// cmdLangUnityAsmdef calibrates declared assembly facts against an independently
+// retained Unity Editor receipt. It opens no store, invokes no Editor, and calls
+// no model or daemon. A partial/unjudged comparison cannot exit successfully.
+func cmdLangUnityAsmdef(args []string, stdout, stderr io.Writer) int {
+	flags := flag.NewFlagSet("lang-unity-asmdef", flag.ContinueOnError)
+	flags.SetOutput(stderr)
+	root := flags.String("project", "", "Unity project root (required)")
+	oracle := flags.String("oracle", "", "retained CompilationPipeline JSON (required)")
+	if err := flags.Parse(args); err != nil {
+		return 2
+	}
+	if *root == "" || *oracle == "" || flags.NArg() != 0 {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "usage: indexbench lang-unity-asmdef -project PATH -oracle RECEIPT.json")
+		return 2
+	}
+	raw, err := os.ReadFile(*oracle)
+	if err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "lang-unity-asmdef:", err)
+		return 2
+	}
+	reading, err := langbench.CalibrateUnityAsmdefs(os.DirFS(*root), raw)
+	if err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "lang-unity-asmdef:", err)
+		return 2
+	}
+	enc := json.NewEncoder(stdout)
+	enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
+	if err = enc.Encode(reading); err != nil {
+		fmt.Fprintln(stderr, "lang-unity-asmdef:", err)
+		return 2
+	}
+	if !reading.Passed || !reading.Complete {
+		return 1
+	}
+	return 0
+}

+func TestLangUnityAsmdefCommand(t *testing.T) {
+	root := t.TempDir()
+	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(root, "Assets"), 0o755); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	def := []byte(`{"name":"Fixture.Core","noEngineReferences":true,"overrideReferences":true,"precompiledReferences":[]}`)
+	src := []byte("namespace Fixture { class Core {} }\n")
+	for name, b := range map[string][]byte{"Core.asmdef": def, "Core.cs": src} {
+		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "Assets", name), b, 0o644); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+	}
+	hash := func(b []byte) string { s := sha256.Sum256(b); return hex.EncodeToString(s[:]) }
+	oracle := map[string]any{"schemaVersion": 1, "oracle": "UnityEditor.Compilation.CompilationPipeline.GetAssemblies", "unityVersion": "6000.3.15f1", "buildTarget": "StandaloneOSX", "assembliesType": "Editor", "scope": "synthetic CLI fixture", "availableAssemblyNames": []string{"Fixture.Core"}, "assemblies": []map[string]any{{"name": "Fixture.Core", "asmdefPath": "Assets/Core.asmdef", "definitionSha256": hash(def), "noEngineReferencesDeclared": true, "overrideReferencesDeclared": true, "precompiledReferencesDeclared": []string{}, "declaredReferences": []string{}, "assemblyReferences": []string{}, "compiledAssemblyReferences": []string{"System.Runtime"}, "emittedReferencesAvailable": true, "emittedAssemblyReferences": []string{"System.Runtime"}, "sourceFiles": []string{"Assets/Core.cs"}, "sourceFacts": []map[string]string{{"path": "Assets/Core.cs", "owner": "Fixture.Core.dll", "sha256": hash(src)}}}}}
+	raw, err := json.Marshal(oracle)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	receipt := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "oracle.json")
+	if err := os.WriteFile(receipt, raw, 0o644); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
+	if code := mainRun([]string{"lang-unity-asmdef", "-project", root, "-oracle", receipt}, &stdout, &stderr); code != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("code=%d stdout=%s stderr=%s", code, &stdout, &stderr)
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(stdout.String(), `"owner_matches": 1`) || !strings.Contains(stdout.String(), `"passed": true`) {
+		t.Fatal(stdout.String())
+	}
+	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "Assets", "Core.cs"), []byte("changed"), 0o644); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	stdout.Reset()
+	stderr.Reset()
+	if code := mainRun([]string{"lang-unity-asmdef", "-project", root, "-oracle", receipt}, &stdout, &stderr); code != 1 || !strings.Contains(stdout.String(), "source-digest-mismatch") {
+		t.Fatalf("false pass code=%d stdout=%s stderr=%s", code, &stdout, &stderr)
+	}
+	stdout.Reset()
+	stderr.Reset()
+	if code := mainRun([]string{"lang-unity-asmdef"}, &stdout, &stderr); code != 2 {
+		t.Fatalf("missing flags exit=%d", code)
+	}

diff --git a/docs/changelog/unreleased/bounded-current-source-window.md b/docs/changelog/unreleased/bounded-current-source-window.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000000000000000000000000000000000..3c8389b7d506f1afa770fe2c6db77aeca455a823
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/changelog/unreleased/bounded-current-source-window.md
@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@
+### Changed
+
+- Default daemon `verify` and `plans status` can validate sealed source-reference facts against the current tree in a bounded two-pass observation window. Each continuation accepts at most 64 MiB and has a five-second deadline. A synchronous filesystem read can overrun that deadline; its return invalidates the window instead of publishing a current verdict. Failed identity or close refuses the current verdict; excluded files keep absence Unknown. Older daemons retain the live scan with its partial disclosure.
+- The console's cached plan section explicitly reports current-worktree freshness as `unknown`; it does not inherit a CLI run's completed-window receipt.
+- A refused current window returns exit 2 and a JSON operational refusal with `current_worktree_freshness: unknown`, a reason, and no plan verdicts. A later re-ingest can supply a new seal for a fresh window.

@@ -1365,6 +1365,38 @@ dialect does not read and stays in scope when the subject holds it), so the benc
 edges ingest stores. EMF and PutMetricData emitters (Stage B) and a telemetry fetch (ADR-058)
 are not read.
 
+### Unity assembly declarations and compiler receipts
+
+The `unity-asmdef` doc dialect exposes `.asmdef` assembly/reference declarations
+and the explicit `noEngineReferences`/`overrideReferences` settings. Reference
+names, including unresolved GUID strings, stay source-tier facts: no `Calls`,
+file-resolved dependency edges, or typed C# call edges are emitted. Its support
+row stays unmeasured until an appropriate public corpus reading exists.
+
+`indexbench lang-unity-asmdef -project PATH -oracle RECEIPT.json` compares these
+facts against an independently retained Unity Editor CompilationPipeline receipt.
+It binds definitions and source files by SHA256, compares named references against
+both available and compiler-referenced assemblies, and checks nearest-asmdef
+source ownership against `GetAssemblyNameFromScriptPath`. Missing/changed files,
+false references and wrong owners refuse. GUID resolution and asmref ownership
+are explicitly unjudged; platform/define selection is observed only for the
+receipt's named Editor/Player configuration, never inferred for other targets.
+
+For an assembly declaring no engine references, its compiler check refuses
+`UnityEngine*` and exact `UnityEditor`/`UnityEditor.CoreModule` references. Other
+Unity-prefixed available references are explicit notices: an Editor build SDK
+can remain available even with `overrideReferences=true`. That setting governs
+project/package precompiled plugins, not every injected Editor SDK. Separately,
+when loaded emitted-assembly metadata is observed, the instrument checks for no
+Unity-prefixed emitted dependency; missing metadata stays unjudged. Available
+compiler references, emitted assembly dependencies and typed/runtime calls are
+different evidence. Neither an available SDK name nor `noEngineReferences` alone
+proves an actual SDK dependency or a violation of Unity's property. See the [Unity 6.3 assembly properties](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.3/Documentation/Manual/class-AssemblyDefinitionImporter.html).
+A successful receipt comparison is neither typed reachability nor a runtime,
+scene-call or full language-grade claim. The command opens no store, launches no
+Editor, and calls no model or daemon; exit 0 requires a complete passing reading,
+1 names counterexamples or unjudged facts, and 2 is operational/schema failure.
+

+### Native import-family calibration boundary (2026-10-20)
+
+`lang-oracle -imports-from tool` selects exactly one neutral imports array alongside an actual SCIP dependency/typed oracle. A `declaration-membership/v1` row states namespace declaration contribution, not actual-use file dependency truth; it cannot grade the dependency fallback. Missing, malformed, unsupported, duplicate or unscoreable selected families refuse rather than silently changing oracle. The default remains SCIP imports. +**Decision models.** None applies. Source spans, symbol identity, import-family selection, hashes and compiler diagnostics are deterministic; provider none, no model egress.

+### C# descriptive test candidates and source-only asset provenance
+
+C# static test reach uses recognized NUnit/Unity attribute heads, not a method-name prefix. +# Source-bound SCIP imports
+
+SCIP supplies typed references. A source receipt binds an index to the actual
+source, generated projects, compiler configuration and reference assemblies
+used by its external producer. It is a deterministic freshness declaration,
+not a signature, a compiler execution attestation or a language excellence grade.
+Fathom does not execute or install the producer.
+
+`scip-dotnet` indexes require a sidecar at `INDEX.scip.receipt.json`. Other
+producers retain legacy behavior without a sidecar; providing one opts that
+index into the same contract. Do not copy a receipt from another index or
+refresh its hashes without rerunning the producer against those inputs.
+
+The closed JSON schema is `fathom.scip.source/v1`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema": "fathom.scip.source/v1",
+  "status": "complete",
+  "root": "/absolute/local/repository",
+  "index_sha256": "64 lowercase hexadecimal characters",
+  "producer": {
+    "name": "scip-dotnet",
+    "version": "the index metadata's actual version",
+    "distribution_version": "the installed distribution's version",
+    "package_path": "/absolute/path/to/pinned/producer.nupkg",
+    "package_sha256": "64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"
+  },
+  "inputs": [
+    {"path": "src/Worker.cs", "sha256": "64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"},
+    {"path": "Actual.csproj", "sha256": "64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"},
+    {"path": "/absolute/path/to/reference.dll", "sha256": "64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"},
+    {"path": "/absolute/path/to/pinned/producer.nupkg", "sha256": "64 lowercase hexadecimal characters"}
+  ],
+  "inventories": [
+    {"root": "src", "pattern": "*.cs", "paths": ["src/Worker.cs"]}
+  ]
+}
+```
+
+The example hashes are placeholders, so this example deliberately cannot pass.
+Paths in `inputs` may be repository-relative or absolute local files. External
+SDK/reference files must be named individually; inventory roots must stay
+inside the repository. Inventories recurse and accept a simple `*.extension`
+pattern. Their paths are repository-relative or absolute. Add separate
+inventories for assembly declarations or other producer inputs as appropriate.
+The limits are 64 MiB per source-bound index, 8 MiB of receipt JSON, 20,000
+input files totaling at most 1 GiB, and 100,000 walked entries per inventory; exceeding a limit refuses the typed import.
+
+The root must match both the service and SCIP metadata. The producer name and
+metadata version must match the index. Every SCIP document must have a current
+source hash and belong to an unchanged inventory. Every inventory member also
+requires an input hash, including files with no SCIP definitions. Every declared input is
+hashed, including generated `.csproj` configuration/defines and referenced DLLs.
+For scip-dotnet, a project hash, reference assembly hash and a bound distribution
+package identity are mandatory. The producer must enumerate its real input
+closure; Fathom checks that declaration, it does not implement MSBuild or infer
+undeclared compiler dependencies.
+
+A producer writes `status: "started"` **before** attempting regeneration, then
+atomically publishes `complete` only after the producer succeeds, diagnostics
+and document coverage pass, and all input hashes still match. A failed attempt
+must leave its sidecar incomplete, even when an older index remains on disk.
+Publish the completed receipt last so partial writes cannot look current.
+
+CLI ingest, direct client import, MCP ingest and daemon refresh share the same
+validation. Root `index.scip`, selected state-directory `scip/*.scip` indexes
+(with `.fathom/scip/*.scip` legacy fallback), and previously registered
+source-bound indexes are reconciled after ingestion. A missing/stale/mixed or
+incomplete receipt refuses typed enrichment, clears only that index's previous
+typed rows and evicts its served graph memo. Other producers' rows remain.
+A refused source-bound import makes ingest fail even when syntax was updated;
+read the diagnostic rather than interpreting the syntax update as a full pass.
+
+State-directory selection uses the same `statedir.SCIPIndexes` precedence as
+CLI ingest. A preferred state-directory file shadows the same legacy basename;
+remembered typed rows for that shadowed legacy index are cleared, while its
+registration and both artifacts remain. A malformed preferred index does not
+fall back to the legacy copy. Root `index.scip` stays independent. This does not
+move old files, rewrite receipts or claim a source binding for an older store.
+
+Freshness is checked at import/refresh boundaries, including file refresh.
+This does **not** continuously hash the filesystem on every query. Before a
+refresh completes, the normal index-staleness/basis rules still apply. It does
+not prove callback execution, serialized scene references, remote behavior or
+successful tests. Raw local producers and source receipts stay distinct from
+runtime test evidence.
+
+Stores created before this contract did not retain the producer identity of
+each imported index. If both an old artifact and its receipt are already gone,
+that identity cannot be reconstructed from its edges. Upgrade with a fresh
+store or explicitly rebuild the affected service; do not present an unknown
+pre-upgrade typed store as source-bound. Once registered under this contract,
+an index remains remembered even if both files disappear.
+
+## Decision models
+
+None applies. Content hashes, inventories, identity matching and namespace
+invalidation are deterministic local checks; no provider or model egress is used.

+# Native Unity NUnit execution evidence
+
+This is a local producer assertion and integrity contract. It does not verify a signature or defend against a malicious local writer. Fathom never starts Unity. Existing test-kit vocabulary/statuses stay authoritative; this bounded native adapter adds source provenance and exact C# identity, not a new certification system. ADR-043's non-Go trigger has fired. I8 remains informational, I43 remains unchanged: a dirty/source-hash-bound native runtime observation is not a live clean-commit certificate.
+
+The example below is a schema sketch with placeholder hashes and deliberately cannot validate. All keys are closed. No credentials, arbitrary provider or remote endpoint is accepted.
+
+The receipt alone is not the attested result. ADR-043/I43 and deferred F76 require a producer-generated standard #TestResult envelope, with `key=sha256:<source digest>`, full native case identity/status/duration, actual commit/dirty facts, `env.runnerClass=unity`, Editor toolchain digest, and artifacts `unity-nunit-xml`/`unity-source-inputs`. `attestation.path/sha256` bind that record. XML/receipt only stays UNKNOWN and out of execution tables. A local unsigned standard envelope is accepted as the producer assertion already supported by Fathom; no signature is invented. The native importer will cross-check all case outcomes and identities and cannot be bypassed by routing an unbound C# envelope through generic file/name ingestion.
+
+The source-input artifact names the canonical bytes defined below, not a differently encoded JSON file. It can be retained as source-inputs.bin. The envelope does not refer to the final receipt hash, avoiding a cycle. `trace.traceId` equals run_id so native run identity is part of the standard content-addressed record. Use the regular active receipt path `<root>/.artifacts/unity-tests/active/<project>/<mode>.json`, replaced atomically with started before each next attempt; archive completed receipts separately. The importer retains that active path and completed hash, so newer incomplete attempts invalidate an older pass without an attempt scheduler or new witness subsystem. Flake policy for the no-retry producer is `{maxRetries:0,quarantineAfter:3,budget:"0%"}`; no retry/flake lineage is inferred. Case id is `<native assembly without .dll>::<native fullname>`, case name is the full native fullname. Skipped and Inconclusive map to standard skip with raw distinctions retained by XML; an all-nonpassing run never becomes pass. A schema sketch is not real evidence.
+
+## Generic envelope boundary
+
+Generic non-Go file/name joins remain available for ordinary envelopes. A bare or DSSE envelope declaring Unity through `env.runnerClass` (case-insensitive) or native artifact names `unity-nunit-xml` / `unity-source-inputs` instead requires the paired native adapter. A generic envelope declaration cannot supply a validated source-bound native binding. This is an unsigned local producer boundary, not authentication against a writer who forges all provenance.
+
+## Producer ordering
+
+Write the receipt as `status:started` before launching the recorded Editor command. Capture `source.inputs`/inventories before launch; include the actual project Assets (all regular files including .meta), Packages and ProjectSettings trees, relevant generated project/assembly-reference/config inputs outside those trees, plus exact producer and Editor bytes. After process exit, parse the actual native XML, capture the same trees/inputs again and only publish `complete` if unchanged. Preserve refused/failed attempts rather than refreshing old hashes. Use a unique immutable `-testResults` path per run. Never stamp historical XML: it can only be parsed as unattested data.
+
+Complete requires every shown field except `symbols`; `attestation` is mandatory and references the existing test-kit #TestResult record, whose bytes must agree with XML and source facts; started may be incomplete and is always refused for execution admission. `mode` is EditMode or PlayMode. `target`, filter and command are exact facts, not inferred from XML. `command[0]` resolves to editor.path; required argv pairs are -projectPath, -buildTarget, -testPlatform and -testResults, plus -runTests. Nonempty filter requires an identical -testFilter pair. XML.path resolves to the command's -testResults path, without following an unrelated replaced symlink. Safe argv only; a producer must never put secrets in receipt commands.
+
+`exit_code:0` is required for an all-passed XML. A complete failed run may have the native nonzero test-failure exit; license/compiler failure with old passing XML is refused. XML start/end must fit the producer interval, allowing only its native whole-second timestamp precision. The receipt cannot prove its producer wrote started on time; that is the trusted runner's responsibility and a fixture/integration obligation.
+
+## Source digest algorithm
+
+Inputs are `{path,sha256}` rows. Internal paths are forward-slash repository relative, external SDK/reference input paths may be absolute. Inventories stay inside root, walk all regular files recursively, and name the exact sorted membership in `paths`. No traversal, backslashes, NUL/control bytes, invalid UTF8, duplicate paths, symlink files/directories or nonregular members. Every inventory member must have a hash. All current input hashes and inventory membership are checked again on admission and when native runtime evidence is read.
+
+Canonical source bytes are UTF8:
+
+1. Literal `fathom.unity.inputs/v1\n`.
+2. For each distinct inventory root, sorted by path: `tree\0` + root + `\n`.
+3. For each distinct input sorted by its path: `file\0` + path + `\0` + lowercase sha256 + `\n`.
+
+Here `\0` and `\n` mean actual NUL and newline bytes, not literal backslash characters. SHA256 of those bytes is `source.before_sha256`; complete must carry an identical `source.after_sha256`. Inventory membership is redundant with hashed inputs and verified by actual walk. The completed receipt retains the before manifest. Root/project/producer/Editor/command/XML identities are additional validated receipt fields, not silently folded into this digest.
+
+The root and project must match the target service/project. Producer.path and Editor.path are individually hash-checked. Reference/config closure is producer-declared rather than independently discovered by Fathom. Maxima will be explicit bounded constants; no unbounded XML/entity/tree or external fetch.
+
+## Typed method identity and variants
+
+Optional `symbols` references an actual SCIP artifact plus its source receipt, both hash-bound. Its root/source validation must succeed using the existing native source-receipt contract. Only exact, unique typed C# declarations matching native assembly + classname/methodname and source location can join; the indexed declaration must carry the current extractor-epoch fingerprint of the same raw hash-bound source bytes, so a stale syntax row cannot borrow a fresh SCIP definition. Raw, prior-epoch and stale fingerprints are refused; the source comparison reads at most 16MiB per C# file. Nested/generic/overloaded/duplicate or absent identities stay refused/unjoined rather than guessed. No stripping argument strings to do a bare-name join. Parameterized cases preserve their full native name/id and each outcome, grouped under one proven method identity only after that binding.
+
+Omitted/unusable symbols can still yield an explicitly unattested/unjoined parse, but cannot yield a native runtime PASS. It is acceptable for the producer to omit symbols when there is no current real index; do not repair an old index's source receipt to manufacture freshness. Parser-only fixtures must never enter test_runs.
+
+Any nonempty native testFilter stays unjoined/UNKNOWN: selected cohort counts do not prove the unfiltered method family, and this version does not interpret filter grammar. The full filtered observation may still be admitted.
+
+For a requested method, the newest complete matching native run is evaluated as a cohort: any failed variant => FAIL; all expected variants passed => PASS; skipped/inconclusive/explicit/missing variants or stale/absent/mixed receipt/source => UNKNOWN. Full raw outcomes/labels remain available. An older pass never overrides a newer unknown/incomplete result. Use a canonical symbol key or the full namespace/class/method for runtime lookup. A bare method is accepted only when unique; class-only suffixes and bare/namespace/overload ambiguity cannot select an arbitrary family. These observations do not invent framework dispatch/call edges, runtime coverage of reached functions, or human/game quality.
+
+## CLI and storage
+
+Extend existing `tests ingest` with explicit `--unity-nunit XML --unity-receipt JSON`, mutually exclusive with --results. No new MCP tool. Native provenance must survive store roundtrip and be revalidated by runtime reads. The additive store/read seam retains run identity and the active receipt hash, rechecks the receipt, XML, envelope, source and native SCIP sidecar on each runtime evidence load, then uses the complete method cohort. Native rows are explicitly excluded from the live-certificate ladder. Existing Go/envelope joins remain unchanged. This adapter is opt-in and does not change default test ingestion or execute a command.
+
+## Decision models
+
+None applies. XML identities/outcomes, content hashes, inventories, input bounds and cohort aggregation are deterministic. Provider none; no source/model egress.
+
+
+## Implemented bounded refusals and limits
+
+This candidate accepts bare standard JSON #TestResult only for native admission; existing generic DSSE handling remains unchanged. Receipt/standard JSON max32MiB; native XML max16MiB, 100,000 leaves, depth64; source closure max100,000 inputs /8GiB; inventory max100,000 entries per root; optional SCIP max256MiB and its existing native receipt limits. Unknown native producer/version and Editor argv outside the safe allowlist refuse. Only EditMode/PlayMode and the four explicitly selected desktop/Web targets are supported.
+
+Native C# binding additionally requires the matching literal AssemblyName and Compile membership in a hash-bound generated .csproj directly under the selected project. This is declared project ownership with a real typed definition, not independent Unity compilation proof; retain the assembly oracle separately. Overloads, nested/generic identities, missing/duplicate declarations, ambiguous method cohorts and Retry/Repeat syntax remain unjoined/UNKNOWN. No retry lineage is fabricated. The parser preserves the observed Unity root state `Failed(Child)` while requiring failed native leaves; arbitrary compound outcomes refuse. It refuses malformed counts, duplicate identities and case-nested test structure; unsupported suite-only setup failures stay refused rather than guessed.
+
+A source-bound standard record without symbols may be stored as an unjoined observation. It cannot yield runtime_pass. XML/receipt without the standard record never enters test_runs. A newer started receipt invalidates the previous result without inventing another execution or updating old hashes. Rechecking uses local reads at the runtime evidence load boundary; there is no filesystem watcher or per-call atomic snapshot guarantee.
+
+
+## Invoke
+
+The external runner must write started before invoking Unity, produce native XML
+and the standard envelope from that same attempt, and atomically publish the
+completed active receipt. Fathom does not provide or invoke that runner:
+
+```sh
+fathom tests ingest --manifest /checkout --service workshop --store /scratch/evidence.sqlite \
+  --unity-nunit /checkout/artifacts/runs/run-unique/results.xml \
+  --unity-receipt /checkout/.artifacts/unity-tests/active/game/Workshop/EditMode.json
+```
+
+Completed archive receipts cannot replace the active receipt for admission. The
+same project/mode active path must publish started before *every* next attempt,
+including a differently filtered attempt, to invalidate earlier results. Never
+rewrite archived XML, envelope, source manifest, symbols or receipts to make a
+historical run appear fresh. A missing symbol artifact is an honest unjoined
+observation; produce a new actual index before a new execution for typed runtime
+identity.
+
+The `producer` name/version supported by this contract is
+`unity-local-runner`/`1`. This names a reviewed local producer assertion; it is
+not an authenticated identity or allowlist of hash-trusted executables. The
+operator owns the runner's before-launch ordering and input-closure declaration.
+The importer validates its declared files, argv, intervals and standard result.
+No signature, hosted execution, malicious-host defense or model call is claimed.
+
+## Minimal shape
+
+All complete receipt keys below are required except `symbols`. Paths and hashes
+are placeholders; source inputs must include all inventory files, generated
+project/reference closure, producer and actual Editor executable. External
+reference paths may be absolute. The three inventories are exactly the selected
+project's Assets, Packages and ProjectSettings, including .meta files.
+
+```json
+{
+  "schema": "fathom.unity.nunit/v1", "status": "complete", "run_id": "run-unique",
+  "root": "/checkout", "project": "game/Workshop", "mode": "EditMode",
+  "target": "WebGL", "filter": "", "started_at": "2026-10-19T12:00:00Z",
+  "finished_at": "2026-10-19T12:00:03Z",
+  "producer": {"name":"unity-local-runner","version":"1","path":"Tools/runner.py","sha256":"<sha256>"},
+  "editor": {"path":"/sdk/Unity","version":"6000.3.15f1","sha256":"<sha256>"},
+  "command": ["/sdk/Unity","-batchmode","-projectPath","/checkout/game/Workshop",
+    "-buildTarget","WebGL","-runTests","-testPlatform","EditMode",
+    "-testResults","/checkout/artifacts/runs/run-unique/results.xml"],
+  "exit_code": 0,
+  "xml": {"path":"artifacts/runs/run-unique/results.xml","sha256":"<sha256>"},
+  "source": {"before_sha256":"<canonical source sha256>","after_sha256":"<same sha256>",
+    "inputs":[{"path":"<input>","sha256":"<sha256>"}],
+    "inventories":[{"root":"game/Workshop/Assets","paths":["<all files>"]},
+      {"root":"game/Workshop/Packages","paths":["<all files>"]},
+      {"root":"game/Workshop/ProjectSettings","paths":["<all files>"]}]},
+  "attestation": {"path":"artifacts/runs/run-unique/test-result.json","sha256":"<sha256>"},
+  "symbols": {"scip_path":"artifacts/csharp.scip","scip_sha256":"<sha256>",
+    "source_receipt_sha256":"<sha256 of csharp.scip.receipt.json>"}
+}
+```
+
+For the envelope, top-level verdict is `fail` if any native case failed, `pass`
+only if every selected leaf passed, otherwise `error`. Native Skipped and
+Inconclusive map to case `skip`; full distinctions, messages and stack traces
+remain in raw XML. Case ids are `<assembly without .dll>::<native fullname>`,
+case names retain the entire native fullname including parameters, attempts is
+1, and native seconds map exactly to Go-style durations. `timing.startedAt`
+represents native start time; env contains actual commit/dirty/race facts,
+runnerClass `unity` and `toolchainDigest=sha256:<Editor digest>`.
+`trace.traceId=run_id`; artifact refs are `unity-nunit-xml` and
+`unity-source-inputs` with their actual digests. Flake policy is
+`{maxRetries:0,quarantineAfter:3,budget:"0%"}`. The native reader validates the
+standard mirrored #TestResult schema as well as these cross-field constraints.
+A suite-only setup failure with no failed leaf is currently refused, not guessed.
+
+
+Current project calibration is native macOS ARM64. The generic parser/unit/store
+fixtures do not establish another Editor host, target, package version or Unity
+platform module. The four target values describe explicit runner selection,
+not execution proof for Windows/Linux players. Keep host/platform evidence
+separate from C# syntax, typed binding and runtime result facts.
+
+
+## Store compatibility
+
+Native joins are stored in additive `test_cases.native_symbol_key`; legacy
+`test_symbol_key` stays empty for those cases. Older readers cannot accidentally
+interpret one native variant as an attested Go-style result without receipt
+validation. Current readers project the protected key only alongside native
+binding metadata. Old read-only stores without the new optional columns retain
+their legacy Go evidence reads; transitional native rows without protected keys
+are suppressed. A new opt-in/disposable store is still the recommended adoption
+path, with the stable default and its configuration preserved.
+
+## Loaded-assembly identity limit
+
+This validator checks declared source/reference byte hashes and optional source-bound SCIP identity. It does not parse or compare NUnit-loaded test-assembly MVIDs against the compiler/assembly oracle. Those separate producer facts are not a validated loaded-assembly-to-compiler identity guarantee. A receipt schema sketch or calibration fixture never fills this gap.
