 | `read_source` | `service` (req), `file` (req, repo-relative), `start_line` (opt), `end_line` (opt), `max_bytes` (opt, default **8000**, ceiling 16000), `ref` (opt, a commit, tag or branch) | `{file, lines: [{line, text}], start_line, end_line, total_lines, clamped_eof, note?, elided?, ref?, commit?}` | Bounded, read-only raw-text read from the service's INDEXED corpus (T5-4, docs/plans/trust-and-tokenomics.md) — the agent surface's `sed -n` equivalent, line-numbered so results are pinnable as citations. **`ref`** (WAE-3): the file's bytes as committed at that commit, read through git in the corpus root (`git ls-tree` then `git cat-file`; no lock, no fetch, no prompt), never the working tree; the response adds `ref` and the `commit` it resolved to, and without `ref` the read and its response are unchanged. Every filter below holds at a ref and its refusal names it, and at a ref a symlink or a submodule entry is refused by its mode (never followed), as is a ref starting with `-`, an unknown ref, a path absent at it, or a corpus root that is not a git work tree. Not the first move after a `find_symbol` hit (already carries file+line) or `symbol_context` (already carries the body) — reach for it only for bytes neither carried. No `start_line`/`end_line`: a capped whole-file view from line 1. Capped at 200 lines / 8000 bytes per call by default (SB-3, docs/plans/strengths-bench.md; O31/O32 — half the old default, since `read_source` was the largest single per-tool payload contributor in the home bench), whichever is hit first; the byte cap bounds the `lines` array as sent — each row's `{line, text}` envelope and JSON escaping count, as `fitToBudget` counts every other budgeted tool's rows (BP-42, docs/plans/bench-pyramid.md: counting raw text let an 8000-byte read reach the model as 11,189 bytes); `max_bytes` raises the byte cap for one call, up to a 16000-byte ceiling; `end_line == total_lines` in the response means EOF was reached; a first line whose row alone does not fit the byte cap (a line longer than the cap, or one a little under it raw once its envelope and escaping count) comes back TRUNCATED (on a rune boundary) so its row fits, with the note set — never whole (minified JS cannot void the cap); the cut itself adds nothing to `elided` (no line was DROPPED, only that one line's content was cut), so a single-line range cut this way carries no `elided` block; a multi-line range the cap stopped short of its natural end carries `elided` (`{count, of, ordering, how_to_get_more}`) naming how many LINES were dropped. **Readable = what ingest walks, enforced:** refuses (RPC error) a `.fathomignore`'d path (the same compiled matcher `Discover` applies, file and ancestor dirs), the always-skipped directories (`vendor`, `.git`, `testdata`, `generated`, `node_modules`, `.idea`, `.vscode`, `.claude`), `.env`-pattern files (unconditional defense in depth — secrets-shaped files are never served even when a repo forgot to ignore them; other dot-paths like `.github/` stay readable since they ARE indexed), a file over the 2MB read ceiling (`os.Stat`-checked before any read; equals the indexer's own extraction cap, so such files aren't in the index either), a binary file (`connector.IsBinary`), an absolute `file`, path traversal, a symlink resolving outside the corpus root (`filepath.EvalSymlinks` containment on both the root and the candidate — a same-corpus symlink target reads fine), and an EXPLICIT range wider than the line cap (narrow it, or make repeated calls — never silently narrowed). An explicit `start_line`/`end_line` landing beyond EOF is clamped, not refused, and noted (`clamped_eof:true`); running past the line/byte cap is separately noted. An empty file reports `total_lines: 0`. The corpus root is resolved from `ServiceMeta` with the same absolute-path discipline as `review_diff`'s project-rule loader (O10/C4 class; SR-27 folded the standalone `arch_conformance` tool into `review_diff`'s in-process check): a service with no recorded root, or a pre-O10 relative one, is refused with a re-ingest pointer rather than resolved against the daemon's ambient CWD. Also on the agent/companion surface. |

+`verify_plan` also accepts `source_window: {op, token, report_id,
+expected_exclusions}`. `op` is `begin|advance|close|result|abort`;
+plan calls use `{token}` for CLI controlled default-current batches. `begin`
+returns a token for one service and sealed generation; `advance` streams the
+before hash in bounded units; plan calls carrying that token return pending
+Unknown rows and an opaque `source_window_report_id`. `close` streams the after
+hash; only then does `result` release the stored final report for each ID.
+The close receipt
+includes cumulative bytes/files and SHA-256 for each excluded path. A missing, expired,
+cancelled or changed window refuses by name. Excluded source rows disclose
+their path and reason and leave absent references Unknown. Without a token,
+the ordinary live scan and its partial/lower-bound fields remain in force.
+The protocol keeps typed, native and attested runtime evidence separate.
+For a full-reference qualification with exclusions, `begin` must receive
+`source_window.expected_exclusions`: the sorted exact reviewed `{path,reason}`
+array. Without it, close and final results say `exclusion_review: unsupplied`,
+so the observation cannot certify the reviewed-exclusion requirement.
+The CLI owns and closes its own window. A qualification driver that needs the
+same window for the original 15 plan calls and four external controls must use
+this MCP lifecycle directly, submit all 19 calls with one token, close once,
+then fetch every final report ID. Separate CLI invocations do not share a token.
+If any phase refuses, the default CLI exits 2. JSON mode emits only an
+operational refusal (`current_worktree_freshness: unknown`, reason, no plan
+verdicts); re-ingest and begin a new window to recover.
+
 `markers`, `routes`, `endpoint_inventory`, and `dependencies` (plus their
 `test_debt`/`api_routes`/`deps` aliases) were deleted as zero-call
 structural redundancy (surface prune, `docs/plans/archive/surface-prune.md`).

+# Native CUE registry-denial policy
+
+Native CUE typed enrichment supports the admitted local module and builtin
+packages. It now supplies an explicit refusal registry; `CUE_REGISTRY=inline:{}`
+was not an offline switch in the pinned CUE loader. External modules are refused,
+including modules already present in an operator's persistent cache. No registry,
+credential reader, transport or persistent module-cache client is constructed by
+this boundary. This does not sandbox local filesystem reads.
+
+The CUE pass now has an independent policy epoch. A completed/partial state from
+before this policy is rechecked on the next ordinary ingest even when no source
+changed. Successful current-policy passes resume normal unchanged-input gating.
+No extractor epoch, database schema or other producer namespace changes.
+
+CUE can collapse a failed multi-package load into a single synthetic instance
+and discard the registry error's type. When the explicit registry observes a
+denial, enrichment therefore performs at most one native retry for each stored
+CUE package identity. Only identities whose own retry invokes that refusal
+registry lose prior typed rows and fingerprints. Transitive dependents are
+identified by their own native loads, not inferred from error text. Healthy local
+packages, other producers, and the existing ordinary compile-failure retention
+policy remain unchanged. Absolute-directory fallback identities must resolve
+physically inside the admitted root before a relative package selection is used.
+
+An incomplete, cancelled or failed inspection names the failure and leaves no
+completed CUE pass stamp, so unchanged input is retried. Some old rows may remain
+after such an incomplete inspection; do not interpret it as a complete invalidation
+or a current typed proof. The native loader itself has no cancellation API;
+cancellation is checked between its finite per-package invocations. Ordinary full
+ingest updates the store watermark, and MCP ingest/refresh evicts the existing
+service graph memos. Direct calls to `EnrichCUEEdges` write the store only; callers
+that hold their own graph snapshots must refresh those snapshots themselves.

+# Native compiler calibration migration
+
+`indexbench lang-unity-asmdef -project ROOT -oracle RECEIPT.json` compares declared `.asmdef` names, references, explicit flags and source ownership against an independently retained CompilationPipeline receipt. Exit 0 requires a complete passing comparison, 1 reports counterexamples/unjudged facts, and 2 names argument/schema/operational failure. The command opens no store and launches no Editor. GUID references and `.asmref` ownership stay unjudged. Available SDK references, emitted dependencies and runtime calls remain distinct evidence.
+
+Native Roslyn `project-declarations` and `project-imports` use the explicit actual project/solution and emission selector described in the [oracle guide](../../calibration/oracles/roslyn/README.md). They do not sandbox MSBuild dependency reads or guarantee no network. Use trusted, independently provisioned projects. Raw declarations/imports are not neutral scoring input or whole-language grades. PE-to-selected-source associations remain unsupported/UNKNOWN with zero invented source targets.
+
+Both native project modes retain error diagnostics in ordinal rendered-string order per project, including duplicates. Preserve old raw outputs and the historical old/new failure. Refresh pins only from newly executed exports; never normalize away a compatibility difference. Strict new/new repeat controls remain required.
+
+`lang-oracle -imports-from tool` needs actual SCIP input and exactly one tool imports array. Declaration-membership truth grades the import-statement family only; SCIP retains dependency/typed families. Default import selection is unchanged. `-scip-defs` now exits 2 before subject/output work when the manifest has no scoreable SCIP definition kinds; use native neutral definitions separately when supported.
+
+The new dialect participates in the existing embedded-data digest and an append-only epoch note. Re-ingest under the new binary before relying on its extraction. Fixtures, source authoring and stale historical receipts do not qualify an adopter or establish L4 support. Native loaded-test-assembly MVID comparison remains outside the validator, as the [native evidence migration](unreleased-native-unity-evidence.md) states.

+# Native source contracts migration
+
+The experimental [`unity-references`](../usage/unity-references.md) command and client methods `PrepareUnityAssetReferences` / `UnityAssetReferences` require an explicit registered service, project, family, immutable receipt and active marker, trusted Editor identity/target, and an exact persistent GUID plus signed64 decimal fileID text. The store is mounted read-only. A prepared DTO cannot authorize a later query; source/context/active generation are checked again. No Editor command, asset payload write, new SQLite family table, MCP tool or runtime code call is introduced.
+
+Asset context/v2 includes all Assets metadata, including opaque Vendor/ThirdParty/folder/importer metadata, plus declared code/config context and ProjectSettings under the original bounds. V1 cannot authorize a current positive query. Grouped locations/properties remain unpaired; partial/native-only/raw-only/package-unbound counts and limitations remain visible. A real new v2 cohort and exact migrated-source qualification remain required; historical failures are not restamped.
+
+C# test candidates require recognized NUnit/Unity attribute syntax rather than an unannotated `Test` method name. Lifecycle hooks, unrelated qualified attributes and strings are excluded. This syntax does not prove framework binding, runner discovery or execution. The upstream non-Go repository convention path remains intact. Native runtime evidence still requires the separate typed/source-bound whole-cohort adapter and remains informational.
+
+Symbol navigation counts distinct canonical keys for ambiguity while retaining repeated source declarations as bounded sorted locations and one deterministic primary definition. This is not typed partial-class merging. Conservation labels the actual stored C# edge source; it does not establish a language grade. Unsupported scip-typescript anonymous object properties remain unmapped, preserving legitimate class/member and other-producer joins.
+
+The native loaded-test-assembly-to-compiler MVID limit is unchanged. See [native evidence](unreleased-native-unity-evidence.md) and [calibration](unreleased-native-calibration.md) migration boundaries. Full generated documentation, ordinary validation and adopter qualification remain separate from source authoring.

+# Native Unity evidence migration
+
+Native admission is explicit: pass `tests ingest --manifest ROOT --unity-nunit XML --unity-receipt ACTIVE_RECEIPT`. The two native flags must appear together and cannot be combined with `--results`. The producer must emit the standard test-kit record and bind it in the source-bound active receipt. Historical XML without that record is not execution evidence. See the [producer contract](../guides/unity-nunit-evidence.md).
+
+Generic bare JSON and DSSE envelopes declaring `env.runnerClass` as Unity (case-insensitive), or artifacts named `unity-nunit-xml` or `unity-source-inputs`, require that adapter. They cannot fall back to generic file/name joins. Other generic envelopes retain upstream joining and unmatched-case reporting. Declarations are not authenticated producer identity.
+
+Native source inventories, command, Editor, XML, envelope, declared build/reference byte-hash closure and optional SCIP source receipt must agree with actual current inputs. Only exact unique typed method identities join. Missing identities, filtered runs and ambiguous definitions remain unjoined. A clipped display signature requires the bounded current full-header read; unreadable or unsupported policy never proves a full cohort.
+
+Store Format v0 gains additive native provenance and protected symbol-key columns. Native cases are isolated from old readers that would otherwise choose a passing parameterized leaf. Conflicting native run-ID replay refuses; read-only legacy evidence remains readable without requiring the new columns.
+
+Runtime reads revalidate the active receipt and current closure, aggregate the complete method cohort and return named UNKNOWN on freshness refusal. They remain informational and do not promote native observations to live clean-commit certificates. This contract does not execute Unity, establish a language-support grade or qualify an adopting repository.
+
+The native validator does not parse or compare NUnit-loaded test-assembly MVIDs against a compiler/assembly oracle. Declared reference hashes and source-bound SCIP definitions do not establish that loaded-assembly identity. Preserve separately observed producer/oracle facts without claiming this validator proves their MVID relationship.

+# Unreleased: source-bound SCIP imports
+
+Existing `scip-dotnet` imports now require a source receipt. An older index
+without one is refused rather than reused as current typed evidence. Other
+producers keep their existing behavior unless a sidecar opts the index in.
+
+Before upgrading a service that imports C# SCIP, use a fresh store or explicitly
+rebuild the affected service. Older stores did not retain each index's producer
+identity, so missing pre-upgrade artifacts cannot retroactively become
+source-bound. Update the local producer
+runner to publish `INDEX.scip.receipt.json` using the
+[source receipt contract](../guides/scip-source-receipts.md). Regenerate the
+index against the actual project, source inventory, compiler configuration,
+reference assemblies and pinned producer package. Do not manufacture fresh
+hashes around an old index.
+
+Use the configured state directory for new `scip/` outputs. Existing
+`.fathom/scip/` files remain readable only when a same-named state-directory
+index does not shadow them. A shadowed remembered index loses its derived typed
+rows; neither artifact is removed. A failed preferred index is a refusal, not
+permission to reuse the legacy copy.
+
+The runner must mark the receipt `started` before generation and publish
+`complete` last. Ingest or refresh the service after generation. A refusal is
+an error and clears that index's previous typed rows and graph memo; unrelated
+typed indexes are preserved. Fix the named input or rerun the producer before
+retrying. Syntax updates alone do not make a refused typed import successful.
+
+Receipt checks run at import and refresh boundaries, including daemon and
+file refresh. They do not continuously monitor disk or attest test execution.

+# Unreleased minor: explicit trace decision sources
+
+This opt-in compatibility-surface change requires a minor release under the
+pre-1.0 policy. It does not change the standard mapping CUE schema or promote
+any decision cell to a certificate, runtime result or compliance approval.
+
+Existing invocations and packs need no migration. Omitting `--decision-source`
+retains `ADR.md` plus `docs/intent/invariants.md`, the legacy citation parser,
+named unread inputs and byte-compatible output. The new `decision_sources`
+field is omitted in that mode.
+
+For project-routed records, use repeatable selectors on export:
+
+```sh
+fathom trace export --standard example --out workspace/evidence-pack \
+  --decision-source INTENT.md --decision-source docs/adr
+```
+
+These replace the legacy inputs. Each selector is a literal committed
+Markdown file or directory, relative to the repository. The pack records the
+canonical selectors and digests of their selected files. Missing/unsafe inputs
+or limit overflow refuse before output is created; see `docs/usage/trace.md`
+for the exact limits and path rules.
+
+Explicit mode recognizes real Markdown heading/table declarations and exact
+citation forms: `ADR0001`, `ADR 0001` and `ADR-0001` are distinct IDs. Numbered
+intent prose does not create named invariants. Code examples and filenames
+are not declarations. Cells remain cited/unproven using the existing matrix
+join and proof tiers.
+
+Use an updated binary to verify an explicit-source pack. Verify re-expands its
+recorded selectors at `COMMIT`; later commits, dirty files and command-line
+overrides cannot substitute decision sources. Older export binaries reject
+the new flag, and older verifiers cannot reproduce the new readings field
+byte-for-byte. Store readings remain live as before: use the store indexed at
+the pack's commit. Preserve original packs instead of refreshing their hashes.
+
+This is local deterministic provenance, not a signature or a defense against
+a writer reconstructing an entire unsigned pack. No model/provider site or
+source egress is added.

+Explicit selectors replace `ADR.md` and `docs/intent/invariants.md`; they do
+not add to those defaults. Paths are literal, repository-relative Git paths,
+never globs. Harmless `./` and trailing slashes are canonicalized, selectors
+are sorted/deduplicated, and overlapping file sets are read/digested once.
+Every selector must name a Markdown file or a directory containing Markdown
+at the resolved `COMMIT`. Current files, untracked additions and later commits
+cannot change that expansion. Missing/non-Markdown inputs, traversal,
+absolute/backslash/control paths, and selected trees containing symlinks or
+gitlinks refuse before a pack is written.
+
+The limits are 16 distinct selectors, 256 Markdown files, 1 MiB per file,
+8 MiB total content, 1 MiB Git tree metadata and 4,096 bytes per path.
+Directory selection reads lowercase `.md` files only. Explicit mode recognizes
+real Markdown ADR headings such as `# ADR0001`, `# ADR 0001`, and
+`## ADR-001`, plus explicit invariant IDs in a table's first column. IDs keep
+their exact case, punctuation, spacing and number width. Numbered prose does
+not create `I1`; fenced/indented examples and filenames declare no IDs.
+Decision cells remain cited or unproven, never compliance or execution proof.
+
+Reverification consumes `decision_sources` from the pack and re-reads at its
+`COMMIT`; `trace verify` accepts no selector override. Omit the export flag to
+keep legacy paths, parser, missing-source disclosures and pack bytes. This is
+deterministic local provenance, not authenticated signing: a completely
+reconstructed unsigned pack is not tamper-proof.

+# Explicit Unity asset-reference reader
+
+`fathom unity-references` answers one-hop persistent object-reference questions
+from a genuinely produced current partial family. It mounts the selected existing
+service store read-only, uses its registered ServiceMeta root and revalidates the
+producer receipt, active generation, raw/native hashes, authored source/context
+membership and bytes on every query. It creates no database, registration,
+snapshot table or cached current authority. Immutable producer run directories
+retain history; the active marker selects current authority.
+
+```sh
+fathom unity-references --store workspace/db/fathom.sqlite --service example \
+  --project game/Example --family cart \
+  --receipt .artifacts/unity-references/runs/cart/run-02/receipt.json \
+  --active .artifacts/unity-references/active/game/Example/cart.json \
+  --editor-version 6000.3.15f1 --editor-sha256 <trusted-local-editor-sha256> \
+  --target StandaloneOSX --guid <exact-guid> --file-id 9007199254740993 \
+  --direction inbound --limit 25 --json
+```
+
+There is no `--root` override or automatic acceptance of receipt-selected Editor
+pins. Required trusted Editor identity/target values come from the operator's
+selected toolchain. All receipt paths are service-relative. GUID plus canonical
+signed64 decimal-string fileID identifies an object, including imported
+subassets; no name/text search, float conversion or transitive traversal is used.
+Direction is `inbound` (default) or `outbound`; limit0 selects25 and the maximum
+is100 groups. `--json` is a standard boolean flag (`--json=false` selects text).
+
+The complete compact JSON response is at most16KiB and has no additional newline
+beyond that budget. Whole groups may be elided: `total` and `truncated` preserve
+the denominator. Text includes bound source/target paths, exact IDs, group counts,
+receipt/source/context identities and partial limits. A refused, stale,
+incomplete, mismatched, cancelled or overbudget read exits nonzero and prints no
+positive response to stdout. A current empty query is an empty selected cohort,
+not proof that no Unity object references exist elsewhere.
+
+Raw declaration locations and native property lists are grouped by persistent
+identity tuple and remain unpaired where equal-target occurrences collide.
+Unbound package targets and native-only properties remain explicit gaps. This
+is separate asset provenance: no typed code calls, callback/scene execution,
+runtime test certification, art approval or excellent language grade follows.
+Complete external package/tool-bundle semantics and interactive Editor state
+remain unproven. A new started attempt invalidates the previous current family;
+historical receipts are never restamped into current evidence.
+
+The required semantic context schema is `fathom.unity.asset-context/v2`.
+Its historical `assets_code` field now binds every Assets `.meta` file, including
+Vendor/ThirdParty, folder and importer metadata, in addition to `.cs`, `.asmdef`,
+`.asmref` and `.rsp` files. These inputs remain opaque hashes; they do not expand
+the parsed asset catalog. All ProjectSettings files are also bound. The existing
+8MiB per-file and 64MiB combined bounds remain unchanged. V1 context receipts
+remain historical and refuse positive current queries: produce a genuinely new
+v2 native run rather than changing a receipt's schema or hashes.
+
+The Go client methods `PrepareUnityAssetReferences` and `UnityAssetReferences`
+have the same registered-root and source-current checks. A caller-supplied
+prepared DTO cannot bypass them. This initial explicit reader adds no SQLite
+tables and no MCP tool or mode; opt-in integration of an existing references
+surface is a later separately reviewed compatibility change.
+
+A migrated implementation or authored fixture does not qualify a current v2 producer cohort. Retain historical v1 failures and all input bindings. Review and execute the exact migrated source against a genuinely produced v2 receipt before claiming the adopting repository’s vendor/importer metadata freshness is covered. This reader does not validate native test-assembly MVID relationships.

 ## The `fathom verify` gate (done-means-proven)
 
+Default daemon `verify` and `plans status` close a bounded current-source
+window before publishing current reference verdicts. Their JSON labels that
+completed observation `current_worktree_freshness: observed_window`. Console
+plan sections are cached without that lifecycle and explicitly label freshness
+`unknown`; their plan counts, criteria and provenance retain verb parity.
+When the window refuses, JSON mode returns one operational refusal with exit 2,
+the reason and no plan rows. Re-ingest and start a new window to recover.
+
 `fathom verify` reads plan files in `docs/plans/*.md` and checks every `[x]`-marked checkbox against the index. A `[x]` line is a *claim* — the task is declared done. The gate verifies each claim has code evidence; unclaimed (`[ ]`) lines are skipped.
 
 **Checkbox semantics:** Annotate a line with `{symbol: Foo}` to name what should exist; add `[US-042]` for spec coverage; add `{reachable_from: Bar}` to require a test edge. An unannotated `[x]` line verifies as `no-contract` (honest, not a false pass).

+package callgraph
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"reflect"
+	"runtime"
+	"sort"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/core"

+// Frozen original buildIndexes. This reference must allocate each map once,
+// including on the baseline arm, so the allocation RED cannot be circular.
+func h3ReservedIndexes(nodes []core.SymbolNode) *Graph {
+	g := &Graph{
+		nodes:     make(map[string]core.SymbolNode, len(nodes)),
+		callees:   make(map[string][]string, len(nodes)),
+		callers:   make(map[string][]string, len(nodes)),
+		byName:    make(map[string]string),
+		byPkgName: make(map[string]string),
+		byDirName: make(map[string]string),
+		byNameAll: make(map[string][]string),
+	}
+
+	// First pass: register all nodes (g.nodes dedupes identical SymbolKeys)
+	// and build the byName / byPkgName indexes. The ambiguity counts MUST be
+	// computed over the deduplicated key set, not the raw slice: duplicate
+	// observations of the same symbol (e.g. stale worktree copies indexed
+	// more than once) would otherwise make a genuinely unique name look
+	// ambiguous and silently drop its cross-package call edges.
+	for _, n := range nodes {
+		g.nodes[n.Key()] = n
+	}
+	nameCounts := make(map[string]int, len(g.nodes))
+	pkgNameCounts := make(map[string]int, len(g.nodes))
+	dirNameCounts := make(map[string]int, len(g.nodes))
+	for _, n := range g.nodes {
+		nameCounts[n.Name]++
+		if n.Package != "" {
+			pkgNameCounts[n.Package+"."+n.Name]++
+		}
+		if dn := dirName(n); dn != "" {
+			dirNameCounts[dn]++
+		}
+	}
+	for _, n := range g.nodes {
+		key := n.Key()
+		g.byNameAll[n.Name] = append(g.byNameAll[n.Name], key)
+		if nameCounts[n.Name] == 1 {
+			g.byName[n.Name] = key
+		}
+		if n.Package != "" && pkgNameCounts[n.Package+"."+n.Name] == 1 {
+			g.byPkgName[n.Package+"."+n.Name] = key
+		}
+		if dn := dirName(n); dn != "" && dirNameCounts[dn] == 1 {
+			g.byDirName[dn] = key
+		}
+	}
+	for k := range g.byNameAll {
+		sort.Strings(g.byNameAll[k])
+	}
+
+	return g
+}
+
+func h3Build(mode string, nodes []core.SymbolNode, typed []core.Edge) *Graph {
+	switch mode {
+	case "both":
+		return BuildBoth(nodes, typed)
+	case "resolved":
+		return BuildResolved(nodes, typed)
+	default:
+		return Build(nodes)
+	}
+}
+
+// Baseline Build's edge pass, with reserved adjacency restored before any
+// insertion. Duplicates and sorting follow the original production algorithm.
+func h3ReservedBuild(mode string, nodes []core.SymbolNode, typed []core.Edge) *Graph {
+	g := h3ReservedIndexes(nodes)
+	if mode != "resolved" {
+		g.buildSuffixIndex()
+		for callerKey, n := range g.nodes {
+			seen := make(map[string]struct{})
+			for _, raw := range n.Calls {
+				calleeKey := g.resolve(n, raw)
+				if calleeKey == "" {
+					continue
+				}
+				if _, duplicate := seen[calleeKey]; duplicate {
+					continue
+				}
+				seen[calleeKey] = struct{}{}
+				g.callees[callerKey] = append(g.callees[callerKey], calleeKey)
+				g.callers[calleeKey] = append(g.callers[calleeKey], callerKey)
+			}
+		}
+		for k := range g.callees {
+			sort.Strings(g.callees[k])
+		}
+		for k := range g.callers {
+			sort.Strings(g.callers[k])
+		}
+	}
+	if mode == "resolved" {
+		resolved := make([]core.Edge, 0, len(typed))
+		for _, e := range typed {
+			if core.EdgeConfidenceOf(e) == core.EdgeConfidenceResolved {
+				resolved = append(resolved, e)
+			}
+		}
+		AddTypedEdges(g, resolved)
+	} else if mode == "both" && len(typed) > 0 {
+		AddTypedEdges(g, typed)
+	}
+	return g
+}
+
+func h3AssertEqual(t *testing.T, got, want *Graph) {
+	t.Helper()
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
+		t.Fatalf("graph contents changed: nodes %d/%d edges %d/%d", got.NodeCount(), want.NodeCount(), got.EdgeCount(), want.EdgeCount())
+	}
+	queries := []string{"missing", "Beta", "Run", "dep.Service.Run", "Entry"}
+	for key := range want.nodes {
+		queries = append(queries, key)
+	}
+	sort.Strings(queries)
+	for _, query := range queries {
+		if !reflect.DeepEqual(CandidateKeys(got, query), CandidateKeys(want, query)) ||
+			Canonical(got, query) != Canonical(want, query) ||
+			!reflect.DeepEqual(CallersDetail(got, query), CallersDetail(want, query)) ||
+			!reflect.DeepEqual(CalleesDetail(got, query), CalleesDetail(want, query)) {
+			t.Fatalf("public query changed for %q", query)
+		}
+		for _, target := range queries {
+			if Reachable(got, query, target) != Reachable(want, query, target) ||
+				!reflect.DeepEqual(CallPath(got, query, target), CallPath(want, query, target)) {
+				t.Fatalf("reachability/order changed for %q -> %q", query, target)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func h3Freeze(g *Graph) *Graph {
+	s := *g
+	s.nodes = cloneNodes(g.nodes)
+	for k, n := range s.nodes {
+		if n.Calls != nil {
+			n.Calls = append(make([]string, 0, len(n.Calls)), n.Calls...)
+			s.nodes[k] = n
+		}
+	}
+	s.callees, s.callers = cloneAdjacency(g.callees), cloneAdjacency(g.callers)
+	s.byName, s.byPkgName, s.byDirName = cloneStrMap(g.byName), cloneStrMap(g.byPkgName), cloneStrMap(g.byDirName)
+	s.byNameAll = cloneAdjacency(g.byNameAll)
+	if g.bySuffix != nil {
+		s.bySuffix = make(map[string]suffixCandidate)
+		for k, v := range g.bySuffix {
+			s.bySuffix[k] = v
+		}
+	}
+	if g.byDotSuffix != nil {
+		s.byDotSuffix = make(map[string]suffixCandidate)
+		for k, v := range g.byDotSuffix {
+			s.byDotSuffix[k] = v
+		}
+	}
+	s.edgeKind = cloneEdgeKindMap(g.edgeKind)
+	if g.dispatchOut != nil {
+		s.dispatchOut = cloneIntMap(g.dispatchOut)
+	}
+	if g.instantiates != nil {
+		s.instantiates = cloneAdjacency(g.instantiates)
+	}
+	s.typedFiles, s.typedDirs = cloneBoolMap(g.typedFiles), cloneBoolMap(g.typedDirs)
+	return &s
+}
+
+func TestAdjacencyCapacitySemantics(t *testing.T) {
+	nodes := []core.SymbolNode{
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "app", Name: "Entry", FilePath: "app/entry.go", Kind: core.KindGoFunc},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "app", Name: "Alpha", FilePath: "app/alpha.go", Kind: core.KindGoFunc},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "one", Name: "Beta", FilePath: "one/beta.go", Kind: core.KindGoFunc},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "two", Name: "Beta", FilePath: "two/beta.go", Kind: core.KindGoFunc},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "dep", Name: "Service.Run", FilePath: "dep/service.go", Kind: core.KindGoMethod},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "data", Name: "Sink", FilePath: "data/config.json", Kind: core.KindJSONKey},
+	}
+	entry, alpha, sink := nodes[0].Key(), nodes[1].Key(), nodes[5].Key()
+	nodes[0].Calls = []string{alpha, alpha, "Beta", "recv.Run", "unknown"}
+	nodes[1].Calls = []string{entry}
+	typed := []core.Edge{
+		{FromService: "fixture", FromFile: nodes[0].FilePath, FromSymbol: entry, ToSymbol: sink, Kind: core.EdgeDirect},
+		{FromService: "fixture", FromFile: nodes[0].FilePath, FromSymbol: entry, ToSymbol: sink, Kind: core.EdgeDirect},
+	}
+	for _, mode := range []string{"syntax", "both", "resolved"} {
+		t.Run(mode, func(t *testing.T) {
+			g, old := h3Build(mode, nodes, typed), h3ReservedBuild(mode, nodes, typed)
+			h3AssertEqual(t, g, old)
+			if g.NodeCount() != 6 || Canonical(g, "Beta") != "" || len(CandidateKeys(g, "Beta")) != 2 {
+				t.Fatal("node universe or ambiguity changed")
+			}
+			if mode != "resolved" && (!reflect.DeepEqual(g.callers[alpha], []string{entry}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(g.callees[alpha], []string{entry})) {
+				t.Fatal("caller/callee orientation or duplicate edge changed")
+			}
+			if mode != "syntax" && !reflect.DeepEqual(g.callers[sink], []string{entry}) {
+				t.Fatal("duplicate typed edge was not represented once")
+			}
+			if mode == "syntax" && !containsStr(g.callees[entry], nodes[4].Key()) || mode == "both" && containsStr(g.callees[entry], nodes[4].Key()) {
+				t.Fatal("typed-file method-guess suppression changed")
+			}
+			t.Logf("initial mode=%s nodes=%d edges=%d", mode, g.NodeCount(), g.EdgeCount())
+			reversed := append([]core.SymbolNode(nil), nodes...)
+			for i, j := 0, len(reversed)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
+				reversed[i], reversed[j] = reversed[j], reversed[i]
+			}
+			h3AssertEqual(t, h3Build(mode, reversed, typed), old)
+
+			// Build is last-wins for duplicate keys, including differing Calls.
+			duplicate := nodes[0]
+			duplicate.Calls = []string{sink, sink}
+			dups := append(append([]core.SymbolNode(nil), nodes...), duplicate)
+			duplicateGraph := h3Build(mode, dups, typed)
+			h3AssertEqual(t, duplicateGraph, h3ReservedBuild(mode, dups, typed))
+			if !reflect.DeepEqual(duplicateGraph.callees[entry], []string{sink}) {
+				t.Fatal("duplicate caller must retain last-wins Calls and one sink edge")
+			}
+			beforeTypedOnly := h3Freeze(g)
+			h3AssertEqual(t, g.ReplacePackage("app", nil, nil), old.ReplacePackage("app", nil, nil))
+			h3AssertEqual(t, g, beforeTypedOnly)
+
+			// Replacement retains its separate raw-entry semantics. It may
+			// append to initially empty maps and must never mutate old holders.
+			fresh := core.SymbolNode{Service: "fixture", Package: "app", Name: "Fresh", FilePath: "app/fresh.go", Kind: core.KindGoFunc}
+			first := nodes[0]
+			first.Calls = []string{sink}
+			last := nodes[0]
+			last.Calls = []string{fresh.Key()}
+			replacements := [][]core.SymbolNode{{first, last, fresh}, {}, {first, fresh}}
+			for step, replacement := range replacements {
+				before := h3Freeze(g)
+				gNext := g.ReplacePackage("app", replacement, []core.Edge{})
+				oldNext := old.ReplacePackage("app", replacement, []core.Edge{})
+				h3AssertEqual(t, gNext, oldNext)
+				h3AssertEqual(t, g, before)
+				if step == 0 {
+					want := []string{sink, fresh.Key()}
+					sort.Strings(want)
+					if !reflect.DeepEqual(gNext.callees[entry], want) {
+						t.Fatal("replacement raw duplicate callers lost an edge")
+					}
+				}
+				if step == 1 && (gNext.EdgeCount() != 0 || len(gNext.callers[alpha]) != 0 || len(gNext.callees[entry]) != 0) {
+					t.Fatal("package removal left outgoing or reverse edges")
+				}
+				t.Logf("replacement mode=%s step=%d nodes=%d edges=%d", mode, step, gNext.NodeCount(), gNext.EdgeCount())
+				g, old = gNext, oldNext
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+func TestAdjacencyCapacityEmptyAndTypedInsertion(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, mode := range []string{"syntax", "both", "resolved"} {
+		h3AssertEqual(t, h3Build(mode, nil, nil), h3ReservedBuild(mode, nil, nil))
+	}
+	nodes := []core.SymbolNode{
+		{Service: "fixture", Name: "A", Kind: core.KindGoFunc},
+		{Service: "fixture", Name: "B", Kind: core.KindGoFunc},
+	}
+	g := BuildResolved(nodes, nil)
+	if g.callees == nil || g.callers == nil || g.HasEdges() {
+		t.Fatal("empty adjacency must remain writable")
+	}
+	edge := core.Edge{FromSymbol: nodes[0].Key(), ToSymbol: nodes[1].Key(), Kind: core.EdgeDirect}
+	AddTypedEdges(g, []core.Edge{edge, edge})
+	if g.EdgeCount() != 1 || !reflect.DeepEqual(g.callees[edge.FromSymbol], []string{edge.ToSymbol}) || !reflect.DeepEqual(g.callers[edge.ToSymbol], []string{edge.FromSymbol}) {
+		t.Fatal("typed insertion into empty adjacency changed")
+	}
+	nodes[0].Calls = []string{nodes[1].Key()}
+	empty := Build(nil)
+	added := empty.ReplacePackage("", nodes, []core.Edge{})
+	if empty.NodeCount() != 0 || empty.EdgeCount() != 0 || added.NodeCount() != 2 || added.EdgeCount() != 1 {
+		t.Fatal("package addition to an empty graph changed")
+	}
+}
+
+func h3Workload(n int, dense bool) ([]core.SymbolNode, []core.Edge) {
+	nodes := make([]core.SymbolNode, n)
+	for i := range nodes {
+		nodes[i] = core.SymbolNode{Service: "fixture", Package: "data", Name: fmt.Sprintf("Key%05d", i), FilePath: "data/config.json", Kind: core.KindJSONKey}
+	}
+	var typed []core.Edge
+	for i := range nodes {
+		if !dense && i > 0 {
+			continue
+		}
+		for offset := 1; offset <= 4; offset++ {
+			target := nodes[(i+offset)%n].Key()
+			nodes[i].Calls = append(nodes[i].Calls, target)
+			typed = append(typed, core.Edge{FromService: "fixture", FromSymbol: nodes[i].Key(), ToSymbol: target, Kind: core.EdgeDirect})
+		}
+	}
+	return nodes, typed
+}
+
+func h3Allocated(build func() *Graph) (uint64, int, int) {
+	runtime.GC()
+	var before, after runtime.MemStats
+	runtime.ReadMemStats(&before)
+	g := build()
+	runtime.ReadMemStats(&after)
+	nodes, edges := g.NodeCount(), g.EdgeCount()
+	runtime.KeepAlive(g)
+	return after.TotalAlloc - before.TotalAlloc, nodes, edges
+}
+
+func TestAdjacencyCapacitySparseAllocationBound(t *testing.T) {
+	// Fixed hypothesis: removing only empty adjacency reservations saves
+	// at least512KiB for16384 indexed nodes. Baseline's identical builders
+	// must expose this RED; compile errors and skips cannot qualify.
+	nodes, _ := h3Workload(16384, false)
+	var saved [3]int64
+	for i := range saved {
+		actual, n, e := h3Allocated(func() *Graph { return buildIndexes(nodes) })
+		reserved, rn, re := h3Allocated(func() *Graph { return h3ReservedIndexes(nodes) })
+		if n != 16384 || rn != n || e != 0 || re != 0 {
+			t.Fatal("index allocation workload changed")
+		}
+		saved[i] = int64(reserved) - int64(actual)
+		t.Logf("sample=%d nodes=%d raw_calls=4 indexed_edges=%d production_B=%d reserved_B=%d saved_B=%d", i, n, e, actual, reserved, saved[i])
+	}
+	runtime.KeepAlive(nodes)
+	for _, saving := range saved {
+		if saving < 512<<10 {
+			t.Fatalf("adjacency reservation saving below512KiB: samples=%v", saved)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+var h3BenchmarkSink *Graph
+
+func BenchmarkAdjacencyCapacity(b *testing.B) {
+	for _, dense := range []bool{false, true} {
+		shape := "sparse"
+		if dense {
+			shape = "dense"
+		}
+		nodes, typed := h3Workload(16384, dense)
+		for _, mode := range []string{"syntax", "both", "resolved"} {
+			b.Run(shape+"/"+mode, func(b *testing.B) {
+				b.ReportAllocs()
+				b.ResetTimer()
+				for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
+					h3BenchmarkSink = h3Build(mode, nodes, typed)
+				}
+				b.StopTimer()
+				b.ReportMetric(float64(h3BenchmarkSink.NodeCount()), "nodes/op")
+				b.ReportMetric(float64(h3BenchmarkSink.EdgeCount()), "edges/op")
+				b.ReportMetric(float64(len(typed)), "raw-calls/op")
+			})
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func h3Retained(build func() *Graph) (int64, int, int) {
+	runtime.GC()
+	var before, after runtime.MemStats
+	runtime.ReadMemStats(&before)
+	g := build()
+	runtime.GC()
+	runtime.ReadMemStats(&after)
+	nodes, edges := g.NodeCount(), g.EdgeCount()
+	runtime.KeepAlive(g)
+	return int64(after.HeapAlloc) - int64(before.HeapAlloc), nodes, edges
+}
+
+func TestAdjacencyCapacityRetainedWorkload(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, dense := range []bool{false, true} {
+		nodes, typed := h3Workload(16384, dense)
+		wantEdges := 4
+		if dense {
+			wantEdges = 16384 * 4
+		}
+		for _, mode := range []string{"syntax", "both", "resolved"} {
+			production, n, e := h3Retained(func() *Graph { return h3Build(mode, nodes, typed) })
+			reserved, rn, re := h3Retained(func() *Graph { return h3ReservedBuild(mode, nodes, typed) })
+			if n != 16384 || rn != n || e != wantEdges || re != e {
+				t.Fatal("retained workload changed node/edge corpus")
+			}
+			t.Logf("dense=%t mode=%s nodes=%d edges=%d raw_calls=%d production_retained_HeapAlloc_B=%d reserved_retained_HeapAlloc_B=%d", dense, mode, n, e, len(typed), production, reserved)
+		}
+		runtime.KeepAlive(nodes)
+	}
+}

+// Distinct directories remain distinct identities; repeated observations of
+// one partial type share one identity. Allocation changes must not substitute
+// a bare, namespace-only or file-basename key in any graph's name indexes.
+func TestGraphKeyAllocationPreservesIdentity(t *testing.T) {
+	nodes := []core.SymbolNode{
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "Acme.Tools", Name: "Panel", Kind: core.KindCSharpClass, FilePath: "src/UI/Panel.cs"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "Acme.Tools", Name: "Panel", Kind: core.KindCSharpClass, FilePath: "src/UI/Panel.Partial.cs"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "Acme.Tools", Name: "Panel.Run", Kind: core.KindCSharpMethod, FilePath: "src/UI/Panel.cs"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "Acme.Tools", Name: "Panel", Kind: core.KindCSharpClass, FilePath: "src/Other/Panel.cs"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "root", Name: "Entry", Kind: core.KindGoFunc, FilePath: "entry.go"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "evidencesignature", Name: "Check", Kind: core.KindGoFunc, FilePath: "lib/evidence-signature/check.go"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "tests", Name: "Probe", Kind: core.KindGoFunc, FilePath: "tests/probe.go",
+			Calls: []string{"evidence-signature.Check", "fixture::src/UI/Acme.Tools.Panel.Run"}},
+	}
+	caller := "fixture::tests/tests.Probe"
+	target := "fixture::lib/evidence-signature/evidencesignature.Check"
+	typed := []core.Edge{{FromService: "fixture", FromFile: "tests/probe.go", FromSymbol: caller, ToSymbol: target, Kind: core.EdgeDirect}}
+	for _, mode := range []string{"syntax", "both", "resolved"} {
+		t.Run(mode, func(t *testing.T) {
+			var g *callgraph.Graph
+			switch mode {
+			case "syntax":
+				g = callgraph.Build(nodes)
+			case "both":
+				g = callgraph.BuildBoth(nodes, typed)
+			case "resolved":
+				g = callgraph.BuildResolved(nodes, typed)
+			}
+			if g.NodeCount() != 6 {
+				t.Fatalf("nodes=%d, want six canonical identities", g.NodeCount())
+			}
+			for query, want := range map[string][]string{
+				"Panel":     {"fixture::src/Other/Acme.Tools.Panel", "fixture::src/UI/Acme.Tools.Panel"},
+				"Panel.Run": {"fixture::src/UI/Acme.Tools.Panel.Run"},
+				"Entry":     {"fixture::root.Entry"},
+				"Check":     {target},
+			} {
+				if got := callgraph.CandidateKeys(g, query); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
+					t.Errorf("CandidateKeys(%q)=%v, want %v", query, got, want)
+				}
+			}
+			if !callgraph.Reachable(g, caller, target) {
+				t.Fatal("canonical import alias target lost")
+			}
+			if mode == "resolved" && callgraph.Reachable(g, caller, "fixture::src/UI/Acme.Tools.Panel.Run") {
+				t.Fatal("resolved-only graph acquired a syntax-only edge")
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+func suffixDemandFixture(noise int) []core.SymbolNode {
+	nodes := []core.SymbolNode{
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "api", Name: "TestEntry", Kind: core.KindGoFunc, FilePath: "api/entry.go", Calls: []string{"Tail.Run", "one/One.Tail.Run", "r.Close", "q.Flush", "odd.End", "p.End", "NoSuch", "Tail.Run"}},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "One", Name: "Tail.Run", Kind: core.KindCSharpMethod, FilePath: "root/one/run.cs"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "Two", Name: "Handle.Close", Kind: core.KindGoMethod, FilePath: "two/close.go"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "Three", Name: "Handle.Flush", Kind: core.KindGoMethod, FilePath: "three/flush.go"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "Four", Name: "Other.Flush", Kind: core.KindGoMethod, FilePath: "four/flush.go"},
+		// Nonmethod End contributes to ambiguity too. A kind filter would lie.
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "odd", Name: "End", Kind: core.KindJSONKey, FilePath: "data/end.json"},
+		{Service: "fixture", Package: "Five", Name: "Handle.End", Kind: core.KindGoMethod, FilePath: "five/end.go"},
+	}
+	nodes = append(nodes, nodes[1]) // same canonical identity must count once
+	for i := 0; i < noise; i++ {
+		nodes = append(nodes, core.SymbolNode{Service: "fixture", Package: "Document", Name: fmt.Sprintf("section%d.payload.deep.value%d", i, i), Kind: core.KindJSONKey, FilePath: fmt.Sprintf("data/section%d/document.json", i)})
+	}
+	return nodes
+}

+// Build an independent eager suffix universe, then use the unchanged resolver
+// to compare every adjacency list, including sinks and repeated observations.
+func suffixDemandEagerReference(nodes []core.SymbolNode) *Graph {
+	g := buildIndexes(nodes)
+	g.bySuffix = make(map[string]suffixCandidate)
+	g.byDotSuffix = make(map[string]suffixCandidate)
+	for key := range g.nodes {
+		for i := 1; i < len(key); i++ {
+			if key[i-1] == '.' || key[i-1] == '/' {
+				addSuffixCandidate(g.bySuffix, key[i:], key)
+				if key[i-1] == '.' {
+					addSuffixCandidate(g.byDotSuffix, key[i:], key)
+				}
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	for key, n := range g.nodes {
+		seen := map[string]bool{}
+		for _, raw := range n.Calls {
+			target := g.resolve(n, raw)
+			if target != "" && !seen[target] {
+				seen[target] = true
+				g.callees[key] = append(g.callees[key], target)
+				g.callers[target] = append(g.callers[target], key)
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	for key := range g.callees {
+		sort.Strings(g.callees[key])
+	}
+	for key := range g.callers {
+		sort.Strings(g.callers[key])
+	}
+	return g
+}

+func TestSuffixDemandSemanticEquivalence(t *testing.T) {
+	nodes := suffixDemandFixture(1024)
+	caller, target := nodes[0].Key(), nodes[1].Key()
+	typed := []core.Edge{{FromSymbol: caller, ToSymbol: target, FromFile: nodes[0].FilePath, Kind: core.EdgeDirect}}
+	for _, mode := range []string{"syntax", "both", "resolved"} {
+		t.Run(mode, func(t *testing.T) {
+			want := suffixDemandEagerReference(nodes)
+			var got *Graph
+			switch mode {
+			case "syntax":
+				got = Build(nodes)
+			case "both":
+				got = BuildBoth(nodes, typed)
+				AddTypedEdges(want, typed)
+			case "resolved":
+				got = BuildResolved(nodes, typed)
+				want = buildIndexes(nodes)
+				AddTypedEdges(want, typed)
+			}
+			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.nodes, want.nodes) || !reflect.DeepEqual(got.callees, want.callees) || !reflect.DeepEqual(got.callers, want.callers) {
+				t.Fatal("complete node or adjacency universe differs from eager reference")
+			}
+			wantEdges := 3 // Tail.Run, unique Close, explicit odd.End
+			if mode == "both" {
+				wantEdges = 2
+			} // typed file suppresses syntax-only Go method Close
+			if mode == "resolved" {
+				wantEdges = 1
+			}
+			if got.EdgeCount() != wantEdges || got.NodeCount() != len(nodes)-1 {
+				t.Fatalf("nodes=%d edges=%d", got.NodeCount(), got.EdgeCount())
+			}
+			for _, q := range []string{"Tail.Run", "Handle.Flush", "Document.section999.payload.deep.value999", "payload.deep.value999", "NoSuch"} {
+				if Canonical(got, q) != Canonical(want, q) || !reflect.DeepEqual(CandidateKeys(got, q), CandidateKeys(want, q)) {
+					t.Fatalf("arbitrary public query %q changed", q)
+				}
+			}
+			if mode == "resolved" && (got.bySuffix != nil || got.byDotSuffix != nil) {
+				t.Fatal("resolved build retained syntax suffix indexes")
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+// This intentional baseline-red structural regression exposes the new memory

+func TestSuffixDemandRetainsOnlyQueries(t *testing.T) {

+		}
+	}
+	for suffix := range g.byDotSuffix {
+		if !wantedMethod[suffix] {
+			t.Fatalf("undemanded method suffix retained: %q", suffix)
+		}
+	}
+	if g.bySuffix["Tail.Run"].count != 1 || g.byDotSuffix["Flush"].count != 2 || g.byDotSuffix["End"].count != 2 {
+		t.Fatal("duplicate identity or ambiguity count changed")
+	}

+func TestSuffixDemandPackageNewQueryAndRemoval(t *testing.T) {
+	target := core.SymbolNode{Service: "fixture", Package: "Handlers", Name: "Handle.Execute", Kind: core.KindCSharpMethod, FilePath: "lib/handle.cs"}
+	caller := core.SymbolNode{Service: "fixture", Package: "api", Name: "Entry", Kind: core.KindGoFunc, FilePath: "api/entry.go"}
+	base := Build([]core.SymbolNode{caller, target})
+	caller.Calls = []string{"receiver.Execute"}
+	patched := base.ReplacePackage("api", []core.SymbolNode{caller}, nil)
+	if !Reachable(patched, caller.Key(), target.Key()) {
+		t.Fatal("new method demand failed to scan preexisting noncalling target")
+	}
+	if base.EdgeCount() != 0 {
+		t.Fatal("patch mutated old graph")
+	}
+	// A newly inserted noncalling target can make existing demand ambiguous.
+	duplicate := target
+	duplicate.Package = "api"
+	duplicate.Name = "Other.Execute"
+	duplicate.FilePath = "other/handle.cs"
+	ambiguous := patched.ReplacePackage("api", []core.SymbolNode{caller, duplicate}, nil)
+	if len(CalleesDetail(ambiguous, caller.Key())) != 0 {
+		t.Fatal("new target did not contribute to ambiguity")
+	}
+	// Removing the extra target refreshes the edited caller's edges.
+	// Untouched packages are deliberately not re-resolved.
+	restored := ambiguous.ReplacePackage("api", []core.SymbolNode{caller}, nil)
+	if !Reachable(restored, caller.Key(), target.Key()) {
+		t.Fatal("removed ambiguity survived caller refresh")
+	}
+	caller.Calls = nil
+	noDemand := restored.ReplacePackage("api", []core.SymbolNode{caller}, nil)
+	if noDemand.EdgeCount() != 0 || len(noDemand.bySuffix) != 0 || len(noDemand.byDotSuffix) != 0 {
+		t.Fatal("removed query retained edges or suffix demand")
+	}
+	if !Reachable(patched, caller.Key(), target.Key()) {
+		t.Fatal("subsequent patch mutated previous graph")
+	}
+}

+// ReplacePackage resolves every newNodes entry, even when node membership
+// takes the last observation for a repeated key. Earlier observations'

+func TestSuffixDemandPackageDuplicateCallerCalls(t *testing.T) {

+	suffix := core.SymbolNode{Service: "fixture", Package: "Odd", Name: "Layer.Run", Kind: core.KindCSharpMethod, FilePath: "src/lib/odd.cs"}

+	exact := core.SymbolNode{Service: "fixture", Package: "helpers", Name: "Exact", Kind: core.KindGoFunc, FilePath: "helpers/exact.go"}
+	named := core.SymbolNode{Service: "fixture", Package: "helpers", Name: "Named", Kind: core.KindGoFunc, FilePath: "helpers/named.go"}
+	original := Build([]core.SymbolNode{caller, suffix, method, exact, named})
+	before := CalleesDetail(original, caller.Key())

+	later := caller
+	later.Calls = []string{"Named"}

+	want := []string{suffix.Key(), method.Key(), exact.Key(), named.Key()}

+		got = append(got, edge.Key)
+	}

+		t.Fatalf("duplicate caller's suffix/method/exact/name union=%v, want %v", got, want)
+	}

+			t.Fatalf("CallersDetail(%q)=%v", target, got)
+		}
+	}
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(patched.nodes[caller.Key()].Calls, later.Calls) {
+		t.Fatal("replacement node stopped taking the last observation")
+	}
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(CalleesDetail(original, caller.Key()), before) || original.EdgeCount() != 1 || original.NodeCount() != 5 || !reflect.DeepEqual(original.nodes[caller.Key()].Calls, caller.Calls) {
+		t.Fatal("duplicate replacement mutated held original graph")
+	}

+// A partial type has multiple source declarations, but only one canonical
+// navigation key. Exercise the real dialect, not only hand-made symbol rows.
+func TestResolveTieredCSharpPartialTypeFromSource(t *testing.T) {
+	e, err := extractor.NewTSExtractor("csharp")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	defer e.Close()
+	var nodes []core.SymbolNode
+	for _, file := range []string{"UI.cs", "Preview.cs", "Panel.cs"} {
+		part, err := e.Extract("svc", "Editor/"+file, []byte("namespace Workshop { public partial class Panel { } }"))
+		if err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		nodes = append(nodes, part...)
+	}
+	key := "svc::Editor/Workshop.Panel"
+	for _, query := range []string{"Panel", "Workshop.Panel", "svc::Workshop.Panel", key} {
+		got, candidates, ok := symbolnav.ResolveTiered(nodes, query)
+		if !ok || got != key || len(candidates) != 1 {
+			t.Errorf("query %q = (%q, %v, %v), want one canonical key %q", query, got, candidates, ok, key)
+		} else if candidates[0].FilePath != "Editor/Panel.cs" {
+			t.Errorf("query %q chooses %s, want deterministic Editor/Panel.cs", query, candidates[0].FilePath)
+		}
+	}
+	before := append([]core.SymbolNode(nil), nodes...)
+	ctx := symbolnav.SymbolContext(nodes, callgraph.Build(nodes), "Panel")
+	if ctx.Def.FilePath != "Editor/Panel.cs" {
+		t.Errorf("definition = %v", ctx.Def)
+	}
+	if len(ctx.Definitions) != 3 {
+		t.Fatalf("source declarations = %v, want all three locations", ctx.Definitions)
+	}
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(nodes, before) {
+		t.Fatal("navigation mutated extractor output")
+	}
+	for i, j := 0, len(nodes)-1; i < j; i, j = i+1, j-1 {
+		nodes[i], nodes[j] = nodes[j], nodes[i]
+	}
+	// Repeated input rows are not an additional source declaration, and input
+	// order does not choose the primary snippet or reorder the locations.
+	nodes = append(nodes, nodes...)
+	got := symbolnav.SymbolContext(nodes, callgraph.Build(nodes), key)
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(ctx, got) {
+		t.Fatalf("reversed/duplicate rows change context:\n%v\n%v", ctx, got)
+	}
+}

+// distinctSymbolCandidates counts identities, not source parts or ingest
+// order. It never mutates the caller's node slice.
+func distinctSymbolCandidates(nodes []core.SymbolNode) []core.SymbolNode {
+	byKey := make(map[string]core.SymbolNode, len(nodes))
+	for _, n := range nodes {
+		k := n.Key()
+		if old, ok := byKey[k]; !ok || definitionLess(n, old) {
+			byKey[k] = n
+		}
+	}
+	var out []core.SymbolNode
+	for _, n := range byKey {
+		out = append(out, n)
+	}
+	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].Key() < out[j].Key() })
+	return out
+}
+
+func definitionLess(a, b core.SymbolNode) bool {
+	if a.FilePath != b.FilePath {
+		return a.FilePath < b.FilePath
+	}
+	if a.Line != b.Line {
+		return a.Line < b.Line
+	}
+	if a.EndLine != b.EndLine {
+		return a.EndLine < b.EndLine
+	}
+	if a.Kind != b.Kind {
+		return a.Kind < b.Kind
+	}
+	return a.Signature < b.Signature
+}

+package assetrefs

+const ContextSchema = "fathom.unity.asset-context/v2"
+
+func checkSourceMemberCount(raw, assets, settings int) error {
+	remaining := memberLimit
+	for _, count := range []int{raw, assets, settings} {
+		if count < 0 || count > remaining {
+			return refused("combined source/context membership exceeds50000")
+		}
+		remaining -= count
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func authoredContextPath(p string) bool {
+	if !relative(p) || !strings.HasPrefix(p, "Assets/") {
+		return false
+	}
+	switch strings.ToLower(path.Ext(p)) {
+	case ".cs", ".asmdef", ".asmref", ".rsp", ".meta":
+		return true
+	}
+	return false
+}
+func settingsContextPath(p string) bool {
+	return relative(p) && strings.HasPrefix(p, "ProjectSettings/")
+}
+
+func contextBytes(c contextInventory) []byte {
+	files := append([]fileHash(nil), c.AssetsCode...)
+	files = append(files, c.ProjectSettings...)
+	slices.SortFunc(files, func(a, b fileHash) int { return strings.Compare(a.Path, b.Path) })
+	var b strings.Builder
+	b.WriteString(ContextSchema + "\n")
+	for _, file := range files {
+		b.WriteString("file\x00" + file.Path + "\x00" + file.SHA256 + "\n")
+	}
+	return []byte(b.String())
+}
+
+// Context discovery does not inherit the asset parser's vendor exclusion.
+// Vendor/ThirdParty source and all Assets metadata may change local type/GUID
+// or importer identity. These bytes are opaque semantic context, never parsed,
+// catalogued or exposed as code by this pass.
+func contextMembers(ctx context.Context, projectRoot, tree string) ([]string, error) {
+	var result []string
+	governor := tenancy.NewRowGovernor(ctx, tenancy.ClassTree)
+	err := filepath.WalkDir(filepath.Join(projectRoot, tree), func(p string, entry fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
+		if walkErr != nil {
+			return walkErr
+		}
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		rel, err := filepath.Rel(projectRoot, p)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		rel = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
+		if entry.Type()&fs.ModeSymlink != 0 {
+			return refused("symlink semantic context %s", rel)
+		}
+		if entry.IsDir() {
+			return nil
+		}
+		if tree == "Assets" && !authoredContextPath(rel) {
+			return nil
+		}
+		if !entry.Type().IsRegular() || !relative(rel) {
+			return refused("unsafe/nonregular semantic context %s", rel)
+		}
+		result = append(result, rel)
+		if len(result) > memberLimit {
+			return refused("semantic context membership exceeds bound")
+		}
+		return nil
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: semantic context discovery: %w", ErrRefused, err)
+	}
+	slices.Sort(result)
+	return result, nil
+}
+
+func validateContext(ctx context.Context, projectRoot string, c *contextInventory, alreadyRead int) error {
+	if c == nil || c.Schema != ContextSchema || !shaPattern.MatchString(c.Before) || c.Before != c.After || digest(contextBytes(*c)) != c.Before || len(c.AssetsCode)+len(c.ProjectSettings) > memberLimit || len(c.ProjectSettings) == 0 {
+		return refused("missing/incomplete semantic context inventory")
+	}
+	sets := []struct {
+		root  string
+		files []fileHash
+		allow func(string) bool
+	}{{"Assets", c.AssetsCode, authoredContextPath}, {"ProjectSettings", c.ProjectSettings, settingsContextPath}}
+	governor := tenancy.NewRowGovernor(ctx, tenancy.ClassTree)
+	total := alreadyRead
+	for _, set := range sets {
+		paths := make([]string, 0, len(set.files))
+		last := ""
+		for _, file := range set.files {
+			if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+			if !set.allow(file.Path) || file.Path <= last || !shaPattern.MatchString(file.SHA256) {
+				return refused("duplicate/unsafe/unsorted semantic input")
+			}
+			last = file.Path
+			paths = append(paths, file.Path)
+			raw, err := readHash(ctx, projectRoot, file, inputLimit)
+			if err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+			total += len(raw)
+			if total > sourceLimit {
+				return refused("combined asset/tool/context source closure exceeds64MiB")
+			}
+		}
+		actual, err := contextMembers(ctx, projectRoot, set.root)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if !slices.Equal(actual, paths) {
+			return refused("stale semantic context membership")
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}

+const artifactLimit = 16 << 20
+const inputLimit = 8 << 20
+const sourceLimit = 64 << 20
+const memberLimit = 50000
+const entityLimit = 100000
+const referenceLimit = 250000
+
+var shaPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{64}$`)
+var guidPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9a-f]{32}$`)
+var metaGUIDPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^guid: ([0-9a-f]{32})$`)
+var keyPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`)

+func refused(format string, args ...any) error {
+	return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrRefused, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...))
+}
+func digest(raw []byte) string { hash := sha256.Sum256(raw); return hex.EncodeToString(hash[:]) }
+func safeText(s string) bool {
+	if !utf8.ValidString(s) {
+		return false
+	}
+	for _, r := range s {
+		if r < 32 || r == 127 {
+			return false
+		}
+	}
+	return true
+}
+func relative(s string) bool {
+	return safeText(s) && fs.ValidPath(s) && s != "." && !strings.Contains(s, "\\") && !strings.Contains(s, ":")
+}
+func skippedPart(p string) bool {
+	for _, part := range strings.Split(p, "/") {
+		switch part {
+		case ".git", ".cache", "Library", "Temp", "Obj", "Logs", "Builds", "Vendor", "ThirdParty", "Packages":
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+func assetPath(p string) bool {
+	return relative(p) && (p == "Assets" || strings.HasPrefix(p, "Assets/")) && !skippedPart(p)
+}
+func projectInput(p string) bool {
+	return assetPath(p) || p == "ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt" || p == "Packages/manifest.json" || p == "Packages/packages-lock.json"
+}
+func artifactPath(p string) bool {
+	return relative(p) && strings.HasSuffix(p, ".json") && (strings.HasPrefix(p, ".artifacts/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, ".cache/"))
+}

+// readRegular never follows a symlink in the supplied root or relative path.
+// Paths from artifacts cannot escape into arbitrary host files.
+func readRegular(ctx context.Context, root, rel string, limit int64) ([]byte, error) {
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if !filepath.IsAbs(root) || filepath.Clean(root) != root || !relative(rel) {
+		return nil, refused("noncanonical local path")
+	}
+	p := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(rel))
+	for at := p; ; at = filepath.Dir(at) {
+		info, err := os.Lstat(at)
+		if err != nil {
+			return nil, refused("read %s: %v", rel, err)
+		}
+		if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
+			return nil, refused("symlink input %s", rel)
+		}
+		if at == p && (!info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Size() > limit) {
+			return nil, refused("nonregular/oversize input %s", rel)
+		}
+		if parent := filepath.Dir(at); parent == at {
+			break
+		}
+	}
+	f, err := os.Open(p)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, refused("open %s: %v", rel, err)
+	}
+	defer f.Close()
+	raw, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, limit+1))
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, refused("read %s: %v", rel, err)
+	}
+	if int64(len(raw)) > limit {
+		return nil, refused("input grew beyond bound %s", rel)
+	}
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return raw, nil
+}
+
+func readHash(ctx context.Context, root string, file fileHash, limit int64) ([]byte, error) {
+	if !shaPattern.MatchString(file.SHA256) {
+		return nil, refused("invalid SHA256")
+	}
+	raw, err := readRegular(ctx, root, file.Path, limit)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if digest(raw) != file.SHA256 {
+		return nil, refused("stale/mixed bytes %s", file.Path)
+	}
+	return raw, nil
+}

+// Standard decoding silently overwrites duplicate JSON keys. Walk the bounded
+// tokens first, refusing duplicates and deep/invalid input before typed decode.
+func strictJSON(raw []byte, value any) error {
+	if len(raw) == 0 || len(raw) > artifactLimit || !utf8.Valid(raw) {
+		return refused("empty/oversize/nonUTF8 JSON")
+	}
+	d := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw))
+	d.UseNumber()
+	if err := uniqueJSON(d, 0, reflect.TypeOf(value), map[reflect.Type]map[string]reflect.Type{}); err != nil {
+		return refused("JSON: %v", err)
+	}
+	if _, err := d.Token(); err != io.EOF {
+		return refused("trailing JSON")
+	}
+	d = json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(raw))
+	d.DisallowUnknownFields()
+	if err := d.Decode(value); err != nil {
+		return refused("JSON shape: %v", err)
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+func uniqueJSON(d *json.Decoder, depth int, expected reflect.Type, fields map[reflect.Type]map[string]reflect.Type) error {
+	if depth > 64 {
+		return fmt.Errorf("nesting exceeds64")
+	}
+	for expected != nil && expected.Kind() == reflect.Pointer {
+		expected = expected.Elem()
+	}
+	t, err := d.Token()
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	delim, ok := t.(json.Delim)
+	if !ok {
+		return nil
+	}
+	switch delim {
+	case '{':
+		var tags map[string]reflect.Type
+		if expected != nil && expected.Kind() == reflect.Struct {
+			tags = fields[expected]
+			if tags == nil {
+				tags = map[string]reflect.Type{}
+				for index := 0; index < expected.NumField(); index++ {
+					field := expected.Field(index)
+					if field.PkgPath != "" {
+						continue
+					}
+					tag := strings.Split(field.Tag.Get("json"), ",")[0]
+					if tag != "" && tag != "-" {
+						tags[tag] = field.Type
+					}
+				}
+				fields[expected] = tags
+			}
+		} else if expected != nil && expected.Kind() != reflect.Map && expected.Kind() != reflect.Interface {
+			return fmt.Errorf("unexpected object shape")
+		}
+		keys := map[string]bool{}
+		for d.More() {
+			k, err := d.Token()
+			if err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+			key, ok := k.(string)
+			if !ok || keys[key] {
+				return fmt.Errorf("duplicate/invalid object key")
+			}
+			keys[key] = true
+			var child reflect.Type
+			if tags != nil {
+				var known bool
+				child, known = tags[key]
+				if !known {
+					return fmt.Errorf("unknown/noncanonical JSON field %q", key)
+				}
+			} else if expected != nil && expected.Kind() == reflect.Map {
+				child = expected.Elem()
+			}
+			if err := uniqueJSON(d, depth+1, child, fields); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+		}
+	case '[':
+		var child reflect.Type
+		if expected != nil {
+			switch expected.Kind() {
+			case reflect.Array, reflect.Slice:
+				child = expected.Elem()
+			case reflect.Interface:
+			default:
+				return fmt.Errorf("unexpected array shape")
+			}
+		}
+		for d.More() {
+			if err := uniqueJSON(d, depth+1, child, fields); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+		}
+	default:
+		return fmt.Errorf("unexpected delimiter")
+	}
+	_, err = d.Token()
+	return err
+}
+
+func metadata(ctx context.Context, projectRoot string) ([]string, error) {
+	var members []string
+	governor := tenancy.NewRowGovernor(ctx, tenancy.ClassTree)
+	err := filepath.WalkDir(filepath.Join(projectRoot, "Assets"), func(p string, entry fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
+		if walkErr != nil {
+			return walkErr
+		}
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		rel, err := filepath.Rel(projectRoot, p)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		rel = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
+		if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
+			if entry.IsDir() {
+				return filepath.SkipDir
+			}
+			return nil
+		}
+		if skippedPart(rel) {
+			if entry.IsDir() {
+				return filepath.SkipDir
+			}
+			return nil
+		}
+		if !entry.IsDir() && strings.HasSuffix(rel, ".meta") {
+			if !entry.Type().IsRegular() {
+				return refused("nonregular metadata")
+			}
+			members = append(members, rel)
+			if len(members) > memberLimit {
+				return refused("metadata membership exceeds bound")
+			}
+		}
+		return nil
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: metadata membership: %w", ErrRefused, err)
+	}
+	slices.Sort(members)
+	return members, nil
+}
+
+func inputMap(files []fileHash) (map[string]string, error) {
+	if len(files) == 0 || len(files) > memberLimit {
+		return nil, refused("empty/overbound source inventory")
+	}
+	m := make(map[string]string, len(files))
+	last := ""
+	for _, file := range files {
+		if !projectInput(file.Path) || !shaPattern.MatchString(file.SHA256) || file.Path <= last {
+			return nil, refused("duplicate/unsorted/noncanonical input")
+		}
+		m[file.Path] = file.SHA256
+		last = file.Path
+	}
+	return m, nil
+}
+
+func sourceBytes(r receipt, i inventory) []byte {
+	var b strings.Builder
+	b.WriteString("fathom.unity.asset-inputs/v1\nproject\x00" + r.Project + "\n")
+	b.WriteString("producer\x00" + r.Producer.Path + "\x00" + r.Producer.SHA256 + "\n")
+	for _, file := range r.Producer.Inputs {
+		b.WriteString("tool\x00" + file.Path + "\x00" + file.SHA256 + "\n")
+	}
+	if r.ContextInventory != nil {
+		b.WriteString("context\x00" + r.ContextInventory.Before + "\n")
+	}
+	for _, scope := range i.Scopes {
+		b.WriteString("scope\x00" + scope + "\n")
+	}
+	metadataMembers := append([]string(nil), i.Metadata...)
+	slices.Sort(metadataMembers)
+	for _, meta := range metadataMembers {
+		b.WriteString("metadata\x00" + meta + "\n")
+	}
+	for _, file := range i.Inputs {
+		b.WriteString("file\x00" + file.Path + "\x00" + file.SHA256 + "\n")
+	}
+	return []byte(b.String())
+}
+
+func validateSource(ctx context.Context, opts Options, r receipt, i inventory) error {
+	if err := tenancy.ProducerAllowsCtx(ctx, tenancy.ClassTree); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	if r.ContextInventory == nil {
+		return refused("missing authored semantic context inventory")
+	}
+	if err := checkSourceMemberCount(len(i.Inputs), len(r.ContextInventory.AssetsCode), len(r.ContextInventory.ProjectSettings)); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	projectRoot := filepath.Join(opts.Root, filepath.FromSlash(opts.Project))
+	if !shaPattern.MatchString(r.Source.Before) || r.Source.Before != r.Source.After || digest(sourceBytes(r, i)) != r.Source.Before {
+		return refused("incomplete/mixed canonical source identity")
+	}
+	producerBytes, err := readHash(ctx, opts.Root, fileHash{r.Producer.Path, r.Producer.SHA256}, inputLimit)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	toolBytes := len(producerBytes)
+	for _, file := range r.Producer.Inputs {
+		raw, err := readHash(ctx, opts.Root, file, inputLimit)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		toolBytes += len(raw)
+		if toolBytes > inputLimit {
+			return refused("producer closure exceeds8MiB")
+		}
+	}
+	members, err := metadata(ctx, projectRoot)
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	expectedMembers := append([]string(nil), i.Metadata...)
+	slices.Sort(expectedMembers)
+	for index, member := range expectedMembers {
+		if index > 0 && member == expectedMembers[index-1] {
+			return refused("duplicate metadata membership")
+		}
+	}
+	if !slices.Equal(members, expectedMembers) {
+		return refused("stale metadata membership")
+	}
+	total := toolBytes
+	governor := tenancy.NewRowGovernor(ctx, tenancy.ClassTree)
+	for _, file := range i.Inputs {
+		if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		raw, err := readHash(ctx, projectRoot, file, inputLimit)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		total += len(raw)
+		if total > sourceLimit {
+			return refused("source closure exceeds64MiB")
+		}
+	}
+	if err := validateContext(ctx, projectRoot, r.ContextInventory, total); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	return tenancy.ProducerAllowsCtx(ctx, tenancy.ClassTree)
+}
+
+func checkScopes(scopes []string) error {
+	if len(scopes) == 0 || len(scopes) > 32 {
+		return refused("empty/overbound scopes")
+	}
+	last := ""
+	for _, scope := range scopes {
+		if !assetPath(scope) || scope <= last {
+			return refused("duplicate/unsorted/unsafe scope")
+		}
+		last = scope
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+func inScope(p string, scopes []string) bool {
+	for _, scope := range scopes {
+		if p == scope || strings.HasPrefix(p, scope+"/") {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}
+func entitySourcePath(p string) bool {
+	switch path.Ext(p) {
+	case ".prefab", ".mat", ".asset":
+		return assetPath(p)
+	}
+	return false
+}

+// Package assetrefs prepares source-bound Unity asset-reference cohorts. It
+// never writes observations, typed edges, code calls or execution evidence.
+package assetrefs
