+package assetrefs
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"path"
+	"slices"
+	"strconv"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/core"
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/tenancy"
+)
+
+func objectID(guid string, id *int64) core.AssetObjectID {
+	value := ""
+	if id != nil {
+		value = strconv.FormatInt(*id, 10)
+	}
+	return core.AssetObjectID{GUID: guid, FileID: value}
+}
+func validID(id core.AssetObjectID) bool {
+	if !guidPattern.MatchString(id.GUID) || len(id.FileID) > 20 {
+		return false
+	}
+	n, err := strconv.ParseInt(id.FileID, 10, 64)
+	return err == nil && n != 0 && strconv.FormatInt(n, 10) == id.FileID
+}
+func objectKey(id core.AssetObjectID) string { return id.GUID + "#" + id.FileID }
+func sourceKey(p string, id *int64) string {
+	if id == nil {
+		return p + "\x00<missing>"
+	}
+	return p + "\x00" + strconv.FormatInt(*id, 10)
+}
+
+type tuple struct {
+	Source core.AssetObjectID
+	Target core.AssetObjectID
+}
+
+func tupleKey(t tuple) string { return objectKey(t.Source) + "\x00" + objectKey(t.Target) }
+
+type referenceGroup struct {
+	Tuple  tuple
+	Path   string
+	Raw    []core.AssetDeclaredLocation
+	Native []string
+}
+
+func normalize(ctx context.Context, opts Options, i inventory, n oracle, inputs map[string]string) (core.AssetReferenceSnapshot, error) {
+	var empty core.AssetReferenceSnapshot
+	governor := tenancy.NewRowGovernor(ctx, tenancy.ClassTree)
+	snapshot := core.AssetReferenceSnapshot{Schema: SnapshotSchema, Family: "unity-declared", Service: opts.Service, Project: opts.Project, FamilyID: opts.FamilyID, Scopes: append([]string(nil), i.Scopes...), Entities: []core.AssetObject{}, References: []core.AssetReference{}, Gaps: []core.AssetReferenceGap{}}
+	snapshot.SkippedMetadata = append([]string(nil), i.Skipped...)
+	slices.Sort(snapshot.SkippedMetadata)
+	snapshot.Limitations = []string{"Selected non-scene authored cohort; no complete asset or language grade.", "Declared/native occurrences are grouped; raw locations and native properties are unpaired.", "Native-only and unbound package targets are disclosed, not admitted declared edges.", "No code calls, callback execution, test certification or art approval."}
+	snapshot.Limitations = append(snapshot.Limitations, "Input-current under bound authored code/settings and recorded trusted Editor/target; complete external package/tool-bundle semantics and current interactive Editor state are not established.")
+	rawSources := map[string]bool{}
+	sourcePaths := map[string]bool{}
+	for _, row := range i.Entities {
+		if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		if !entitySourcePath(row.Path) || !inScope(row.Path, i.Scopes) || inputs[row.Path] == "" || row.FileID == nil || *row.FileID == 0 || row.ClassID <= 0 {
+			return empty, refused("unsupported/unbound raw source entity")
+		}
+		key := sourceKey(row.Path, row.FileID)
+		if rawSources[key] {
+			return empty, refused("duplicate raw source fileID")
+		}
+		rawSources[key] = true
+		sourcePaths[row.Path] = true
+	}
+	nativeSources := map[string]core.AssetObjectID{}
+	objects := map[string]core.AssetObject{}
+	for _, row := range n.Entities {
+		if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		key := sourceKey(row.Path, row.FileID)
+		asset, ok := i.Assets[row.Path]
+		id := objectID(row.GUID, row.FileID)
+		if !rawSources[key] || !ok || asset.GUID != row.GUID || !validID(id) || !safeText(row.TypeName) || row.TypeName == "" || len(row.TypeName) > 1024 {
+			return empty, refused("mixed/unbound native source identity")
+		}
+		if _, duplicate := nativeSources[key]; duplicate {
+			return empty, refused("duplicate native source entity")
+		}
+		if _, duplicate := objects[objectKey(id)]; duplicate {
+			return empty, refused("duplicate native persistent identity")
+		}
+		nativeSources[key] = id
+		objects[objectKey(id)] = core.AssetObject{ID: id, Path: path.Join(opts.Project, row.Path), Basis: "native-source", TypeName: row.TypeName}
+	}
+	if len(rawSources) != len(nativeSources) {
+		return empty, refused("incomplete native source enumeration")
+	}
+	assetSeen := map[string]bool{}
+	for _, row := range n.Assets {
+		if !sourcePaths[row.Path] || assetSeen[row.Path] || i.Assets[row.Path].GUID != row.GUID || !guidPattern.MatchString(row.DependencyHash) {
+			return empty, refused("mixed/duplicate native source asset")
+		}
+		assetSeen[row.Path] = true
+		if len(row.Dependencies) == 0 || len(row.Dependencies) > memberLimit {
+			return empty, refused("missing/overbound native dependencies")
+		}
+		lastDependency := ""
+		includesSelf := false
+		for _, dependency := range row.Dependencies {
+			if !relative(dependency) || dependency <= lastDependency {
+				return empty, refused("unsafe/duplicate/unsorted native dependency")
+			}
+			lastDependency = dependency
+			if dependency == row.Path {
+				includesSelf = true
+			}
+			if strings.HasPrefix(dependency, "Assets/") && inputs[dependency] == "" {
+				return empty, refused("unbound authored native dependency")
+			}
+		}
+		if !includesSelf {
+			return empty, refused("native dependency inventory omits source asset")
+		}
+	}
+	if len(assetSeen) != len(sourcePaths) {
+		return empty, refused("incomplete native dependency enumeration")
+	}
+	groups := map[string]*referenceGroup{}
+	getGroup := func(t tuple) *referenceGroup {
+		key := tupleKey(t)
+		group := groups[key]
+		if group == nil {
+			group = &referenceGroup{Tuple: t}
+			groups[key] = group
+		}
+		return group
+	}
+	locations := map[string]bool{}
+	for _, row := range i.References {
+		if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		source, ok := nativeSources[sourceKey(row.Source, row.SourceID)]
+		if !ok || row.Line <= 0 || row.Line > 10000000 || !safeText(row.Field) || row.Field == "" || len(row.Field) > 4096 {
+			return empty, refused("invalid raw reference origin")
+		}
+		location := row.Source + "\x00" + strconv.Itoa(row.Line)
+		if locations[location] {
+			return empty, refused("duplicate raw reference location")
+		}
+		locations[location] = true
+		if row.FileID == nil {
+			return empty, refused("missing raw fileID")
+		}
+		if row.Target != "" && !assetPath(row.Target) {
+			return empty, refused("unsafe raw target path")
+		}
+		if *row.FileID == 0 {
+			if row.Status != "null" {
+				return empty, refused("mixed raw null status")
+			}
+			snapshot.Counts.RawNull++
+			continue
+		}
+		switch row.Status {
+		case "resolved_local", "resolved_serialized", "unknown_imported_or_outside_parse_scope_id", "external_or_missing_guid":
+		default:
+			return empty, refused("unknown/invalid raw target identity")
+		}
+		guid := row.GUID
+		if guid == "" {
+			guid = source.GUID
+		}
+		target := objectID(guid, row.FileID)
+		if !validID(target) {
+			return empty, refused("invalid raw target GUID/fileID")
+		}
+		group := getGroup(tuple{source, target})
+		group.Raw = append(group.Raw, core.AssetDeclaredLocation{Line: row.Line, Field: row.Field})
+		snapshot.Counts.RawNonnull++
+	}
+	properties := map[string]bool{}
+	// A persistent GUID owns one asset path across the entire cohort, not
+	// merely inside one source/target tuple or the admitted-edge branch.
+	// Seed authored ownership before looking at package/native-only targets.
+	targetOwners := map[string]string{}
+	for _, assetPath := range sortedKeys(i.Assets) {
+		targetOwners[i.Assets[assetPath].GUID] = assetPath
+	}
+	for _, row := range n.References {
+		if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		source, ok := nativeSources[sourceKey(row.Source, row.SourceID)]
+		if !ok || source.GUID != row.SourceGUID || row.Property == "" || !safeText(row.Property) || len(row.Property) > 4096 {
+			return empty, refused("invalid native property origin")
+		}
+		propertyKey := objectKey(source) + "\x00" + row.Property
+		if properties[propertyKey] {
+			return empty, refused("duplicate native property identity")
+		}
+		properties[propertyKey] = true
+		if row.Available == nil || row.TargetID == nil {
+			return empty, refused("missing native availability/fileID")
+		}
+		if !*row.Available {
+			if row.TargetGUID != "" || *row.TargetID != 0 || row.TargetPath != "" {
+				return empty, refused("conflicting unavailable native target")
+			}
+			snapshot.Counts.NativeUnavailable++
+			continue
+		}
+		target := objectID(row.TargetGUID, row.TargetID)
+		if !validID(target) || !relative(row.TargetPath) {
+			return empty, refused("missing available native target identity")
+		}
+		if owner, known := targetOwners[row.TargetGUID]; known && owner != row.TargetPath {
+			return empty, refused("conflicting global native GUID owner path")
+		}
+		targetOwners[row.TargetGUID] = row.TargetPath
+		group := getGroup(tuple{source, target})
+		if group.Path != "" && group.Path != row.TargetPath {
+			return empty, refused("conflicting native target path")
+		}
+		group.Path = row.TargetPath
+		group.Native = append(group.Native, row.Property)
+		snapshot.Counts.NativeAvailable++
+	}
+	for _, key := range sortedKeys(groups) {
+		if err := governor.Row(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		group := groups[key]
+		slices.Sort(group.Native)
+		slices.SortFunc(group.Raw, func(a, b core.AssetDeclaredLocation) int {
+			if a.Line < b.Line {
+				return -1
+			}
+			if a.Line > b.Line {
+				return 1
+			}
+			return strings.Compare(a.Field, b.Field)
+		})
+		if len(group.Raw) > len(group.Native) {
+			return empty, refused("raw-only or missing native target occurrence")
+		}
+		matched := len(group.Raw)
+		nativeOnly := len(group.Native) - matched
+		snapshot.Counts.Matched += matched
+		snapshot.Counts.NativeOnly += nativeOnly
+		if nativeOnly > 0 {
+			snapshot.Gaps = append(snapshot.Gaps, core.AssetReferenceGap{Reason: "native-only-not-declared", Source: group.Tuple.Source, Target: group.Tuple.Target, TargetPath: group.Path, Occurrences: nativeOnly, NativeProperties: append([]string(nil), group.Native...)})
+		}
+		if matched == 0 {
+			continue
+		}
+		targetAsset, mapped := i.Assets[group.Path]
+		bound := mapped && targetAsset.GUID == group.Tuple.Target.GUID && inputs[group.Path] != "" && inputs[targetAsset.Meta] != ""
+		if !bound {
+			if strings.HasPrefix(group.Path, "Assets/") {
+				return empty, refused("unbound/missing authored target GUID/fileID")
+			}
+			snapshot.Counts.NativeObservedUnbound += matched
+			snapshot.Gaps = append(snapshot.Gaps, core.AssetReferenceGap{Reason: "native-observed-unbound", Source: group.Tuple.Source, Target: group.Tuple.Target, TargetPath: group.Path, Occurrences: matched, DeclaredLocations: group.Raw, NativeProperties: group.Native})
+			continue
+		}
+		if sourcePaths[group.Path] {
+			id, err := strconv.ParseInt(group.Tuple.Target.FileID, 10, 64)
+			if err != nil {
+				return empty, refused("invalid target fileID")
+			}
+			if _, ok := nativeSources[sourceKey(group.Path, &id)]; !ok {
+				return empty, refused("unknown local target fileID")
+			}
+		}
+		object := core.AssetObject{ID: group.Tuple.Target, Path: path.Join(opts.Project, group.Path), Basis: "observed-target"}
+		if old, exists := objects[objectKey(object.ID)]; exists {
+			if old.Path != object.Path {
+				return empty, refused("conflicting object owner path")
+			}
+		} else {
+			objects[objectKey(object.ID)] = object
+		}
+		sourceObject := objects[objectKey(group.Tuple.Source)]
+		snapshot.References = append(snapshot.References, core.AssetReference{Kind: "declared-object-reference", Source: group.Tuple.Source, Target: group.Tuple.Target, SourcePath: sourceObject.Path, TargetPath: object.Path, MatchedOccurrences: matched, DeclaredLocations: group.Raw, NativeProperties: group.Native})
+		snapshot.Counts.AdmittedMatched += matched
+	}
+	if snapshot.Counts.Matched == 0 {
+		return empty, refused("empty independently matched cohort")
+	}
+	for _, key := range sortedKeys(objects) {
+		snapshot.Entities = append(snapshot.Entities, objects[key])
+	}
+	return snapshot, nil
+}

+package assetrefs

+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"path"

+	"strings"

+// Prepare validates a genuinely producer-bound raw/native partial cohort. It
+// returns no snapshot on refusal and makes no store/service/config mutation.
+// The caller must supply trusted local root/tool identity and an active marker.
+func Prepare(ctx context.Context, opts Options) (core.AssetReferenceSnapshot, error) {
+	var empty core.AssetReferenceSnapshot
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	if err := tenancy.ProducerAllowsCtx(ctx, tenancy.ClassTree); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	if !filepath.IsAbs(opts.Root) || filepath.Clean(opts.Root) != opts.Root || !safeText(opts.Service) || opts.Service == "" || len(opts.Service) > 512 || (opts.Project != "." && !relative(opts.Project)) || !keyPattern.MatchString(opts.FamilyID) || !artifactPath(opts.ReceiptPath) || !artifactPath(opts.ActivePath) || opts.ReceiptPath == opts.ActivePath {
+		return empty, refused("missing/noncanonical caller scope")
+	}
+	if opts.ExpectedEditorVersion == "" || !safeText(opts.ExpectedEditorVersion) || !shaPattern.MatchString(opts.ExpectedEditorSHA256) || opts.ExpectedBuildTarget == "" || !safeText(opts.ExpectedBuildTarget) {
+		return empty, refused("missing expected local Editor identity/target")
+	}
+	activeRaw, err := readRegular(ctx, opts.Root, opts.ActivePath, artifactLimit)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	var a active
+	if err := strictJSON(activeRaw, &a); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	if a.Schema != ActiveSchema || a.Phase != "complete" || a.Project != opts.Project || a.FamilyID != opts.FamilyID || !keyPattern.MatchString(a.RunID) || a.Receipt.Path != opts.ReceiptPath {
+		return empty, refused("missing/incomplete/wrong active attempt")
+	}
+	receiptRaw, err := readHash(ctx, opts.Root, a.Receipt, artifactLimit)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	var r receipt
+	if err := strictJSON(receiptRaw, &r); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	if err := checkReceipt(opts, a, r); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	invRaw, err := readHash(ctx, opts.Root, r.Inventory, artifactLimit)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	nativeRaw, err := readHash(ctx, opts.Root, r.Oracle, artifactLimit)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	var i inventory
+	var n oracle
+	if err := strictJSON(invRaw, &i); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	if err := strictJSON(nativeRaw, &n); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	inputs, err := checkArtifacts(opts, r, i, n)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	if err := validateSource(ctx, opts, r, i); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	projectRoot := filepath.Join(opts.Root, filepath.FromSlash(opts.Project))
+	versionBytes, err := readHash(ctx, projectRoot, fileHash{"ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt", inputs["ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt"]}, inputLimit)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	versionLine := strings.SplitN(string(versionBytes), "\n", 2)[0]
+	if versionLine != "m_EditorVersion: "+opts.ExpectedEditorVersion {
+		return empty, refused("Editor differs from actual project pin")
+	}
+	if _, err := readHash(ctx, projectRoot, r.OracleAssembly, artifactLimit); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	if err := validateMetadata(ctx, projectRoot, i, inputs); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	snapshot, err := normalize(ctx, opts, i, n, inputs)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	// Close ordinary change windows across normalization; this is not a hostile
+	// filesystem transaction or a cryptographic producer signature.
+	if err := validateSource(ctx, opts, r, i); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	for _, file := range []fileHash{a.Receipt, r.Inventory, r.Oracle, {opts.ActivePath, digest(activeRaw)}} {
+		if _, err := readHash(ctx, opts.Root, file, artifactLimit); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+	}
+	if _, err := readHash(ctx, projectRoot, r.OracleAssembly, artifactLimit); err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	snapshot.ReceiptSHA256 = digest(receiptRaw)
+	snapshot.SourceSHA256 = r.Source.Before
+	snapshot.ContextSHA256 = r.ContextInventory.Before
+	snapshot.EditorVersion = r.Editor.Version
+	snapshot.BuildTarget = n.BuildTarget
+	return snapshot, nil
+}
+
+func checkReceipt(opts Options, a active, r receipt) error {
+	if r.Schema != ReceiptSchema || r.Status != "complete" || r.RunID != a.RunID || r.Project != opts.Project || r.FamilyID != opts.FamilyID || r.ExitCode == nil || *r.ExitCode != 0 {
+		return refused("incomplete/mixed producer receipt")
+	}
+	if r.ContextInventory == nil {
+		return refused("missing authored semantic context inventory")
+	}
+	if r.Producer.Name != ProducerName || r.Producer.Version != "1" || !relative(r.Producer.Path) || !shaPattern.MatchString(r.Producer.SHA256) || len(r.Producer.Inputs) == 0 || len(r.Producer.Inputs) > 32 {
+		return refused("missing/wrong producer identity/closure")
+	}
+	last := ""
+	for _, file := range r.Producer.Inputs {
+		if !relative(file.Path) || !shaPattern.MatchString(file.SHA256) || file.Path <= last || file.Path == r.Producer.Path {
+			return refused("duplicate/unsafe/unsorted producer inputs")
+		}
+		last = file.Path
+	}
+	if r.Editor.Version != opts.ExpectedEditorVersion || r.Editor.SHA256 != opts.ExpectedEditorSHA256 {
+		return refused("wrong expected Editor identity")
+	}
+	start, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, r.StartedAt)
+	if err != nil {
+		return refused("invalid attempt start")
+	}
+	finish, err := time.Parse(time.RFC3339Nano, r.FinishedAt)
+	if err != nil || !finish.After(start) {
+		return refused("invalid attempt interval")
+	}
+	if r.Coverage.FamilyComplete == nil || *r.Coverage.FamilyComplete || r.Coverage.SourceFormat != "selected-non-scene-authored-assets" || r.Coverage.Cohort != "declared-native-intersection" {
+		return refused("unsupported coverage assertion")
+	}
+	if !artifactPath(r.Inventory.Path) || !artifactPath(r.Oracle.Path) || r.Inventory.Path == r.Oracle.Path || r.Inventory.Path == opts.ReceiptPath || r.Oracle.Path == opts.ReceiptPath || r.Inventory.Path == opts.ActivePath || r.Oracle.Path == opts.ActivePath {
+		return refused("conflicting/unsafe raw artifacts")
+	}
+	if !relative(r.OracleAssembly.Path) || path.Dir(r.OracleAssembly.Path) != "Library/ScriptAssemblies" || path.Ext(r.OracleAssembly.Path) != ".dll" || !shaPattern.MatchString(r.OracleAssembly.SHA256) {
+		return refused("invalid local oracle assembly identity")
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+func checkArtifacts(opts Options, r receipt, i inventory, n oracle) (map[string]string, error) {
+	if i.Schema != "unity-declared-references/v1" || i.Parser != "stdlib-inline-map-subset/v1" || i.Project != filepath.Join(opts.Root, filepath.FromSlash(opts.Project)) || len(i.Problems) != 0 {
+		return nil, refused("unsupported/incomplete inventory")
+	}
+	if err := checkScopes(i.Scopes); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if len(i.Entities) == 0 || len(i.Entities) > entityLimit || len(i.References) > referenceLimit || len(i.Assets) > memberLimit || len(i.Metadata) == 0 || len(i.Metadata) > memberLimit {
+		return nil, refused("empty/overbound source cohort")
+	}
+	inputs, err := inputMap(i.Inputs)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	for _, skipped := range i.Skipped {
+		if !relative(skipped) || !strings.HasPrefix(skipped, "Assets/") || !strings.HasSuffix(skipped, ".meta") {
+			return nil, refused("unsafe skipped metadata disclosure")
+		}
+	}
+	for _, required := range []string{"ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt", "Packages/manifest.json", "Packages/packages-lock.json"} {
+		if inputs[required] == "" {
+			return nil, refused("missing project/package pin")
+		}
+	}
+	if n.Schema != 1 || n.Oracle != "Unity SerializedObject/ObjectReference + AssetDatabase" || n.UnityVersion != r.Editor.Version || n.BuildTarget != opts.ExpectedBuildTarget || n.InventorySHA256 != r.Inventory.SHA256 || n.AssemblySHA256 != r.OracleAssembly.SHA256 || len(n.Unjudged) != 0 {
+		return nil, refused("incomplete/mixed native oracle")
+	}
+	if len(n.Entities) == 0 || len(n.Entities) > entityLimit || len(n.References) > referenceLimit || len(n.Assets) > memberLimit {
+		return nil, refused("empty/overbound native cohort")
+	}
+	nativeInputs, err := inputMap(n.Inputs)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if len(inputs) != len(nativeInputs) {
+		return nil, refused("mixed native input membership")
+	}
+	for p, hash := range inputs {
+		if nativeInputs[p] != hash {
+			return nil, refused("mixed native input identity")
+		}
+	}
+	return inputs, nil
+}
+
+func validateMetadata(ctx context.Context, root string, i inventory, inputs map[string]string) error {
+	if len(i.Assets) != len(i.Metadata) {
+		return refused("incomplete metadata mapping")
+	}
+	seen := map[string]string{}
+	last := ""
+	metadataMembers := append([]string(nil), i.Metadata...)
+	slices.Sort(metadataMembers)
+	for _, meta := range metadataMembers {
+		if !assetPath(meta) || !strings.HasSuffix(meta, ".meta") || meta <= last || inputs[meta] == "" {
+			return refused("invalid metadata membership")
+		}
+		last = meta
+		asset := strings.TrimSuffix(meta, ".meta")
+		declared, ok := i.Assets[asset]
+		if !ok || declared.Meta != meta || !guidPattern.MatchString(declared.GUID) {
+			return refused("missing/invalid asset GUID mapping")
+		}
+		if old := seen[declared.GUID]; old != "" {
+			return refused("duplicate GUID maps to multiple assets")
+		}
+		seen[declared.GUID] = asset
+		raw, err := readHash(ctx, root, fileHash{meta, inputs[meta]}, inputLimit)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		if !utf8.Valid(raw) || bytes.IndexByte(raw, 0) >= 0 {
+			return refused("binary/nonUTF8 metadata")
+		}
+		matches := metaGUIDPattern.FindAllSubmatch(raw, -1)
+		if len(matches) != 1 || string(matches[0][1]) != declared.GUID {
+			return refused("missing/duplicate/mixed metadata GUID")
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// Query revalidates raw proof, active generation and current source before
+// serving a bounded one-hop result. A supplied prepared DTO is not authority.
+func Query(ctx context.Context, opts Options, q core.AssetReferenceQuery) (core.AssetReferenceResult, error) {
+	var empty core.AssetReferenceResult
+	if !validID(q.Object) || (q.Direction != "inbound" && q.Direction != "outbound") || q.Limit < 0 || q.Limit > 100 {
+		return empty, refused("invalid asset query scope")
+	}
+	limit := q.Limit
+	if limit == 0 {
+		limit = 25
+	}
+	snapshot, err := Prepare(ctx, opts)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	result := core.AssetReferenceResult{Status: "current_partial", Service: opts.Service, Project: opts.Project, FamilyID: opts.FamilyID, Object: q.Object, Direction: q.Direction, ReceiptSHA256: snapshot.ReceiptSHA256, SourceSHA256: snapshot.SourceSHA256, ContextSHA256: snapshot.ContextSHA256, EditorVersion: snapshot.EditorVersion, BuildTarget: snapshot.BuildTarget, References: []core.AssetReference{}, Counts: snapshot.Counts}
+	result.Limitations = append([]string(nil), snapshot.Limitations...)
+	for _, reference := range snapshot.References {
+		id := reference.Source
+		if q.Direction == "inbound" {
+			id = reference.Target
+		}
+		if id == q.Object {
+			result.Total++
+		}
+	}
+	result.Truncated = result.Total
+	baseBytes, err := json.Marshal(result)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, refused("encode asset result: %v", err)
+	}
+	if len(baseBytes) > 16<<10 {
+		return empty, refused("asset result metadata exceeds16KiB")
+	}
+	for _, reference := range snapshot.References {
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return empty, err
+		}
+		id := reference.Source
+		if q.Direction == "inbound" {
+			id = reference.Target
+		}
+		if id != q.Object {
+			continue
+		}
+		if len(result.References) >= limit {
+			continue
+		}
+		result.References = append(result.References, reference)
+		result.Truncated = result.Total - len(result.References)
+		encoded, err := json.Marshal(result)
+		if err != nil {
+			return empty, refused("encode bounded asset result: %v", err)
+		}
+		if len(encoded) > 16<<10 {
+			result.References = result.References[:len(result.References)-1]
+			result.Truncated = result.Total - len(result.References)
+		}
+	}
+	result.Truncated = result.Total - len(result.References)
+	// The source may change while constructing even this bounded projection.
+	// Prepare did its own post-check; repeat the active+raw/source validation
+	// rather than returning apparently-current positive rows from a changed run.
+	final, err := Prepare(ctx, opts)
+	if err != nil {
+		return empty, err
+	}
+	if final.ReceiptSHA256 != snapshot.ReceiptSHA256 || final.SourceSHA256 != snapshot.SourceSHA256 {
+		return empty, refused("source/generation changed during query")
+	}
+	return result, nil
+}
+
+// Keep sorting explicit for deterministic source ordering at every wire seam.
+func sortedKeys[V any](m map[string]V) []string {
+	keys := make([]string, 0, len(m))
+	for k := range m {
+		keys = append(keys, k)
+	}
+	slices.Sort(keys)
+	return keys
+}

+func writeFile(t *testing.T, root, p string, raw []byte) {
+	t.Helper()
+	absolute := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(p))
+	if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(absolute), 0700); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if err := os.WriteFile(absolute, raw, 0600); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+}
+func writeJSON(t *testing.T, root, p string, value any) []byte {
+	t.Helper()
+	raw, err := json.Marshal(value)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	writeFile(t, root, p, raw)
+	return raw
+}

+	}
+	f.native.References = append(f.native.References, nativeReference{Source: "Assets/Fixture/Cart.prefab", SourceGUID: sourceGUID, SourceID: i64(sourceID), Property: "shader", TargetGUID: packageGUID, TargetID: i64(4800000), TargetPath: "Packages/fixture/Shader.shader", Available: boolean(true)}, nativeReference{Source: "Assets/Fixture/Cart.prefab", SourceGUID: sourceGUID, SourceID: i64(sourceID), Property: "m_PrefabAsset", TargetGUID: sourceGUID, TargetID: i64(sourceID), TargetPath: "Assets/Fixture/Cart.prefab", Available: boolean(true)}, nativeReference{Source: "Assets/Fixture/Cart.prefab", SourceGUID: sourceGUID, SourceID: i64(sourceID), Property: "null", TargetID: i64(0), Available: boolean(false)})
+	f.active = active{Schema: ActiveSchema, Project: project, FamilyID: "cart", Phase: "complete", RunID: f.receipt.RunID, Receipt: fileHash{Path: f.opts.ReceiptPath}}
+	f.publish(t)
+	return f
+}
+func (f *fixture) publish(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Helper()
+	raw := writeJSON(t, f.opts.Root, f.receipt.Inventory.Path, f.inventory)
+	f.receipt.Inventory.SHA256 = digest(raw)
+	f.native.InventorySHA256 = f.receipt.Inventory.SHA256
+	raw = writeJSON(t, f.opts.Root, f.receipt.Oracle.Path, f.native)
+	f.receipt.Oracle.SHA256 = digest(raw)
+	if f.receipt.ContextInventory != nil {
+		f.receipt.ContextInventory.Before = digest(contextBytes(*f.receipt.ContextInventory))
+		f.receipt.ContextInventory.After = f.receipt.ContextInventory.Before
+	}
+	f.receipt.Source.Before = digest(sourceBytes(f.receipt, f.inventory))
+	f.receipt.Source.After = f.receipt.Source.Before
+	raw = writeJSON(t, f.opts.Root, f.opts.ReceiptPath, f.receipt)
+	f.active.Receipt.SHA256 = digest(raw)
+	writeJSON(t, f.opts.Root, f.opts.ActivePath, f.active)
+}
+func expectRefused(t *testing.T, f *fixture) {
+	t.Helper()
+	s, err := Prepare(context.Background(), f.opts)
+	if !errors.Is(err, ErrRefused) || !reflect.DeepEqual(s, core.AssetReferenceSnapshot{}) {
+		t.Fatalf("expected refusal with no snapshot, got %#v, %v", s, err)
+	}
+}

+func TestPrepareUnityAssetReferencesPreservesDistinctProvenanceAndMultiplicity(t *testing.T) {
+	f := newFixture(t)
+	s, err := Prepare(context.Background(), f.opts)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if s.FamilyComplete || s.Runtime || s.Grade != nil || s.Family != "unity-declared" {
+		t.Fatalf("inflated proof: %#v", s)
+	}
+	if len(s.References) != 1 || s.References[0].MatchedOccurrences != 2 || len(s.References[0].DeclaredLocations) != 2 || !slices.Equal(s.References[0].NativeProperties, []string{"body.mesh", "preview.mesh"}) {
+		t.Fatalf("lost grouped multiplicity: %#v", s.References)
+	}
+	if s.References[0].Source.FileID != "-5831914722253275453" || s.References[0].Target.FileID != "9007199254740993" {
+		t.Fatalf("rounded signed64 identity: %#v", s.References[0])
+	}
+	if s.References[0].SourcePath != "game/Fixture/Assets/Fixture/Cart.prefab" || s.References[0].TargetPath != "game/Fixture/Assets/Fixture/Model.fbx" {
+		t.Fatalf("reference lacks bound readable endpoint paths: %#v", s.References[0])
+	}
+	if s.Counts.RawNonnull != 3 || s.Counts.Matched != 3 || s.Counts.AdmittedMatched != 2 || s.Counts.NativeObservedUnbound != 1 || s.Counts.NativeOnly != 1 || s.Counts.RawNull != 1 || s.Counts.NativeUnavailable != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("gap denominator lost: %#v", s.Counts)
+	}
+	if len(s.Gaps) != 2 || len(s.Entities) != 2 || s.Entities[1].Basis != "observed-target" || s.Entities[1].TypeName != "" {
+		t.Fatalf("invented target type/gaps: %#v", s)
+	}
+	raw, err := json.Marshal(s)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	for _, forbidden := range []string{`"Calls"`, `"typed"`, `"runtime":true`, `"family_complete":true`} {
+		if strings.Contains(string(raw), forbidden) {
+			t.Fatalf("code/runtime contamination: %s", raw)
+		}
+	}
+	if !strings.Contains(string(raw), `"file_id":"9007199254740993"`) {
+		t.Fatalf("ID is not a JSON string: %s", raw)
+	}
+}

+func TestUnityAssetReferenceJSONFieldNamesAreCaseExactAtEveryStructLevel(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := []struct {
+		raw    string
+		target any
+	}{
+		{`{"status":"failed","Status":"complete"}`, &receipt{}},
+		{`{"Status":"complete"}`, &receipt{}},
+		{`{"phase":"started","Phase":"complete"}`, &active{}},
+		{`{"Phase":"complete"}`, &active{}},
+		{`{"editor":{"version":"old","Version":"new"}}`, &receipt{}},
+		{`{"editor":{"Version":"new"}}`, &receipt{}},
+		{`{"context_inventory":{"schema":"old","Schema":"new"}}`, &receipt{}},
+		{`{"context_inventory":{"Schema":"new"}}`, &receipt{}},
+		{`{"producer":{"inputs":[{"path":"old","Path":"new"}]}}`, &receipt{}},
+	}
+	for _, test := range cases {
+		if err := strictJSON([]byte(test.raw), test.target); !errors.Is(err, ErrRefused) {
+			t.Fatalf("accepted case-folded wire fields %s: %v", test.raw, err)
+		}
+	}
+	// Dynamic map keys remain exact data, not struct field names. Their owning
+	// semantic path validator is a separate step; capitalization is not erased.
+	var inv inventory
+	if err := strictJSON([]byte(`{"assets":{"Assets/MixedCase.mat":{"guid":"11111111111111111111111111111111","meta":"Assets/MixedCase.mat.meta","importer":"NativeFormatImporter"}}}`), &inv); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if _, ok := inv.Assets["Assets/MixedCase.mat"]; !ok {
+		t.Fatal("dynamic asset path key was changed")
+	}
+}
+
+func TestUnityAssetReferenceQueryBudgetsTheCompleteJSONEnvelope(t *testing.T) {
+	f := newFixture(t)
+	for index := 0; index < 4; index++ {
+		extra := f.native.References[0]
+		extra.Property = strings.Repeat("x", 3900) + string(rune('a'+index))
+		f.native.References = append(f.native.References, extra)
+	}
+	f.publish(t)
+	snapshot, err := Prepare(context.Background(), f.opts)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	group, err := json.Marshal(snapshot.References[0])
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if len(group) >= 16<<10 {
+		t.Fatalf("fixture must isolate envelope overhead, not overlarge group: %d", len(group))
+	}
+	result, err := Query(context.Background(), f.opts, core.AssetReferenceQuery{Object: objectID(meshGUID, i64(meshID)), Direction: "inbound"})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	encoded, err := json.Marshal(result)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if len(encoded) > 16<<10 || result.Total != 1 || result.Truncated != 1 || len(result.References) != 0 {
+		t.Fatalf("complete wire budget/denominator violated: %d bytes %#v", len(encoded), result)
+	}
+	control := result
+	control.References = snapshot.References
+	control.Truncated = 0
+	controlBytes, err := json.Marshal(control)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	if len(controlBytes) <= 16<<10 {
+		t.Fatalf("fixture does not exercise group-fitting/envelope-overflow boundary: %d", len(controlBytes))
+	}
+}

+func TestUnityAssetReferenceCanonicalStreamsMatchIndependentLiteralGolden(t *testing.T) {
+	one := "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111"
+	two := "2222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222222"
+	contextGolden := []byte("fathom.unity.asset-context/v2\nfile\x00Assets/Base.cs\x00" + one + "\nfile\x00ProjectSettings/Editor.asset\x00" + two + "\n")
+	c := contextInventory{Schema: ContextSchema, AssetsCode: []fileHash{{"Assets/Base.cs", one}}, ProjectSettings: []fileHash{{"ProjectSettings/Editor.asset", two}}}
+	if got := contextBytes(c); !bytes.Equal(got, contextGolden) {
+		t.Fatalf("context protocol literal differs: %q", got)
+	}
+	sum := sha256.Sum256(contextGolden)
+	c.Before = hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
+	c.After = c.Before
+	r := receipt{Project: "game/Fixture", Producer: producer{Path: "Tools/run.py", SHA256: one, Inputs: []fileHash{{"Tools/helper.py", two}}}, ContextInventory: &c}
+	i := inventory{Scopes: []string{"Assets/Fixture"}, Metadata: []string{"Assets/Fixture.meta"}, Inputs: []fileHash{{"Assets/Fixture.meta", two}}}
+	mainGolden := []byte("fathom.unity.asset-inputs/v1\nproject\x00game/Fixture\nproducer\x00Tools/run.py\x00" + one + "\ntool\x00Tools/helper.py\x00" + two + "\ncontext\x00" + c.Before + "\nscope\x00Assets/Fixture\nmetadata\x00Assets/Fixture.meta\nfile\x00Assets/Fixture.meta\x00" + two + "\n")
+	if got := sourceBytes(r, i); !bytes.Equal(got, mainGolden) {
+		t.Fatalf("main protocol literal differs: %q", got)
+	}
+}

+// Native inventory uses deterministic Path order (a directory's children sort
+// before its adjacent folder.meta); the canonical protocol uses bytewise string
+// order. Artifact array order is not a membership assertion.
+func pathOrderedMetadataFixture(t *testing.T) *fixture {
+	t.Helper()
+	f := newFixture(t)
+	meta := "Assets/Fixture.meta"
+	metaBytes := []byte("guid: 44444444444444444444444444444444\n")
+	writeFile(t, f.opts.Root, f.opts.Project+"/"+meta, metaBytes)
+	f.inventory.Metadata = append(f.inventory.Metadata, meta)
+	f.inventory.Assets["Assets/Fixture"] = rawAsset{GUID: "44444444444444444444444444444444", Meta: meta, Importer: "DefaultImporter"}
+	f.inventory.Inputs = append(f.inventory.Inputs, fileHash{meta, digest(metaBytes)})
+	f.receipt.ContextInventory.AssetsCode = append(f.receipt.ContextInventory.AssetsCode, fileHash{meta, digest(metaBytes)})
+	slices.SortFunc(f.receipt.ContextInventory.AssetsCode, func(a, b fileHash) int { return strings.Compare(a.Path, b.Path) })
+	slices.SortFunc(f.inventory.Inputs, func(a, b fileHash) int { return strings.Compare(a.Path, b.Path) })
+	f.native.Inputs = append([]fileHash(nil), f.inventory.Inputs...)
+	f.publish(t)
+	// Bind the canonical sorted stream without changing original artifact bytes.
+	canonical := f.inventory
+	canonical.Metadata = append([]string(nil), f.inventory.Metadata...)
+	slices.Sort(canonical.Metadata)
+	f.receipt.Source.Before = digest(sourceBytes(f.receipt, canonical))
+	f.receipt.Source.After = f.receipt.Source.Before
+	raw := writeJSON(t, f.opts.Root, f.opts.ReceiptPath, f.receipt)
+	f.active.Receipt.SHA256 = digest(raw)
+	writeJSON(t, f.opts.Root, f.opts.ActivePath, f.active)
+	return f
+}

+// A v1 receipt has its own genuine canonical stream, rather than just a v1
+// label pasted onto v2 hashes. Its omitted metadata cannot authorize a v2 read.
+func TestUnityAssetReferenceContextV1CannotAuthorizeCurrentLinks(t *testing.T) {

+	c.Schema = "fathom.unity.asset-context/v1"
+	c.AssetsCode = slices.DeleteFunc(c.AssetsCode, func(file fileHash) bool {
+		return strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(file.Path), ".meta")
+	})
+	legacyFiles := append([]fileHash(nil), c.AssetsCode...)
+	legacyFiles = append(legacyFiles, c.ProjectSettings...)
+	slices.SortFunc(legacyFiles, func(a, b fileHash) int { return strings.Compare(a.Path, b.Path) })
+	var legacy strings.Builder
+	legacy.WriteString("fathom.unity.asset-context/v1\n")
+	for _, file := range legacyFiles {
+		legacy.WriteString("file\x00" + file.Path + "\x00" + file.SHA256 + "\n")
+	}

+	c.After = c.Before
+	f.receipt.Source.Before = digest(sourceBytes(f.receipt, f.inventory))
+	f.receipt.Source.After = f.receipt.Source.Before
+	// publish would deliberately recompute the current v2 canonical header.

+	f.active.Receipt.SHA256 = digest(raw)
+	writeJSON(t, f.opts.Root, f.opts.ActivePath, f.active)

+func TestUnityAssetReferenceCombinedMemberCountBoundary(t *testing.T) {
+	cases := []struct {
+		name                  string
+		raw, assets, settings int
+		refuse                bool
+	}{
+		{"mixed-exact50000", 12000, 30000, 8000, false},
+		{"mixed-over50001", 12000, 30000, 8001, true},
+		{"metadata-exact50000", 5, 49994, 1, false},
+		{"metadata-added50001", 5, 49995, 1, true},
+		{"raw-exact50000", 49998, 1, 1, false},
+		{"raw-plus-context50002", 50000, 1, 1, true},
+		{"overflow-cannot-wrap", int(^uint(0) >> 1), 1, 1, true},
+	}
+	for _, tc := range cases {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			err := checkSourceMemberCount(tc.raw, tc.assets, tc.settings)
+			if !tc.refuse {
+				if err != nil {
+					t.Fatal(err)
+				}
+				return
+			}
+			if !errors.Is(err, ErrRefused) || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "combined source/context membership exceeds50000") {
+				t.Fatalf("combined member boundary not specifically refused: %v", err)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+package connector
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"context"
+	"errors"
+	"io"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"reflect"
+	"runtime"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// Frozen independent oracle: the original fetchCapped implementation from the
+// qualified H3 source. It deliberately retains the original ReadAll algorithm.
+func legacyFetchCapped(ctx context.Context, path string, limit int64) ([]byte, error) {
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	fi, err := os.Stat(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if fi.Size() > limit {
+		return nil, &OversizeError{Path: path, Size: fi.Size(), Cap: limit}
+	}
+	f, err := os.Open(path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	defer f.Close()
+	data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(f, limit+1))
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if int64(len(data)) > limit {
+		return nil, &OversizeError{Path: path, Size: int64(len(data)), Cap: limit}
+	}
+	return data, nil
+}
+
+func TestCappedFetchFileDifferential(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, size := range []int{0, 1, 511, 512, 8192, 1 << 20, MaxFetchSize, MaxFetchSize + 1} {
+		path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "input")
+		data := bytes.Repeat([]byte{0, 255, 'x', '\n'}, (size+3)/4)[:size]
+		if err := os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o600); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		want, oldErr := legacyFetchCapped(context.Background(), path, MaxFetchSize)
+		got, newErr := fetchCapped(context.Background(), path, MaxFetchSize)
+		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) || !sameFetchError(oldErr, newErr) {
+			t.Fatalf("size=%d: bytes/errors differ: old=%d/%v new=%d/%v", size, len(want), oldErr, len(got), newErr)
+		}
+		if newErr == nil && !bytes.Equal(got, data) {
+			t.Fatalf("size=%d: delivered bytes changed", size)
+		}
+	}
+	missing := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "absent")
+	_, oldErr := legacyFetchCapped(context.Background(), missing, MaxFetchSize)
+	_, newErr := fetchCapped(context.Background(), missing, MaxFetchSize)
+	if !errors.Is(oldErr, os.ErrNotExist) || !errors.Is(newErr, os.ErrNotExist) {
+		t.Fatalf("missing-file semantics changed: %v, %v", oldErr, newErr)
+	}
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	cancel()
+	_, oldErr = legacyFetchCapped(ctx, missing, MaxFetchSize)
+	_, newErr = fetchCapped(ctx, missing, MaxFetchSize)
+	if !errors.Is(oldErr, context.Canceled) || !errors.Is(newErr, context.Canceled) {
+		t.Fatalf("pre-cancel precedence changed: %v, %v", oldErr, newErr)
+	}
+}
+
+func sameFetchError(a, b error) bool {
+	if a == nil || b == nil {
+		return a == nil && b == nil
+	}
+	var x, y *OversizeError
+	if errors.As(a, &x) && errors.As(b, &y) {
+		return *x == *y
+	}
+	return a.Error() == b.Error()
+}
+
+type fetchScriptReader struct {
+	data   []byte
+	step   int
+	err    error
+	cancel context.CancelFunc
+}
+
+func (r *fetchScriptReader) Read(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	if r.cancel != nil {
+		r.cancel()
+		r.cancel = nil
+	}
+	if len(r.data) == 0 {
+		if r.err != nil {
+			return 0, r.err
+		}
+		return 0, io.EOF
+	}
+	n := min(len(p), len(r.data))
+	if r.step > 0 {
+		n = min(n, r.step)
+	}
+	copy(p, r.data[:n])
+	r.data = r.data[n:]
+	if len(r.data) == 0 && r.err != nil {
+		return n, r.err
+	}
+	return n, nil
+}
+
+func TestCappedFetchGrowthShrinkAndReadErrors(t *testing.T) {
+	sentinel := errors.New("read failure with bytes")
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name string
+		size int64
+		data []byte
+		step int
+		err  error
+	}{
+		{"stable", 8, []byte("abcdefgh"), 0, nil},
+		{"shrink", 12, []byte("abc"), 1, nil},
+		{"grow-under-cap", 1, []byte("abcdefghi"), 2, nil},
+		{"zero-stat-grow", 0, []byte("abcdef"), 1, nil},
+		{"grow-over-cap", 2, bytes.Repeat([]byte("x"), 32), 1, nil},
+		{"error-with-bytes", 2, []byte("abc"), 1, sentinel},
+		{"initial-read-error", 2, nil, 1, sentinel},
+		{"EOF-with-bytes", 2, []byte("abc"), 2, io.EOF},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			const limit = int64(16)
+			old := &fetchScriptReader{data: tc.data, step: tc.step, err: tc.err}
+			fresh := &fetchScriptReader{data: tc.data, step: tc.step, err: tc.err}
+			want, oldErr := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(old, limit+1))
+			if oldErr != nil {
+				want = nil // fetchCapped discards partial bytes on a read error.
+			}
+			got, newErr := readFetchSized(context.Background(), fresh, tc.size, limit)
+			if !bytes.Equal(got, want) || !sameFetchError(oldErr, newErr) {
+				t.Fatalf("old=%q/%v new=%q/%v", want, oldErr, got, newErr)
+			}
+			if len(tc.data)-len(fresh.data) > int(limit+1) {
+				t.Fatal("read beyond the existing limit+1 probe")
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+func TestCappedFetchOwnedBytesAndCancellation(t *testing.T) {
+	input := []byte("mutable source")
+	got, err := readFetchSized(context.Background(), bytes.NewReader(input), int64(len(input)), 64)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	input[0] = 'X'
+	if string(got) != "mutable source" {
+		t.Fatal("returned bytes alias the reader's storage")
+	}
+	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	r := &fetchScriptReader{data: []byte("a long read"), step: 1, cancel: cancel}
+	got, err = readFetchSized(ctx, r, 12, 64)
+	if !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || got != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("cancellation between reads returned data/success: %q, %v", got, err)
+	}
+	// Cancellation on the final successful EOF is not a new late refusal.
+	ctx, cancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
+	r = &fetchScriptReader{data: []byte("a"), err: io.EOF, cancel: cancel}
+	got, err = readFetchSized(ctx, r, 1, 64)
+	if err != nil || string(got) != "a" {
+		t.Fatalf("completed final read was discarded: %q, %v", got, err)
+	}
+}

+var fetchSizedSink []byte
+
+func allocatedFetch(t *testing.T, path string, fn func(context.Context, string, int64) ([]byte, error)) uint64 {
+	t.Helper()
+	runtime.GC() // Synthetic measurement only; no production GC change.
+	var before, after runtime.MemStats
+	runtime.ReadMemStats(&before)
+	got, err := fn(context.Background(), path, MaxFetchSize)
+	runtime.ReadMemStats(&after)
+	if err != nil || len(got) != 1<<20 {
+		t.Fatalf("allocation workload changed: %d, %v", len(got), err)
+	}
+	fetchSizedSink = got
+	return after.TotalAlloc - before.TotalAlloc
+}
+
+func TestCappedFetchAllocationBound(t *testing.T) {
+	path := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "one-mebibyte")
+	if err := os.WriteFile(path, bytes.Repeat([]byte("x"), 1<<20), 0o600); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	for i := 0; i < 3; i++ {
+		oldBytes := allocatedFetch(t, path, legacyFetchCapped)
+		newBytes := allocatedFetch(t, path, fetchCapped)
+		saved := int64(oldBytes) - int64(newBytes)
+		t.Logf("sample=%d delivered_B=%d legacy_B=%d sized_B=%d saved_B=%d", i, 1<<20, oldBytes, newBytes, saved)
+		if saved < 1<<20 {
+			t.Fatalf("sized read did not save the fixed 1MiB floor: %d", saved)
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func BenchmarkCappedFetchMaterialization(b *testing.B) {
+	for _, size := range []int{1024, 64 << 10, 1 << 20} {
+		path := filepath.Join(b.TempDir(), "input")
+		if err := os.WriteFile(path, bytes.Repeat([]byte("x"), size), 0o600); err != nil {
+			b.Fatal(err)
+		}
+		for _, item := range []struct {
+			name string
+			fn   func(context.Context, string, int64) ([]byte, error)
+		}{{"legacy", legacyFetchCapped}, {"sized", fetchCapped}} {
+			b.Run(item.name+"/"+benchmarkFetchSize(size), func(b *testing.B) {
+				b.ReportAllocs()
+				for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
+					got, err := item.fn(context.Background(), path, MaxFetchSize)
+					if err != nil || len(got) != size {
+						b.Fatalf("workload changed: %d, %v", len(got), err)
+					}
+					fetchSizedSink = got
+				}
+				b.ReportMetric(float64(size), "delivered-B/op")
+			})
+		}
+	}
+}
+
+func benchmarkFetchSize(size int) string {
+	switch size {
+	case 1024:
+		return "1KiB"
+	case 64 << 10:
+		return "64KiB"
+	default:
+		return "1MiB"
+	}
+}

+// readFetchSized uses the observed size plus one growth-probe byte for the
+// ordinary read. A file that grew can require one additional bounded buffer;
+// no file is read beyond limit+1. The returned bytes are owned by this call.
+func readFetchSized(ctx context.Context, r io.Reader, size, limit int64) ([]byte, error) {
+	data := make([]byte, min(size+1, limit+1))
+	n, err := fillFetchBuffer(ctx, r, data)
+	if err != nil && err != io.EOF {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	if err == io.EOF || n < len(data) || int64(n) > limit {
+		return data[:n], nil
+	}
+	// The stat underreported the file. Preserve the probe and read the rest
+	// under the original cap, including its one-byte oversize sentinel.
+	grown := make([]byte, limit+1)
+	copy(grown, data[:n])
+	m, err := fillFetchBuffer(ctx, r, grown[n:])
+	if err != nil && err != io.EOF {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	return grown[:n+m], nil
+}
+
+func fillFetchBuffer(ctx context.Context, r io.Reader, data []byte) (int, error) {
+	used := 0
+	for used < len(data) {
+		// Check between reads, without a goroutine, changed producer class,
+		// or a late check that would discard a successfully completed read.
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return used, err
+		}
+		n, err := r.Read(data[used:])
+		used += n
+		if err != nil {
+			return used, err
+		}
+	}
+	return used, nil
+}

+package connector
+
+// A discovery-policy receipt is available for LocalConnector. Other
+// connectors do not claim a complete policy identity.
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"crypto/sha256"
+	"encoding/binary"
+	"encoding/hex"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"hash"
+	"io/fs"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/core"
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/gitro"
+)
+
+// policyPart frames data unambiguously. The digest is a receipt of effective
+// discovery inputs, not a claim that indexed bytes still match the worktree.
+func policyPart(h hash.Hash, label string, data []byte) {
+	for _, b := range [][]byte{[]byte(label), data} {
+		var length [8]byte
+		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(length[:], uint64(len(b)))
+		_, _ = h.Write(length[:])
+		_, _ = h.Write(b)
+	}
+}
+
+func policyFile(h hash.Hash, label, path string) error {
+	b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
+	if os.IsNotExist(err) {
+		policyPart(h, label, []byte("absent"))
+		return nil
+	}
+	if err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	policyPart(h, label+":present", b)
+	return nil
+}
+
+func gitPolicyFiles(ctx context.Context, h hash.Hash, dir string) error {
+	config, err := gitro.Output(ctx, dir, "config", "--list", "--show-origin", "-z")
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("git config: %w", err)
+	}
+	policyPart(h, "git-config:"+dir, config)
+	info, err := gitro.Output(ctx, dir, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/exclude")
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("git info exclude path: %w", err)
+	}
+	infoPath := strings.TrimSpace(string(info))
+	if !filepath.IsAbs(infoPath) {
+		infoPath = filepath.Join(dir, infoPath)
+	}
+	if err := policyFile(h, "git-info-exclude:"+dir, infoPath); err != nil {
+		return err
+	}
+	excludes, err := gitro.Output(ctx, dir, "config", "--path", "--get", "core.excludesFile")
+	if err == nil {
+		path := strings.TrimSpace(string(excludes))
+		if path != "" {
+			if !filepath.IsAbs(path) {
+				path = filepath.Join(dir, path)
+			}
+			if err := policyFile(h, "git-global-exclude:"+path, path); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+		}
+	} else {
+		var exit *exec.ExitError
+		if !errors.As(err, &exit) || exit.ExitCode() != 1 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("git excludes config: %w", err)
+		}
+		// Git's default global exclude when core.excludesFile is unset.
+		base := os.Getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME")
+		if base == "" {
+			home, homeErr := os.UserHomeDir()
+			if homeErr != nil {
+				return homeErr
+			}
+			base = filepath.Join(home, ".config")
+		}
+		path := filepath.Join(base, "git", "ignore")
+		if err := policyFile(h, "git-default-exclude:"+path, path); err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// DiscoveryPolicyDigest uses the same scoped ignore load, connector config,
+// and Git mode that Discover used. In Git mode it binds enclosing/nested
+// .gitignore files, per-repository info/exclude, effective Git configuration,
+// and the global excludes file. A bounded metadata walk finds nested policy
+// files even when an ignore change leaves discovered membership unchanged.
+func (c *LocalConnector) DiscoveryPolicyDigest(ctx context.Context, svc core.ServiceRef) (string, error) {
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	h := sha256.New()
+	policyPart(h, "version", []byte("local-discovery-policy-v2"))
+	policyPart(h, "root", []byte(svc.Path))
+	_, patterns, _, err := LoadIgnoreScopedForWithPatterns(svc.Path, svc.ID)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	for _, p := range patterns {
+		policyPart(h, "scoped-ignore", []byte(p))
+	}
+	if err := policyFile(h, "connector-config", filepath.Join(svc.Path, connectorConfigName)); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	include, configuredGit := loadConnectorConfig(svc.Path)
+	gitSelected := configuredGit || c.RespectGitignore
+	ex := c.Exclusions(svc.ID)
+	if ex.Git {
+		policyPart(h, "mode", []byte("git"))
+	} else {
+		policyPart(h, "mode", []byte("walk"))
+	}
+	if gitSelected {
+		policyPart(h, "git-opt-in", []byte("true"))
+	}
+	if !gitSelected || !isGitWorkTree(ctx, svc.Path) {
+		return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)), nil
+	}
+	topBytes, err := gitro.Output(ctx, svc.Path, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel")
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	top, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(strings.TrimSpace(string(topBytes)))
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	root, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(svc.Path)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	rel, err := filepath.Rel(top, root)
+	if err != nil || rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("corpus root outside Git top")
+	}
+	if err := gitPolicyFiles(ctx, h, root); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	// Parent ignores govern a corpus rooted below the Git top level.
+	parent := top
+	if err := policyFile(h, "gitignore:"+parent, filepath.Join(parent, ".gitignore")); err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	if rel != "." {
+		for _, segment := range strings.Split(rel, string(filepath.Separator)) {
+			parent = filepath.Join(parent, segment)
+			if parent == root {
+				break
+			}
+			if err := policyFile(h, "gitignore:"+parent, filepath.Join(parent, ".gitignore")); err != nil {
+				return "", err
+			}
+		}
+	}
+	ignore, _, err := LoadIgnoreScopedFor(svc.Path, svc.ID)
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	entries := 0
+	err = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
+		if walkErr != nil {
+			return walkErr
+		}
+		entries++
+		if entries > 200000 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("discovery policy metadata bound exceeded")
+		}
+		if entries%256 == 0 {
+			if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+		}
+		rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, path)
+		if err != nil {
+			return err
+		}
+		rel = filepath.ToSlash(rel)
+		if d.IsDir() && path != root {
+			if d.Name() == ".git" {
+				if filepath.Dir(path) != root {
+					if err := gitPolicyFiles(ctx, h, filepath.Dir(path)); err != nil {
+						return err
+					}
+				}
+				return filepath.SkipDir
+			}
+			if skipDir(d.Name()) || defaultIgnoredDir(d.Name(), rel, include) || (ignore != nil && ignore.Match(rel+"/")) {
+				return filepath.SkipDir
+			}
+		}
+		if d.Name() == ".gitignore" && !d.IsDir() {
+			return policyFile(h, "gitignore:"+path, path)
+		}
+		if d.Name() == ".git" && path != root && !d.IsDir() && filepath.Dir(path) != root {
+			return gitPolicyFiles(ctx, h, filepath.Dir(path))
+		}
+		return nil
+	})
+	if err != nil {
+		return "", err
+	}
+	return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil)), nil
+}

+package connector_test

+import (
+	"context"

+// Opt-in, read-only probe for the production corpus. It does not ingest or
+// modify files. The digest's error reports a policy-identity refusal.
+func TestDiscoveryPolicyProductionProbe(t *testing.T) {
+	root := os.Getenv("FATHOM_POLICY_PROBE_ROOT")
+	if root == "" {
+		t.Skip("set FATHOM_POLICY_PROBE_ROOT to enable")
+	}
+	ctx := context.Background()
+	svc := core.ServiceRef{ID: "policy-probe", Path: root}
+	c := connector.NewLocalConnector()
+	start := time.Now()
+	refs, err := c.Discover(ctx, svc)
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	t.Logf("discovered=%d discover_elapsed=%s exclusions=%+v", len(refs), time.Since(start), c.Exclusions(svc.ID))
+	start = time.Now()
+	digest, err := c.DiscoveryPolicyDigest(ctx, svc)
+	t.Logf("policy_digest=%q policy_elapsed=%s policy_error=%v", digest, time.Since(start), err)
+	if err != nil || digest == "" {
+		t.Fatalf("production policy identity unavailable: %v", err)
+	}
+}

+package connector_test
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"reflect"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/connector"
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/core"
+)

+// These rules change without changing the discovered members. The policy
+// receipt must still move because a later file could match the new rule.
+func TestDiscoveryPolicyDigestGitIgnoreSources(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, tc := range []struct {
+		name  string
+		setup func(*testing.T, string) (core.ServiceRef, string)
+	}{
+		{"nested", func(t *testing.T, root string) (core.ServiceRef, string) {
+			return core.ServiceRef{ID: "svc", Path: root}, filepath.Join(root, "pkg", ".gitignore")
+		}},
+		{"parent", func(t *testing.T, root string) (core.ServiceRef, string) {
+			p := filepath.Join(root, "pkg", ".fathom", "config.toml")
+			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0755); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if err := os.WriteFile(p, []byte("[connector]\nrespect_gitignore=true\n"), 0644); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			return core.ServiceRef{ID: "svc", Path: filepath.Join(root, "pkg")}, filepath.Join(root, ".gitignore")
+		}},
+		{"global", func(t *testing.T, root string) (core.ServiceRef, string) {
+			xdg := t.TempDir()
+			t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", xdg)
+			t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", os.DevNull)
+			t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM", "1")
+			p := filepath.Join(xdg, "git", "ignore")
+			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0755); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			return core.ServiceRef{ID: "svc", Path: root}, p
+		}},
+	} {
+		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
+			root := gitRepo(t, "[connector]\nrespect_gitignore=true\n")
+			svc, path := tc.setup(t, root)
+			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte("never-one-*.generated\n"), 0644); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			c := connector.NewLocalConnector()
+			before, err := c.Discover(context.Background(), svc)
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			d1, err := c.DiscoveryPolicyDigest(context.Background(), svc)
+			if err != nil || d1 == "" {
+				t.Fatalf("first digest=%q err=%v", d1, err)
+			}
+			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte("never-two-*.generated\n"), 0644); err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			after, err := c.Discover(context.Background(), svc)
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			if !reflect.DeepEqual(before, after) {
+				t.Fatalf("membership changed: before=%v after=%v", before, after)
+			}
+			d2, err := c.DiscoveryPolicyDigest(context.Background(), svc)
+			if err != nil || d2 == d1 {
+				t.Fatalf("policy drift undetected: before=%q after=%q err=%v", d1, d2, err)
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}

+package connector_test
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/connector"
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/core"
+)
+
+// The ingest dialect alone is insufficient: discovery, language reporting and
+// capabilities must classify the same Unity assembly-definition files. The
+// serialized metadata and assembly-reference format are not claimed by it.
+func TestUnityAsmdefClassificationAcrossLocalDiscovery(t *testing.T) {
+	root := t.TempDir()
+	files := map[string]string{
+		"Rules.asmdef":      `{"name":"Fixture.Rules","noEngineReferences":true}`,
+		"Rules.asmdef.meta": "fileFormatVersion: 2\n",
+		"Other.asmref":      `{"reference":"Fixture.Rules"}`,
+		"Rules.cs":          "namespace Fixture { public class Rules {} }",
+	}
+	for path, source := range files {
+		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, path), []byte(source), 0o644); err != nil {
+			t.Fatal(err)
+		}
+	}
+	refs, err := connector.NewLocalConnector().Discover(context.Background(), core.ServiceRef{ID: "unity", Path: root})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	found := false
+	for _, ref := range refs {
+		if ref.Path != "Rules.asmdef" {
+			continue
+		}
+		found = true
+		if ref.Kind != core.SourceKind("UnityAssemblyDefinition") {
+			t.Errorf("discovery kind = %q, want UnityAssemblyDefinition", ref.Kind)
+		}
+		if lang := connector.LanguageForPath(ref.Path); lang != "unity-asmdef" {
+			t.Errorf("language = %q, want unity-asmdef", lang)
+		}
+	}
+	if !found {
+		t.Fatal("local discovery omitted the assembly definition")
+	}
+	if producer := connector.TypedEdgeProducer("unity-asmdef"); producer != "syntax" {
+		t.Errorf("declared facts producer = %q, want syntax (no typed edges)", producer)
+	}
+	for _, path := range []string{"Other.asmref", "Rules.asmdef.meta"} {
+		if lang := connector.LanguageForPath(path); lang != core.LangUnclassified {
+			t.Errorf("unsupported %s classified as %q", path, lang)
+		}
+	}
+}

+				tc.edges[i].FromSymbol = "svc::Game.Worker.Run"

+// AssetObjectID is a persistent imported object identity, never a code symbol
+// or a Unity instance ID. FileID is canonical signed64 decimal text so JSON
+// clients cannot round IDs outside JavaScript's exact integer range.

+}

+}

+package core
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+	"text/scanner"
+)
+
+// TestIdentity is the source convention that makes n a test candidate, not
+// proof that a runner discovered or executed it. C# requires a recognized
+// NUnit/Unity test-shaped attribute; a method's name alone is insufficient.
+// Short attribute names are deliberately labelled syntax: they do not resolve
+// using aliases or a custom same-named attribute. Semantic index references
+// and attested runner evidence remain separate facts.
+func (n SymbolNode) TestIdentity() string {
+	if n.Kind == KindCSharpMethod {
+		if name := csharpTestAttribute(n.Signature); name != "" {
+			return "csharp-attribute-syntax:" + name
+		}
+		return ""
+	}
+	if strings.HasPrefix(string(n.Kind), "CSharp") {
+		return ""
+	}
+	if strings.HasPrefix(n.Name, "Test") {
+		return "name-prefix"
+	}
+	return ""
+}
+
+func (n SymbolNode) IsTest() bool { return n.TestIdentity() != "" }
+
+type attributeToken struct {
+	kind rune
+	text string
+}
+
+// Read only leading attribute lists. Quoted argument strings are opaque
+// scanner tokens, and commas in arguments/arrays cannot start an attribute.
+// An unreadable/truncated list is not a positive identity.
+func csharpTestAttribute(signature string) string {
+	var s scanner.Scanner
+	s.Init(strings.NewReader(signature))
+	s.Mode = scanner.ScanIdents | scanner.ScanStrings | scanner.ScanChars | scanner.ScanComments | scanner.SkipComments
+	bad := false
+	s.Error = func(*scanner.Scanner, string) { bad = true }
+	var found string
+	for tok := s.Scan(); tok == '['; tok = s.Scan() {
+		depth, parens := 1, 0
+		var part []attributeToken
+		flush := func() {
+			if name := testAttributeName(part); found == "" && name != "" {
+				found = name
+			}
+			part = nil
+		}
+		for depth > 0 {
+			tok = s.Scan()
+			if tok == scanner.EOF || bad {
+				return ""
+			}
+			switch tok {
+			case '[':
+				depth++
+			case ']':
+				depth--
+			case '(':
+				parens++
+			case ')':
+				parens--
+			}
+			if depth == 0 {
+				flush()
+				break
+			}
+			if tok == ',' && depth == 1 && parens == 0 {
+				flush()
+				continue
+			}
+			part = append(part, attributeToken{tok, s.TokenText()})
+		}
+	}
+	if bad {
+		return ""
+	}
+	return found
+}
+
+func testAttributeName(tokens []attributeToken) string {
+	// A return-value attribute annotates a different target, never this test.
+	if len(tokens) > 2 && tokens[0].kind == scanner.Ident && tokens[1].kind == ':' && tokens[2].kind != ':' {
+		if tokens[0].text != "method" {
+			return ""
+		}
+		tokens = tokens[2:]
+	}
+	var name strings.Builder
+	for i, tok := range tokens {
+		if tok.kind == '(' {
+			break
+		}
+		if tok.kind != scanner.Ident && tok.kind != '.' && tok.kind != ':' {
+			return ""
+		}
+		if tok.kind == scanner.Ident && i > 0 && tokens[i-1].kind == scanner.Ident {
+			return ""
+		}
+		name.WriteString(tok.text)
+	}
+	declared := strings.TrimPrefix(name.String(), "global::")
+	bare := strings.TrimSuffix(declared, "Attribute")
+	switch bare {
+	case "Test", "TestCase", "TestCaseSource", "Theory", "UnityTest",
+		"NUnit.Framework.Test", "NUnit.Framework.TestCase", "NUnit.Framework.TestCaseSource", "NUnit.Framework.Theory",
+		"UnityEngine.TestTools.UnityTest":
+		return declared
+	}
+	return ""
+}

+package core
+
+import "testing"
+
+func TestCSharpTestAttributeIdentity(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, signature := range []string{
+		"[Test] public void KeepsStock()", "[TestAttribute] void KeepsStock()",
+		"[NUnit.Framework.Test] void KeepsStock()", "[global::NUnit.Framework.TestAttribute] void KeepsStock()",
+		"[TestCase(1, 2)] void KeepsStock(int a, int b)", "[TestCaseSource(nameof(Data))] void KeepsStock(int a)",
+		"[UnityTest] IEnumerator Places()", "[UnityEngine.TestTools.UnityTestAttribute] IEnumerator Places()",
+		"[Description(\"], [Other.Test]\"), NUnit.Framework.Test] void KeepsStock()",
+		"[Description(@\"[Test]\")][Test] void KeepsStock()", "[method: Test] void KeepsStock()",
+		"[Theory] void KeepsStock()",
+	} {
+		n := SymbolNode{Name: "Cases.KeepsStock", Kind: KindCSharpMethod, Signature: signature}
+		if !n.IsTest() || n.TestIdentity() == "" {
+			t.Errorf("missing syntactic identity: %s", signature)
+		}
+	}
+	for _, signature := range []string{
+		"void KeepsStock()", "void TestKeepsStock()", "[SetUp] void KeepsStock()", "[TearDown] void KeepsStock()",
+		"[OneTimeSetUp] void KeepsStock()", "[Other.Test] void KeepsStock()", "[Other.TestAttribute] void KeepsStock()",
+		"[Description(\"[Test]\")] void KeepsStock()", "[Description(@\"[Test]\")] void KeepsStock()",
+		"[return: Test] object KeepsStock()", "[Te st] void KeepsStock()", "[Description(\"unterminated",
+		"[TestCase(1, 2)", "[TestFixture] void KeepsStock()", "[TestCaseData] void KeepsStock()",
+	} {
+		if n := (SymbolNode{Name: "TestCases.TestKeepsStock", Kind: KindCSharpMethod, Signature: signature}); n.IsTest() {
+			t.Errorf("non-test or unreadable syntax counted: %s", signature)
+		}
+	}
+	if n := (SymbolNode{Name: "TestCases", Kind: KindCSharpClass, Signature: "[TestFixture] class TestCases"}); n.IsTest() {
+		t.Fatal("fixture class is not a test case")
+	}
+	if n := (SymbolNode{Name: "TestKeepsStock", Kind: KindGoFunc}); !n.IsTest() || n.TestIdentity() != "name-prefix" {
+		t.Fatal("legacy Go naming changed")
+	}
+}

+package extractor
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"strings"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/core"
+)
+
+const csharpTestSourceLimit = 16 << 20
+const csharpTestHeaderLimit = 64 << 10
+
+// CSharpMethodHeaders reads complete, bounded method headers for an explicit
+// source-bound test-policy check. Normal indexed/display signatures remain
+// capped by the dialect. These are syntax facts, not resolved NUnit attributes.
+// A source over 16MiB returns an error. Normalized UTF-8 headers over 64KiB or
+// clipped headers are omitted, never treated as complete policy.
+func CSharpMethodHeaders(service, relPath string, src []byte) ([]core.SymbolNode, error) {
+	if len(src) > csharpTestSourceLimit {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("C# test-policy source exceeds 16MiB")
+	}
+	registry, err := tsRegistry()
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	base := registry["csharp"]
+	if base == nil {
+		return nil, fmt.Errorf("C# test-policy dialect unavailable")
+	}
+	// Clone the per-extractor rule values. Shared registry/query/parser policy
+	// must not acquire a larger display limit from this read-side operation.
+	cloneVariant := func(v tsVariant) tsVariant {
+		rules := *v.rules
+		rules.sigMax = csharpTestHeaderLimit + 1
+		v.rules, v.leaseOwner = &rules, ""
+		return v
+	}
+	spec := *base
+	spec.defaultVariant = cloneVariant(base.defaultVariant)
+	spec.variantForExt = make(map[string]tsVariant, len(base.variantForExt))
+	for ext, variant := range base.variantForExt {
+		spec.variantForExt[ext] = cloneVariant(variant)
+	}
+	e := newTSExtractorFromSpec(&spec)
+	defer e.Close()
+	nodes, err := e.Extract(service, relPath, src)
+	if err != nil {
+		return nil, err
+	}
+	out := make([]core.SymbolNode, 0)
+	for _, n := range nodes {
+		if n.Kind == core.KindCSharpMethod && len(n.Signature) <= csharpTestHeaderLimit && !strings.HasSuffix(n.Signature, "…") {
+			out = append(out, n)
+		}
+	}
+	return out, nil
+}

+package extractor
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/core"
+)
+
+func TestCSharpMethodHeadersKeepCompletePolicyWithoutChangingDisplay(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, policy := range []string{"", "[Retry(2)]", "[NUnit.Framework.Repeat(2)]"} {
+		t.Run(policy, func(t *testing.T) {
+			t.Parallel() // Concurrent header reads must not mutate shared display rules.
+			src := []byte("namespace Workshop { class BowlTests { [TestCase(1)] [TestCase(2)] [Category(\"" + strings.Repeat("category", 45) + "\")] " + policy + " public void Fits(int n) {} } }")
+			ordinary, err := NewTSExtractor("csharp")
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			defer ordinary.Close()
+			before, err := ordinary.Extract("svc", "Assets/BowlTests.cs", src)
+			if err != nil {
+				t.Fatal(err)
+			}
+			headers, err := CSharpMethodHeaders("svc", "Assets/BowlTests.cs", src)
+			if err != nil || len(headers) != 1 {
+				t.Fatalf("headers=%+v err=%v", headers, err)
+			}
+			h := headers[0]
+			if h.Name != "BowlTests.Fits" || h.Package != "Workshop" || h.Line != 1 || h.EndLine != 1 || !h.IsTest() || !strings.HasSuffix(h.Signature, "public void Fits(int n)") {
+				t.Fatalf("incomplete or wrong method policy: %+v", h)
+			}
+			if policy != "" && !strings.Contains(h.Signature, policy) {
+				t.Fatal("a policy beyond the display boundary was lost")
+			}
+			after, err := ordinary.Extract("svc", "Assets/BowlTests.cs", src)
+			if err != nil || len(after) != len(before) {
+				t.Fatalf("ordinary extractor changed: %+v %v", after, err)
+			}
+			for i := range before {
+				if before[i].Signature != after[i].Signature {
+					t.Fatal("read-side header extraction mutated the shared display policy")
+				}
+				if before[i].Kind == core.KindCSharpMethod && (!strings.HasSuffix(before[i].Signature, "…") || before[i].IsTest()) {
+					t.Fatal("the ordinary clipped display must stay fail-closed")
+				}
+			}
+		})
+	}
+}
+
+func TestCSharpMethodHeadersRefuseOverboundPolicyAndSource(t *testing.T) {
+	for _, value := range []string{strings.Repeat("x", csharpTestHeaderLimit+1), strings.Repeat("界", csharpTestHeaderLimit/3+1)} {
+		src := []byte("namespace Workshop { class BowlTests { [TestCase(1)] [Category(\"" + value + "\")] public void Fits(int n) {} [Test] public void Other() {} } }")
+		headers, err := CSharpMethodHeaders("svc", "Assets/BowlTests.cs", src)
+		if err != nil || len(headers) != 1 || headers[0].Name != "BowlTests.Other" {
+			t.Fatalf("oversize policy must not hide a small sibling or become a positive header: %+v %v", headers, err)
+		}
+	}
+	if _, err := CSharpMethodHeaders("svc", "Assets/BowlTests.cs", make([]byte, csharpTestSourceLimit+1)); err == nil {
+		t.Fatal("overbound source accepted")
+	}
+}

+func TestUnityAsmdefDeclaredFacts(t *testing.T) {
+	x, err := NewDocDialectExtractor("unity-asmdef")
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	r, err := x.ExtractDoc("fixture", "Assets/Adapters/Adapters.asmdef", []byte(`{
+ "name":"Fixture.Adapters",
+ "references":["Fixture.Rules","GUID:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"],
+ "noEngineReferences":false,
+ "autoReferenced":true
+}`))
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}
+	var got []string
+	for _, n := range r.Nodes {
+		got = append(got, string(n.Kind)+":"+n.Name)
+		if len(n.Calls) != 0 {
+			t.Errorf("declaration became calls: %+v", n)
+		}
+	}
+	want := []string{"UnityAssemblyDefinition:Fixture.Adapters", "UnityAssemblyReference:Fixture.Rules", "UnityAssemblyReference:GUID:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"}
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
+		t.Fatalf("nodes=%q, want %q", got, want)
+	}
+	if r.Nodes[0].Signature != "noEngineReferences=false; autoReferenced=true" {
+		t.Errorf("signature=%q", r.Nodes[0].Signature)
+	}
+	var facts []string
+	for _, f := range r.Facts {
+		facts = append(facts, f.Key+"="+f.Value)
+	}
+	if !reflect.DeepEqual(facts, []string{"reference=Fixture.Rules", "reference=GUID:0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef", "noEngineReferences=false"}) {
+		t.Errorf("facts=%q", facts)
+	}
+	if len(r.CrossFile) != 0 {
+		t.Fatal("declared references must not become resolved/typed edges")
+	}
+}

+// This minimal test double implements the public load.Config.Registry contract.
+// It does not delegate to modconfig.NewRegistry, modcache, HTTP or credentials.
+// The producer has a separate zero-state refusal implementation; recording names
+// here is confined to a temp module and verifies the pinned native API contract.
+type cueRefusingRegistryFixture struct {
+	mu    sync.Mutex
+	calls []string
+}
+
+func (r *cueRefusingRegistryFixture) refuse(method, target string) error {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	r.calls = append(r.calls, method+" "+target)
+	return fmt.Errorf("%s (%s %s)", cueRegistryRefusalReason, method, target)
+}

+func (r *cueRefusingRegistryFixture) Requirements(_ context.Context, target module.Version) ([]module.Version, error) {
+	return nil, r.refuse("Requirements", target.String())

+	return module.SourceLoc{}, r.refuse("Fetch", target.String())

+func (r *cueRefusingRegistryFixture) ModuleVersions(_ context.Context, target string) ([]string, error) {
+	return nil, r.refuse("ModuleVersions", target)
+}
+
+func (r *cueRefusingRegistryFixture) attempted() []string {
+	r.mu.Lock()
+	defer r.mu.Unlock()
+	return append([]string(nil), r.calls...)

+func TestCUENativeExplicitDenyRegistryPreservesLocalImportsAndBuiltinEvaluation(t *testing.T) {

+		Env: []string{"CUE_REGISTRY=file:must-not-open-ambient-registry-config"},

+		t.Fatalf("local module/builtin consulted registry: %v", calls)

+func TestCUENativeExplicitDenyRegistryRefusesRemoteDependencyByName(t *testing.T) {

+	// cueRegistryFixture deliberately owns only fixture files; overwrite its module
+	// declaration here to pin a remote dependency, without touching any cache.
+	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "cue.mod", "module.cue"), []byte(moduleSource), 0644); err != nil {
+		t.Fatal(err)
+	}

+		Dir: root, ModuleRoot: root, Registry: registry,
+	})

+			failures = append(failures, instance.Err.Error())
+		}

+			failures = append(failures, err.Error())
+		}
+	}

+		t.Fatalf("remote dependency refusal lost its cause or target: %q; registry=%v", joined, registry.attempted())
+	}
+	if calls := registry.attempted(); len(calls) == 0 {
+		t.Fatal("remote fixture did not exercise the explicit registry boundary")
+	}

+package fusion
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"fmt"
+	"os"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"sync/atomic"
+
+	"cuelang.org/go/cue/ast"
+	"cuelang.org/go/cue/build"
+	"cuelang.org/go/cue/load"
+	"cuelang.org/go/mod/modconfig"
+	"cuelang.org/go/mod/module"
+
+	"github.com/geoffmilleraz/fathom/internal/store"
+)
+
+const cueRegistryRefusalReason = "CUE native index refuses registry access: local module and builtins only"
+
+// cueLocalOnlyRegistry closes cue/load's external-module boundary. In particular,
+// CUE_REGISTRY=inline:{} is not an offline switch: a nil Config.Registry creates
+// the default registry and its persistent module cache. This implementation never
+// constructs or delegates to a registry, cache, credential reader or transport.
+// It intentionally refuses external modules even if an operator cached them.
+// Local module imports and builtins are resolved by cue/load without this port.
+// This is not a filesystem sandbox or a per-file loader read boundary.
+type cueLocalOnlyRegistry struct{ denied atomic.Bool }
+
+var _ modconfig.Registry = (*cueLocalOnlyRegistry)(nil)
+
+func (r *cueLocalOnlyRegistry) Requirements(_ context.Context, target module.Version) ([]module.Version, error) {
+	return nil, r.refuse("Requirements", target.String())
+}
+
+func (r *cueLocalOnlyRegistry) Fetch(_ context.Context, target module.Version) (module.SourceLoc, error) {
+	return module.SourceLoc{}, r.refuse("Fetch", target.String())
+}
+
+func (r *cueLocalOnlyRegistry) ModuleVersions(_ context.Context, target string) ([]string, error) {
+	return nil, r.refuse("ModuleVersions", target)
+}
+
+func (r *cueLocalOnlyRegistry) refuse(method, target string) error {
+	r.denied.Store(true)
+	return fmt.Errorf("%s (%s %s)", cueRegistryRefusalReason, method, target)
+}
+
+func cueLocalLoadConfig(root string, registry *cueLocalOnlyRegistry) *load.Config {
+	return &load.Config{
+		Dir: root, ModuleRoot: root,
+		Package: "*", // every package; files with no package clause -> "_"
+		// An inline-empty CUE_REGISTRY still enables the default registry.
+		Registry: registry,
+		Env:      []string{},
+	}
+}
+
+// invalidateCUEDeniedPackages uses native package loads to attribute policy
+// denial. Pinned cue/load formats away the registry's error identity and can
+// collapse ./... into one failed synthetic instance without package metadata.
+// A fresh, pass-local denial flag therefore observes each prior CUE package's
+// own native load. No error-string matching or all-producer purge is involved.
+// Work is at most one retry per stored CUE package, never recursive. cue/load has
+// no cancellation API; cancellation is checked between its bounded invocations.
+func invalidateCUEDeniedPackages(ctx context.Context, st store.Store, service, root string, loadInstances func([]string, *load.Config) []*build.Instance) error {
+	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("CUE registry denial inspection incomplete: %w", err)
+	}
+	packages, err := st.ListTypedEdgePackages(ctx, service)
+	if err != nil {
+		return fmt.Errorf("CUE registry denial inspection incomplete: list prior packages: %w", err)
+	}
+	for _, key := range packages { // store contract returns a sorted distinct list
+		if !strings.HasPrefix(key, cuePackageKeyPrefix) {
+			continue
+		}
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("CUE registry denial inspection incomplete: %w", err)
+		}
+		arg, err := cueRegistryInspectionArg(root, strings.TrimPrefix(key, cuePackageKeyPrefix))
+		if err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("CUE registry denial inspection incomplete for %q: %w", key, err)
+		}
+		registry := &cueLocalOnlyRegistry{}
+		instances := loadInstances([]string{arg}, cueLocalLoadConfig(root, registry))
+		if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("CUE registry denial inspection incomplete for %q: %w", key, err)
+		}
+		if len(instances) == 0 {
+			return fmt.Errorf("CUE registry denial inspection incomplete for %q: native loader returned no instance", key)
+		}
+		if !registry.denied.Load() {
+			continue // preserve healthy packages and the ordinary failure policy
+		}
+		if err := st.DeleteTypedEdgePackage(ctx, service, key); err != nil {
+			return fmt.Errorf("CUE registry denial invalidation failed for %q: %w", key, err)
+		}
+	}
+	return nil
+}
+
+// Native package IDs normally are import paths. Legacy/anonymous IDs instead
+// use absolute-dir:PkgName; convert only an existing, physically in-root directory
+// into a relative package selection. Never pass a stored absolute path to load.
+func cueRegistryInspectionArg(root, id string) (string, error) {
+	if colon := strings.LastIndexByte(id, ':'); colon >= 0 && filepath.IsAbs(id[:colon]) {
+		dir, name := id[:colon], id[colon+1:]
+		if !ast.IsValidIdent(name) {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported fallback package name %q", name)
+		}
+		rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, dir)
+		if err != nil || rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("fallback directory is outside the module root")
+		}
+		realRoot, rootErr := filepath.EvalSymlinks(root)
+		realDir, dirErr := filepath.EvalSymlinks(dir)
+		if rootErr != nil || dirErr != nil {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("fallback directory cannot be resolved")
+		}
+		if info, err := os.Stat(realDir); err != nil || !info.IsDir() {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("fallback directory is not an existing directory")
+		}
+		physicalRel, err := filepath.Rel(realRoot, realDir)
+		if err != nil || physicalRel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(physicalRel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) {
+			return "", fmt.Errorf("fallback directory resolves outside the module root")
+		}
+		return "./" + filepath.ToSlash(rel) + ":" + name, nil
+	}
+	if err := module.CheckImportPath(id); err != nil {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid stored native import identity: %w", err)
+	}
+	if name := ast.ParseImportPath(id).Qualifier; name != "" && !ast.IsValidIdent(name) {
+		return "", fmt.Errorf("invalid stored native package qualifier %q", name)
+	}
+	return id, nil
+}

+func writeCUERegistryFile(t *testing.T, root, name, content string) {
+	t.Helper()
